कक्षक: Kakṣaka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Vāsuki, listed by Sūta among those offered in the सर्पसत्र of Janamejaya 1. 52. 6.
कच्छप: Kacchapa m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, one of those who came to greet the birth of Arjuna 1. 114. 60, 40.
कद्रू: Kadrū f.: A mythical being. A. Family: Daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati (दक्षकन्या), sister of Vinatā, wife of Kaśyapa 1. 14. 6; 1. 59. 13. B. Her progeny: Mother of all serpents (भुजगानाम् अशेषाणां माता कद्रूर् इति श्रुतिः 1. 49. 5); hence serpents called कद्रूपुत्र- 1. 30. 11; 1. 14. 8; 1. 23. 5; कद्रुज 13. 151. 13; [also see Kādraveya]; according to 1. 60. 66, however, Surasā (daughter of Tāmrā ? 1. 50. 54, 59, of Śukī ? 1. 60. 57, of Kadrū 1. 60. 66) gave birth to नागस् (also 5. 101. 4) and Kadrū to पन्नगस्; after marriage, Kaśyapa, her husband, granted her a boon; she chose to be the mother of a thousand serpents (वव्रे कद्रूः सुतान् नागान् सहस्रम्) 1. 14. 6-8, 10; 1. 31. 2; after a long period she lay one thousand eggs which were preserved in warm pots (सोप-स्वेदेषु भाण्डेषु) and the serpents came out of the eggs after five hundred years 1. 14. 12-14 [Nī. सोपस्वेदेषु उष्मवत्सु । तत्र ह्य् अण्डान्तर्जलम् ऊष्मणा शीघ्रं घनी-भवतीति on 1. 16. 15 Bom. edn.]; principal नागस् like Śeṣa, Vāsuki and others listed among the sons of Kadrū (काद्रवेयाः) 1. 31. 4 ff.; 1. 59. 40; Śeṣa left Kadrū to practise austerity on the Gandhamādana 1. 32. 2. C. Myth: Kadrū once asked Vinatā about the colour of the horse Uccaiḥśravas; Vinatā declared it to be white and asked Kadrū to say what she felt about it and then offered to put a wager on it (ततो ऽत्र विपणावहे) 1. 18. 3; Kadrū said that the horse had dark hair on its tail; she accepted Vinatā's challenge and specified slavery as a stake (एहि सार्द्-धं मया दीव्य दासीभावाय भामिनि) 1. 18. 4, 5; 1. 19. 2; 1. 24. 9; Kadrū asked her serpent sons to turn themselves into black hair and enter the horse (i. e. his tail) so that she did not lose the contest; when the serpents did not agree she cursed them that they would be burnt in the snake-sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 18. 6-8; 1. 49. 5-7; Pitāmaha thought her curse to be too cruel 1. 18. 9; next morning Kadrū and Vinatā went to inspect the colour of Uccaiḥśravas 1. 19. 1-2; on way they crossed the ocean 1. 20. 1; on inspection they found black hair sticking to the tail of the horse; Kadrū, the winner of the bet, made Vinatā her दासी 1. 20. 2; once Kadrū asked Vinatā to carry her to the abode of the नागस् inside the ocean (समुद्रकुक्षौ); Kadrū, the mother of serpents (सर्पमाता), was taken there by Vinatā 1. 21. 3-5; Kadrū praised Śakra to obtain relief for her sons when they, riding on the back of Garuḍa, were tormented by the rays of the sun and had swooned 1. 21. 6; pleased, Śakra showered rain to the delight of the serpents 1. 22. 1. D. Mahāgraha: Kadrū mentioned among afflictions (ग्रहाः, महाग्रहाः) unfavour-able to the newly born children until they were sixteen; assumes a subtle form and enters the body of a pregnant woman; she eats up the foetus and the woman delivers a serpent 3. 219. 22, 36, 41 [as told by Skanda, Mothers, in various forms, afflict young children for the first sixteen years 3. 219. 22].
कपिल: Kapila m.: A mythical king of serpents. Called high-spirited (महात्मन्); a नागतीर्थ, sacred to him, famous in the three worlds 3. 82 28-29.
कपोत: Kapota m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 13, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
कम्बल: Kambala m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 9, 1. Son of Surasā an Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 10. 5-7; name occurs also among the sons of Kadrū listed by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 10, 2; waits without feeling fatigue on Varuṇa in his सभा 2. 9. 9, 11; always mentioned with serpent Aśvatara (कम्बलाश्वतरौ); marked with banner (पताकिन्) and round spots (मण्ड-लिन्), hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 10.

Kambala nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। The तीर्थस् Prayāga, Pratiṣṭhāna, Kam-bala, Aśvatara and Bhogavatī form the Vedī of Prajāpati; there the Vedas and the sacri-fices, in bodily form (मूर्तिमन्तः), and the sages wait upon Prajāpati; gods and Cakra-caras offer sacrifices there 3. 83. 72-73.
करवीर: Karavīra m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 14, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; name occurs also among the sons of Kadrū, listed by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 12, 2.
कर्कर: Karkara m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 15, 2.
कर्कोटक: Karkoṭaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 9, 1. A. Birth: Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; also mentioned among the sons of Kadrū, listed by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 5, 2; often mentioned with serpent Dhanaṃjaya (कर्कोटकधनं-जयौ) 1. 31. 5; 2. 9. 9; 5. 101. 9. B. Descrip-tion and status: Marked with gem, स्वस्तिक, circles, कमण्डलु (ascetic's vessel); having mouths in varying numbers 5. 101. 5-7; king of serpents (नागराजन्) 3. 64. 3; 3. 75. 17; (नागराज) 3. 70. 32; no other serpent his equal (मत्समो नास्ति पन्नगः 3. 63. 7). C. Activities: Waits, with other नागस्, on Varuṇa in his सभा 2. 9. 9; present among those who arrived to greet Arjuna's birth 1. 114, 60; one of the नागस् who received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 14. D. Part played in the Nala story: Nala heard him inviting for help and saw him lying in coils in a forest fire; he introduced himself as Nāga Karkoṭaka; he once seized (?प्रलब्ध) a Brahmanical sage and, due to his curse, was since unable to move; agreed to become Nala's friend and, if saved by Nala, assured to teach him something which would stand him in good stead (श्रेयः); Karkoṭaka could change his size at will and become of the size of a thumb; he asked Nala to take him some distance and while doing so count his steps; Nala picked him up and took him to a place where there was no fire; at the tenth step (दशमे पदे) he bit Nala when, apparently, Nala must have uttered the word दश (which was also a command to bite); as a result Nala became deformed (विकृत); Karkoṭaka as-sumed his natural form and advised Nala to go to king Ṛtuparṇa of Ayodhyā; Karkoṭaka changed Nala's appearance so that no one should recognize him; he gave Nala two pieces of cloth and asked him to put them on, after remembering Karkoṭaka, to regain his original form 3. 63. 1-24; the piece of cloth was free from dust (वस्त्रम् अरजः), and when Nala did, as advised, he regained his original form 3. 75. 17; Kali who had entered Nala's body was all along burning due to the sharp (तीक्ष्ण) poison of Karkoṭaka which was in Nala's body; when Kali came out of Nala's body he vomitted this poison 3. 70. 27, 32.

Karkoṭaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. A Brāhmaṇa had said in the assembly of the Kurus that according to a certain Rākṣasī one should avoid the Karkoṭakas (यद् अन्यो ऽप्य् उक्तवान् सभ्यो ब्राह्मणः कुरुसंसदि … कर्कोटकान् वीरकांश् च … विवर्जयेत्) 8. 30. 41, 45.
कलश: Kalaśa m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 11, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
कल्माष: Kalmāṣa m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 7, 2.
काकी: Kākī f.: A mythical female-crow. Daughter of divine (देवी) Tāmrā, she gave birth to owls 1. 60. 54-55.
काद्रवेय: Kādraveya m.: Son of Kadrū. Specifically mentioned as such are Vāsuki, Airāvata and Elāpatra who, with others, held consultation on the means of avoid-ing destruction which threatened them due to their mother's curse 1. 33. 10, 1, 2; 1. 34. 1; Śeṣa, Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kūrma and Kulika—these six are mentioned as काद्र-वेयस् 1. 59. 40; Karkoṭaka, Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Kacchapa, Cāpakuṇḍa and Takṣaka are the काद्रवेयस् who arrived to greet Arjuna's birth 1. 114. 60, 40; when mythical beings took sides between Karṇa and Arjuna, काद्रवेयस् were on the side of Arjuna—here specifically named are Vāsuki, Citrasena, Takṣaka, Upa-takṣaka 8. 63. 36. [See Kadrū].
कामदुह्: Kāmaduh f.: A mythical cow. As the best among the cows, listed among the विभूतिस् of Bhagavān 6. 32. 28. [See Nandinī].
कालदन्तक: Kāladantaka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Vāsuki, offered in the सर्पसत्र of Janamejaya 1. 52. 6, 4.
कालिय: Kāliya m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 6, 2.
कालीय: Kālīya m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 9, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
कालीयक: Kālīyaka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 10, 2.
काश्यप: Kāśyapa m.: A mythical crane. [See Nāḍījaṅgha and Rājadharman]
काश्यपि: Kāśyapi m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 10, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because engaged in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
कुकुण: Kukuṇa m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 10, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
कुकुर: Kukura m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 10, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.

Kukura1 m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Description: Strong (बलिन्) 2. 17. 27. B. Characteristic: Nārada mentioned them among those who were attached to Kṛṣṇa (कुकुरा भोजाः … त्वय्य् आसक्ता महाबाहो) 12. 82. 29. C. History: Since Jarāsandha was assisted by two counsellors Haṃsa and Ḍibhaka (2. 17. 25), he was let alone by Kukuras and Andhakas out of consideration of policy (एवम् एष तदा वीर बलिभिः कुकुरान्धकैः । … नीतिहेतोर् उपेक्षितः 2. 17. 27. D. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa had assured Yudhiṣṭhira while he was in forest that the Daśārha heroes, as well as Kukuras and others, would carry out his orders and take positions in battle where he willed, in case Yudhiṣṭhira wanted to fight with Duryodhana (दशार्हयोधाः कुकुरान्धकाश् च । एते निदेशं तव पाल-यन्ति तिष्ठन्ति यत्रेच्छसि तत्र राजन् ॥ ) 3. 180. 31; (2) In the war they were on the side of Kauravas; Duryodhana men-tions them among his army; on the second day of the war, he asked Droṇa, assisted by Kukuras and others, to protect Bhīṣma वेणिकाः कुकुरास् तथा । … भीष्मम् एवाभि-रक्षन्तु) 6. 47. 7, 9; (3) In the mutual killing in which the Yādavas indulged with the एरका grass, Kukuras and Andhakas got killed as moths in fire (पतङ्गा इव चाग्नौ ते न्यपतन् कुकुरान्धकाः) 16. 4. 41; the Pāṇḍavas were grieved when their death was reported to them by Dāruka 16. 6. 2.

Kukura2 m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada of the south. Saṃjaya lists them among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणाः) 6. 10. 56; 6. 10. 37, 5; (कुकु-राङ्गदमारिषाः) 6. 10. 59.
कुञ्जर: Kuñjara m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 15, 2; one of those who received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 14, 12.
कुठारमुख: Kuṭhāramukha m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग) and ‘very poisonous’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 14, 13, 1.
कुण्डल: Kuṇḍala m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Kauravya, offered in the snake-sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 12, 1.
कुण्डलधर: Kuṇḍaladhara m.: A mythical serpent. One of those who, without feeling fatigue, wait upon Varuṇa in his सभा 2. 9. 9, 11; described as पताकिन् (marked with banner), मण्डलिन् (marked with spots), फणवन्त् (hooded) 2. 9. 10.
कुण्डलिन्: Kuṇḍalin m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 9, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahmin-hood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
कुण्डोदर: Kuṇḍodara m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 15, 2.
कुमार: Kumāra1 m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 15, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.

Kumāra2 m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 13, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahmin-hood because indulging in the destruction of kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
कुमारक: Kumāraka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Kauravya, one of those offered in the सर्पसत्र of Janamejaya 1. 52. 12, 11.
कुमुद: Kumuda1 m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 13, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 15; he, with other serpents, received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 14, 12.

Kumuda2 m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 12, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; marked with श्री-वत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; feeding on serpents; by action a Kṣatriya not obtaining Brahmin-hood because engaged in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
Kumuda3 m.: A mythical lordly elephant (वारणसत्तम), living in पाताल 5. 97. 1. Born in the वंश of Supratīka, pointed out by Nārada to Mātali 5. 97. 15.
Kumuda4 m.: A monkey-chief. Kept watch, with Sugrīva and others, over the bodies of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, fallen on the ground, tied with arrows by Indrajit 3. 273. 4, 1-3.

Kumuda m.: Name of a mountain. One of the six mountains of the Kuśa-dvīpa; the mountain is, indeed, lustrous (? द्युतिमान् नाम; or is Dyutimant another name of the mountain Kumuda ?) all the six mountains are described as excellent moun-tains (पर्वतोत्तमाः); the distance between them doubles as one moves from the one to the other (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 13. 10-11.
कुमुदाक्ष: Kumudākṣa m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 15, 2.
कुरर: Kurara m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 15, 2.
कुलिक: Kulika m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, daughter of Dakṣa; listed among the Kādraveyas by Vaiśaṃpāyana at the request of Janamejaya 1. 59. 40, 13.
कुशक: Kuśaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 15, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
कूर्म: Kūrma m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, daughter of Dakṣa; listed among the Kādraveyas by Vaiśaṃpāyana at the request of Janamejaya 1. 59. 40, 13.
कृश: Kṛśa m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Airāvata, one of those offered in the snake sacrifice of Jana-mejaya 1. 52. 10, 11, 1.
कृष्ण: Kṛṣṇa m.: A mythical serpent. 2. 9. 8. Waits on Varuṇa in his सभा without feeling fatigue (विगतक्लम) 2. 9. 11; de-scription: marked with banner (पताकिन्), and spots (मण्डलिन्), hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 10.

Kṛṣṇa m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the west in the Madhyama Dvīpa, it looks like Nārāyaṇa (पर्वतः पश्चिमः कृष्णो नारायणनिभो नृप) 6. 13. 4; there Keśava himself stands guard to all heavenly jewels; sitting near Prajāpati he gave happiness to creatures (प्रजापतिम् उपासीनः प्रजानां विदधे सुखम्) 6. 13. 5.

Kṛṣṇa m. (pl.): Name (?) of a people. Mentioned by Duryodhana among those who had brought tributes of different kinds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira but were stopped at the gate (कृष्णान् … द्वारि वारितान् । बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्य नाना-रूपान् अनेकशाः) 2. 47. 19-20.
केसरिन्: Kesarin m.: A monkey. Hanūmant begotten on the wife (क्षेत्र) of Kesarin by Vāyu 3. 147. 24.
कैलासक: Kailāsaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 11, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
कोटनक: Koṭanaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 12, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5 7; also listed among the sons of Kadrū by Sūta 1. 31. 8.
कोटिक: Koṭika m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Vāsuki: one of those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janame-jaya; description: some snakes in this family were dark-red, others white in colour; terrific, huge, and having excess of poison (विषोत्बण) 1. 52. 5, 1, 4, 6.
कोणप: Koṇapa m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Vāsuki; one of those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; description: some snakes in this family were dark-red, others white in colour, terrific, huge, having excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 5, 1, 4, 6.
कोणवासन: Koṇavāsana m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed by Sūta among her sons at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 14, 2.
कोणवेग: Koṇavega m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Vāsuki; one of those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; description: some snakes in this family were dark-red, others white in colour, terrific, huge, having excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 5, 1, 4, 6.
कोमठक: Komaṭhaka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, one of those offered in the snake sacrifice of Jana-mejaya 1. 52. 15, 1; described as having the speed of wind (वातवेग) and excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 13.
कौरव्य: Kauravya m.: A mythical serpent. A. Birth: Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 13, 2; also mentioned as son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 15, 4, 17; but ac-cording to 1, 206. 18 born in the कुल of Airāvata. B. Progeny and Relatives: Serpents Aiṇḍila, Kuṇḍala and others, born in the कुल of Kauravya, offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 11, 12; his daughter Ulūpī (1. 206. 18; 14. 90. 2) dragged Arjuna down while he was bathing in Gaṅgā and took him to her father's residence; at Ulūpī's request Arjuna spent a night at Kauravya's residence 1. 206. 13, 34; serpent Sumukha, stood before Kauravya (and Āryaka, also born in the कुल of Airāvata), when seen by Mātali 5. 101. 19, 23. C. Resi-dence: Living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 1; Kauravya's residence highly praised (भवने परमार्चिते), where Arjuna saw well-establi-shed sacrificial fire (पावकं सुसमाहीतम्) 1. 206. 14. D. Description and eminence: Serpents in Bhogavatī Purī marked with gem, स्वस्तिक and circles, characterized by कमण्डलु, terrible by nature, of huge shape, and having varying numbers of heads and mouths 5. 101. 5-7; Kauravya called ‘king of serpents’ (नागराज) 1. 206. 13, (पन्नगेश्वर) 1. 206. 33, (उरगपति) 14. 82. 5).
क्रथन: Krathana m.: A mythical bird. Garuḍa fought with him in the air and tore him apart while Garuḍa was on his ex-pedition to get अमृत 1. 28. 18. [According to Nilakaṇṭha, Krathana was a Yakṣa 1. 32. 18 Bom. Ed.]
क्राथ: Krātha1 m.: A mythical serpent. He, with other snakes, received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 15, 12.
Krātha2 m.: A monkey-chief. One of the guardians of Rāma's army of monkeys 3. 267. 19.
क्षेमक: Kṣemaka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 11, 2.
काकुदीक: Kākudīka nt.: Name of a missile. One of the eight missiles Rāma (Jāma-dagnya) enumerated to Duryodhana 5. 94. 38; for the effects produced by these missiles (5. 94. 39-40). [See Akṣisaṃtarjana].
कालदण्ड: Kāladaṇḍa m.: A missile of Kāla. [See Daṇḍa].
किङ्कर: Kiṃkara m.: A missile of Mṛtyu or Yama. Kiṃkara of Mṛtyu identified with his Daṇḍa (?) (मृत्योर् वै किंकरो दण्डः) 13. 61. 24 [किंकर इति दण्डस्य नाम Comm. of an unidentified author, see Cr. Ed. Vol. 17. Part II. Critical Notes p. 1079]; but Kiṃkara and Daṇḍa of Mṛtyu seem to be different (perhaps किंकर = पाश, see end of this entry); Bhīma would fight even with Mṛtyu equipped with Kiṃkara and Daṇḍa (किंकरोद्यतदण्डेन (?) मृत्युनापि व्रजेद् रणम्) 8. 34 20; Duryodhana with his raised गदा compared with Yama with his hand raised with Kiṃkara (वैवस्वतम् इव क्रुद्-धं किंकरोद्यतपाणिनम्) 9. 31. 47 [but Nī. on 8. 50. 24 (Bom. Ed.) करेण्च्द्यतो दण्डो येन तेन मृत्युना समः । किंशब्द उपमार्थे); Yama equipped with Kiṃkara came to take away Satyavān (सुप्तं चैनं यमः साक्षाद् उपागच्छत् सकिंकरः) 3. 282. 38; Yama came to take away Satyavān with पाश in hand (पाशहस्त) 3. 281. 9; Satyavān bound by the पाश 3. 281. 16, and later released 3. 281. 54; hence किंकर likely to be the same as पाश। [See Daṇḍa].
किंकर: Kiṃkara m.: A missile of Mṛtyu or Yama. Kiṃkara of Mṛtyu identified with his Daṇḍa (?) (मृत्योर् वै किंकरो दण्डः) 13. 61. 24 [किंकर इति दण्डस्य नाम Comm. of an unidentified author, see Cr. Ed. Vol. 17. Part II. Critical Notes p. 1079]; but Kiṃkara and Daṇḍa of Mṛtyu seem to be different (perhaps किंकर = पाश, see end of this entry); Bhīma would fight even with Mṛtyu equipped with Kiṃkara and Daṇḍa (किंकरोद्यतदण्डेन (?) मृत्युनापि व्रजेद् रणम्) 8. 34 20; Duryodhana with his raised गदा compared with Yama with his hand raised with Kiṃkara (वैवस्वतम् इव क्रुद्-धं किंकरोद्यतपाणिनम्) 9. 31. 47 [but Nī. on 8. 50. 24 (Bom. Ed.) करेण्च्द्यतो दण्डो येन तेन मृत्युना समः । किंशब्द उपमार्थे); Yama equipped with Kiṃkara came to take away Satyavān (सुप्तं चैनं यमः साक्षाद् उपागच्छत् सकिंकरः) 3. 282. 38; Yama came to take away Satyavān with पाश in hand (पाशहस्त) 3. 281. 9; Satyavān bound by the पाश 3. 281. 16, and later released 3. 281. 54; hence किंकर likely to be the same as पाश। [See Daṇḍa].
कैशिक: Kaiśika m.: One of the different move-ments (मार्ग) adopted while fighting with a sword and a shield. Abhimanyu adopted it while fighting alone with six Kaurava warriors 7. 47. 35 [See Kauśika].

Kaiśika m. (pl.): Name of a people. Caturyu (Jarāsandha ? cf. 2. 13. 8) conquered them along with Pāṇḍyas and Krathakas by the power of his knowledge (in the use of missiles ?) (चतुर्युः स महाराज … विद्याबलाद् यो व्यजयत् पाण्ड्य-क्रथककैशिकान्) 2. 13. 20.
कौमोदकी: Kaumodakī f.: Name of a club (गदा) of Hari (Viṣṇu). It was frightful (घोरा); killer of demons (दैत्यान्तकरणी); when hurled, it produced sound like a thunderbolt (अशनि-निःस्वना); a weapon of Hari (Viṣṇu), it was given by Varuṇa to Kṛṣṇa to equip him to help Agni burn the Khāṇḍava forest 1. 216. 25; Kṛṣṇa asked his charioteer Dāruka to put it in his chariot when he asked Dāruka to keep the chariot ready for his eventual inter-vention in the war 7. 56. 32.
कौशीक: Kauśīka m. (pl.): Name of a movement (मार्ग) adopted while fighting with a mace (गदा). The movement of jumping up; it was adopted by Duryodhana to frustrate the attempts of Bhīma to strike him with his mace 9. 56. 46. [See Kaiśika].
क्रौञ्च: Krauñca, Krauñcāruṇa m.: Name of a particular arrangement of the army (व्यूह) 6. 46. 39; 6. 47. 1; 6. 71. 14; 7. 6. 15. A. History: Taught by Bṛhaspati to Indra at the time of the war between the gods and the demons 6. 46. 40. B. Description: ‘which cannot be penetrated’ (अभेद्य) 6. 47. 1; ‘destroyer of all enemies’ (सर्व-शत्रुनिबर्हण) 6. 46. 39; (परानीक-विनाशन) 6. 46. 40; ‘not seen before by kings’ (अदृष्टपूर्वं राजानः पश्यन्तु कुरुभिः सह) 6. 46. 40. C. Use in the epic war: (1) Yudhiṣṭhira (पार्थ) suggested it to Dhṛṣṭadyumna for arrange-ment of the army on the second day of the war; in this arrangement Arjuna was stationed in front of all the divisions of the army (सर्वसैन्यानाम् अग्रे), Drupada at the ‘head’ (शिरस्); Kuntibhoja and Caidya kings were the ‘eyes’ (चक्षुषी) of the व्यूह, Dāśārṇakas and others were the ‘neck’ (ग्रीवा), Yudhiṣṭhira with Paṭaccaras and others formed the ‘back’ (पृष्ठ), Bhīmasena and Dhṛṣṭadyumna himself took positions as ‘wings’ (पक्षौ); Draupadī's sons and Abhimanyu with Piśācas and others were stationed at the ‘right wing’ (दक्षि-णं पक्षम्), while Nakula and Sahadeva with Agniveśyas and others were stationed at the ‘left wing’ (वामं पार्श्वम्); in addition an अयुत chariots were placed at each ‘wing’, नियुत chariots at the ‘head’, an अर्बुद and twenty thousand at the ‘back’, a नियुत and seventy thousand at the ‘neck’; elephants were stationed at the edge of the wings, at the expanse of the wings and at the ends of the wings (पक्षकोटिप्र-पक्षेषु पक्षान्तेषु च वारणाः); Virāṭa, the Kekayas, Kāśirāja and Śaibya with three अयुतस् of chariot-fighters guarded the ‘rear’ (जघन) of the व्यूह 6. 46. 41-54; (2) On the sixth day Bhīṣma arranged the Kaurava army according to the Krauñca vyūha to oppose the Makara vyūha of the Pāṇḍavas; Bhāradvāja (Droṇa) formed its ‘beak’ (तुण्ड), Aśvat-thāman and Kṛpa its ‘eyes’, Kṛtavarman with the Kāmbojas and others its ‘head’; Śūrasenas and Duryodhana, aided by many kings, its ‘neck’; Prāgjyotiṣa (Bhagadatta) with Madras and others its ‘chest’ (उरस्); Suśarman with his army took position at the ‘left wing’; while Tuṣāras and others stood at the ‘right wing’; Śrutāyus, and Saumadatti (Bhūriśravas) guarded the rear 6. 71. 14-21; called महाव्यूह 6. 73. 24; (3) Dharmarāja (Yudhiṣṭhira) arranged the Pāṇḍava army this way on the eleventh day of the war when Droṇa took charge of the Kaurava army and arranged his army the Śakaṭa way; in the front of the Pāṇḍava army were Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa (व्यूहप्रम्न्खतः 7. 6. 16; अग्रतः 7. 6. 20; बलसेनाग्रगौ 7. 6. 21) 7. 6. 15-21.

Krauñca1 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Family: Son of Himavant (हिम-वतः सुतम्) 3. 214. 31. B. Location: Part of the Śveta mountain 3. 214. 30-31; 34-35. C. Description: Great mountain (महाद्रि) 9. 16. 50; best among the moun-tains (पर्वतश्रेष्ठ) 9. 45. 78; resounding with sounds of Krauñca birds (क्रौञ्च-नादनिनादित) 9. 45. 73; having Śāla and Sarala (pine) trees (सशालस्कन्धसरल) 9. 45. 74; description of the mountain when pierced by the शक्ति of Kārttikeya (the mountain began to burn; the terrified ani-mals, birds and serpents deserted it; the Vidyādharas and the Kinnaras, living on the peaks of the mountain, flew upwards; the Daityas came out in the open in hundreds and thousands and were killed by the follo-wers of Kumāra Kārttikeya) 9. 45. 74-79; the Krauñca mountain, though reduced to a pitiable condition continued, to be resplendent (शोच्याम् अपि दशां प्राप्तो रराजैव स पर्-वतः) 9. 45. 76. D. Mythological events: (1) Kumāra (Kārttikeya) pierced the Krau-ñca mountain with his arrows; through the crevice created by the arrows swans and vultures go to the mountain Meru (तेन हंसाश् च गृध्राश् च मेरुं गच्छन्ति पर्वतम्) 3. 214. 30-31; the mountain, thus shattered, fell down issuing sounds of excessive pain; seeing the Krauñca fall down, other mountains howled excessively due to fear 3. 214. 32; (2) When Kārttikeya killed many Asuras, Bāṇa, the son of Bali, resorted to Krauñca and started harassing gods; when attacked by Kārttikeya, Bāṇa took refuge with the Krauñca; then Kārttikeya pierced Krauñca with the शक्ति given to him by Agni 9. 45. 70, 73, 79, 81. E. Similes: (1) The arrows shot by Arjuna from his Gāṇḍīva entered Karṇa as swans enter the Krauñca (हंसाः क्रौञ्चम् इवाविशन्) 7. 114. 82; (2) The arrows shot by Karṇa at Bhīma entered his left arm as the birds the Krauñca (प्राविशन् … क्रौञ्चं पत्ररथा इव) 7. 109. 29; (3) Śalya, with blood is-suing out of his body when hit by the शक्ति of Yudhiṣṭhira, was like the Krauñca hit by Skanda 9. 16. 50; (4) Ghaṭotkaca said to Aśvatthāman that he would strike at him as did Agnisuta (Skanda) the Krauñca moun-tain 7. 131. 56.

Krauñca2 m.: Name of a mountain. Located in the Krauñcadvīpa, it is des-cribed as a great mountain (क्रौञ्चद्वीपे महाराज क्रौञ्चो नाम महागिरिः) 6. 13. 17; beyond the Krauñca is the mountain called Vāmanaka 6. 13. 17; the country relat-ed to Krauñca is the Kuśala (क्रौञ्चस्य कुशलो देशः) 6. 13. 20.
कर्णपर्वन्: Karṇaparvan nt.: Name of the 73rd पर्वन् of the Bhārata in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 59, 33, 70; it is listed as the eighth पर्वन् in the list of the eighteen major parvans by those who have thought about Bhārata (भारत-चिन्तकैः) 1. 2. 169, 172, 233, 71. Described as containing great wonders (परमाद्भुतम्); it has 69 Adhyāyas and 4900 Ślokas 1. 2. 169, 172; in this पर्वन् we are told the following: (1) the Madrarāja (Śalya) was asked to act as a charioteer; (2) an ancient आख्यान about the destruction of the Tripuras; (3) harsh dispute between Karṇa and Śalya; (4) the story of the swan and the crow; (5) Yudhiṣṭhira and Arjuna getting angry with each other; (6) Karṇa's death at the hands of Arjuna in a duel that was fought from chariots (द्वैरथ) 1. 2. 169-171; the last incident is referred to in Dhṛtarāṣṭra's summary made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 146.
कर्णस्य: Karṇasya vivādaparva: Name of the 55th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha (ज्ञेयं विवादपर्वात्र कर्णस्यापि महात्-मनः) 1. 2. 52, 33, 70; (कृष्णकर्णसं-वादरूपं पर्व Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 2. 64). Referred to in the listing of the contents of the Udyogaparvan (रथम् आरोप्य कृष्णेन यत्र कर्णोनुमन्त्रितः) 1. 2. 148 (अनुमन्त्रितः उपजापितः उपायपूर्वं भेदपूर्वम् Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 2. 236); related to the incidents narrated in the Adhyāyas 5. 138-148.
कापव्यचरित: Kāpavyacarita nt.: The story of Kāpavya, born of a Niṣāda woman from a Kṣatriya father 12. 133. 25, 3. This is cited by Bhīṣma as an ancient narrative (इतिहासं पुरातनम्) 12. 133. 1; it describes how Kāpavya instructed the Dasyus to follow the right path 12. 133. 13-22; one who narrates this Kāpavyacarita need have no fear from the forest-dwellers, nor from human beings, nor immortal ones 12. 133. 25-26.
कामशास्त्र: Kāmaśāstra nt.: A text dealing with the art of love. One who knows how to destroy the (teachings of the) Kāmaśāstra gets over all miseries (एवं यो वेद … वधं वै कामशास्त्रस्य स दुःखान्य् अतिवर्तते 12. 246. 8; Nī. who reads बन्धं वै काम-शास्त्रस्य adds वधम् इति पाठे त्यागम् on Bom. Ed. 12. 254. 8).
कार्ष्ण: Kārṣṇa adj.: of the Veda; the Bhārata or the Mahābhārata so called because it was composed by Kṛṣṇa (Dvaipāyana). One, who having known the Veda of Kṛṣṇa, i. e. the Mahābhārata, recites it to those that are noble-minded, generous, truth-ful, and who are not atheists achieves his objective (अक्षुद्रान् दानशीलांश् च सत्य-शीलान् अनास्तिकान् । काऋष्णं वेदम् इमं विद्वाञ् छ्रावयित्वार्थम् अश्नुते) 1. 56. 17; the reciter is also no doubt freed of the sin of killing an embryo (भ्रूणहत्याकृतं चापि पापं जह्यान् न संशयः) 1. 56. 17; 1. 1. 205. [See Bhārata, Mahābhārata]
किर्मीरवध: Kirmīravadha m.: Name of the 30th पर्वन् of the Bhārata in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 42, 33, 70. Referred to in the listing of the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 106; related to the incidents narrated in the Adhyāya 3. 12.
कीचकानां: Kīcakānāṃ vadhaḥ: Name of the 46th पर्वन् of the Bhārata in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 48, 33, 70. Referred to in the listing of the con-tents of the Virāṭaparvan 1. 2. 131; related to the incidents of the Adhyāyas 4. 13-23.
कुण्डलाहरण: Kuṇḍalāharaṇa nt.: Name of the 43rd पर्वन् of the Bhārata in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 47, 33, 70. Referred to in the listing of the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 127; related to the incidents narrated in Adhyāyas 3. 284-294.
कैरात: Kairāta nt.: Name of the 31st पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 42, 33, 70. Referred to in the listing of the con-tents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 107; alluded to in 5. 195. 12 (यत् तद् घोरं पशुपतिः प्रादाद् अस्त्रं महन् मम । कैराते द्वन्द्वयुद्धे वै तद् इदं मयि वर्तते); the incident in this पर्वन् men-tioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra in his summary made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 109; related to the incidents narrated in the Adhyāyas 3. 24-42.

Kairāta adj.: Of the highest place on the mountain Himavant (where Śiva lives). The place Kairāta, described as the high-est (कैरातम् स्थानम् उत्तमम्) on the mountain Himavant (13. 20. 29), lies beyond the mountains Kailāsa, Mandara and Haima 13. 20. 28-29; Aṣṭāvakra went north to reach this mountain and after descending from it he went round it thrice bowing down his head; he then became a person of cleansed soul; from there he again proceeded northwards (प्रदक्षिणं ततश् चक्रे प्रयतः शिरसा नमन् । धरणीम् अवतीर्याथ पूतात्मासौ तदाभवत् ॥ स तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा त्रिः शैलम् चोत्तरामुखः । … ययौ) 13. 20. 28-30.
क्षेमदर्शीय: Kṣemadarśīya nt.: Name of an Itihāsa (अत्रायं क्षेमदर्शीयम् इतिहासो ऽनुगीयते) 12. 105. 2. It was narrated by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣ-ṭhira in reply to his question how a righte-ous king, when oppressed by his ministers and deprived of his treasure and authority (च्युतः कोशाच् च दण्डाच् च), should act if he sought happiness 12. 105. 1-2; this advice was earlier sought by prince Kṣemadarśa (and hence so called) from the sage Kālaka-vṛkṣīya 12. 105. 3 ff.
कलि: Kali m., Kaliyuga nt.: Name of one of the four Yugas or ages; also called Puṣya (6. 11. 3-4, 7, 12, 13) and Tiṣya (is कलि-पुरस्कृत 12. 327. 76; 12. 337. 42; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 10. 3. (= Cr. Ed. 6. 11. 3 reads तिष्यम् (in place of Cr. Ed. पुष्यम्) and explains it as कलियुगम्). A. Characterization: Characterized as कृष्णयुग (12. 337. 44) and तामसयुग (3. 148. 33). B. Place among the four Yugas: Fourth and the last Yuga, hence referred to as the चतुर्थ युग (युगस्य च चतुर्थस्य राजा भवति कारणम्) 5. 130. 16; 12. 70. 25, or as पश्चिम युगकाल 3. 189. 13; it comes at the close of the Dvāpara Yuga (संक्षेपाद् द्वाप-रस्याथ ततः पुष्यं प्रवर्तते) 6. 11. 4; hence referred to after the Dvāpara as अपर युग 12. 259. 32; Hanūmant told Bhīma that the Kaliyuga will commence soon (after the Dvāpara) (एअतत् कलियुगं नाम अचिराद् यत् प्रवर्तते) 3. 148. 37; after the Kaliyuga commences again the Kṛtayuga (क्षीणे कलियुगे चैव प्रवर्तति कृतं युगम्) 3. 186. 22. C. Duration: Mārkaṇḍeya told Yudhiṣṭhira that the Kali Yuga lasts for 1000 years; it is preceded by dawns of 100 years and followed by evenings of equal duration (सहस्रम् एकं वर्षाणां ततः कलियुगं स्मृतम् । तस्य वर्षशतं संध्या संध्यांशश् च ततः परम् । संध्यासंध्यांशयोस् तुल्यं प्रमाणम् उपधारय) 3. 186. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 188. 23: सन्ध्या पूर्वस्मिन् युगे उत्तर-युगधर्माणाम् उपसर्जनतया संक्र-मः । सन्ध्यांशस् तूत्तरस्मिन् पूर्वयुग-धर्माणाम्); the same duration for Kaliyuga was narrated by Vyāsa to Śuka 12. 224. 20. D. Events marking the advent of the Kali Yuga: (1) The armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas fought each other near the Samanta-pañcaka at the junction of the Dvāpara and the Kali Yuga (अन्तरे चैव सं-प्राप्ते कलिद्वापरयोर् अभूत् । समन्त-पञ्चके युद्धं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः) 1. 2. 9; (2) Nārāyaṇa told Apāntaratamas that when the Tiṣyayuga will have set in the kings born in the line of Bharata, known as the Kurus, will be born of him (i. e. of Apān-taratamas then born as Vyāsa) and that there will be a feud in the family leading to mutual destruction (here Tiṣya, i. e. Kali, is mentioned in place of Dvāpara due to close proximity ?) (पुनस् तिष्ये च संप्रा-प्ते कुरवो नाम भारताः । भविष्यन्ति महात्मानो राजानः प्रथिता भुवि ॥ तेषां त्वत्तः प्रसूतानां कुलभेदो भविष्यति । परस्परविनाशार्थं) 12. 337. 42-43; (3) Nārāyaṇa told Nārada that at the end of the junction of the Dvāpara and the Kali age he would appear in Mathurā for the killing of Kaṃsa (द्वापरस्य कलेश् चैव संधौ पर्यवसानिके । प्रादुर्भा-वः कंसहेतोः मथुरायां भविष्यति) 12. 326. 82; (4) at the end of the Dvā-para and the beginning of the Kali age Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa), along with Saṃkarṣaṇa, is sung according to the Sātvata mode of worship (द्वापरस्य युगस्यान्ते आदौ कलियुगस्य च । सात्वतं विधिस्म् आस्थाय गीतः संकर्षणेन यः) 6. 62. 39. E. Kaliyuga and Nārāyaṇa and Vyāsa: (1) Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that in the Kali Yuga Kṛṣṇa came down to the earth as अधर्म (कृष्णः । कलाव् अधर्मः क्षितिम् आजगाम 13. 143. 9; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 158. 10: कलौ त्व् अधर्म एव बलवान् इति भावः); the god (Nārāyaṇa i. e. Kṛṣṇa-Janārdana 3. 187. 52, 50) told Mārkaṇḍeya that he has dark colour in the Kaliyuga (कृष्णः कलियुगे तथा) 3. 187. 31; तामसं युगम् आसाद्य कृष्णो भवति केशवः) 3. 148. 33; (2) Hari-Nārāyaṇa told Apāntaratamas (12. 337. 38) that when Kṛṣṇayuga (i. e. Kaliyuga) sets in he (as Vyāsa) will have dark colour (कृष्णे युगे च संप्राप्ते कृष्णवर्णो भविष्यसि) 12. 337. 44. F. King and the Kali Yuga: All the Yugas are dependent on the king's behaviour, hence a king is called a युग (राजवृत्तानि सर्वाणि राजैव युगम् उच्यते) 12. 92. 6; according to Bhīṣma all the Yugas, including Kali, are rooted in a king (राजमूलानि सर्वाणि) 12. 139. 10; it is the king who makes the Yugas what they are and hence he is also the cause of the fourth Yuga (i. e. the Kaliyuga) (युगस्य च चतुर्थ-स्य राजा भवति कारणम्) 5. 130. 16; 12. 70. 25; by bringing about the Kali age the king incurs immense sin (कलेः प्रवर्तनाद् राजा पापम् अत्यन्तम् अश्नुते) 12. 70. 27; by bringing about the Kaliyuga (not directly stated) the evil-doer (i. e. the king) lives eternally in the hell (ततो वसति दुष्कर्मा नरके शाश्वतीः समाः) 5. 130. 18; when the king wholly gives up दण्डनीति and oppresses his subjects unjustly the Kali age makes its appearance (दण्डनीतिं परित्य-ज्य यदा कार्त्स्न्येन भूमिपः । प्रजाः क्लिश्नात्य् अयोगेन प्रविश्यति तदा कलिः) 12. 70. 18; where the sinful ones move about freely among the righteous, there the Kali age (? or the evil spirit ?) meets the kings (? यत्र पापा ज्ञायमानाश् चरन्ति सतां कलिर् विन्दति तत्र राज्ञाः) 12. 92. 27 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 91. 28: राज्ञः नृपान्). G. Kali Yuga and धर्म: While describing the four Yugas Hanūmant told Bhīma that in the Kali Yuga धर्म stands only on one foot (पादेनैकेन कौन्तेय धर्मः कलियुगे स्थितः) 3. 148. 32; (पादेन त्व् अपरे (i. e. कलौ) युगे) 12. 259. 32; (ततस् तिष्ये ऽथ सं-प्राप्ते युगे कलिपुरस्कृते । एकपाद-स्थितो धर्मो यत्र तत्र भविष्यति) 12. 327. 76 (however, commentator Vādirāja: तिष्ये पुष्यनक्षत्रे, note on this stanza in the Cr. Ed.); 12. 224. 23; gods asked Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa what they should do when the धर्म in the Tiṣya Yuga stood on one foot 12. 327. 77; in the Kali Yuga (not directly mentioned) अधर्म rules over men in three parts while धर्म attends men only in one part (त्रिभिर् अंशैर् अधर्मस् तु लोकान् आक्रम्य तिष्ठति । चतुर्-थांशेन धर्मस् तु मनुष्यान् उपति-ष्ठति) 3. 188. 12; in the Kali Yuga धर्म is reduced to its sixteenth कोला on account of the misbehaviour of kings (तथा कलियुगे प्राप्ते राज्ञां दुश्चरितेन ह । भवेत् कालविशेष्ण कला धर्मस्य षोडशी) 12. 259. 33. H. Nature of the Kali Yuga and its effects on men: Vedic practices dwin-dle, so also the religious and the sacrificial rites; on the other hand, seasonal calamities, diseases, lassitude, vices like anger and others, calamities and mental agonies are ex-perienced (वेदाचाराः प्रशाम्यन्ति धर्म-यज्ञक्रियास् तथा ॥ ईतयो व्याधयस् तन्द्री दोषाः क्रोधादयस् तथा । उपद्रवाश् च वर्तन्ते आधयो व्याधयस् तथा ॥ 3. 148. 33-34; also cf. 3. 186. 24-55; 3. 188. 5-6, 13-84; 12. 224. 62; in the Kali Yuga the Vedas are seen (i. e. practised) by some and not by others; they, which alone serve as dams of धर्म, fall into ruin along with the sacrifices (दृश्यन्ते नापि दृश्यन्ते वेदाः कलियुगे ऽखिलाः । उत्सीदन्ते सयज्ञाश् च केवला धर्मसेतवः ॥ ) 12. 224. 66; 12. 230. 15-17; the study of the Vedas dwindles gradually in each succeeding Yuga (वेद-वादाश् चानुयुगं ह्रसन्तीति च नः श्रुतम्) 12. 224. 25; the अधर्म in the Yugas other than the Kṛta is on increase due to the practice of theft, falsehood and deceipt 12. 224. 23; the duties (धर्माः) to be followed in the Kali Yuga are different (from those of the other Yugas); they have been prescribed as if keeping in mind the (lowered) capacity of men in that age (अन्ये कलियुगे धर्मा यथाशक्तिकृता इव) 12. 224. 26 = 12. 252. 8; giving gifts is specially recommended for the Kali Yuga (दानम् एव कलौ युगे) 12. 224. 27; in the Kali age अधर्म is practised by many, and धर्म only by a few; all the Varṇas are disinclined to follow धर्म proper to them 12. 70. 19; also 20-24; the nature of men in the Puṣyayuga is describ-ed also in 6. 11. 12-13; strict adherence to धर्म is not to be expected in the Kali Yuga-this is what Kṛṣṇa implied in his words addressed to Balarāma to assuage his wrath (प्राप्तं कलियुगं विद्धि) 9. 59. 21; in the Kali age (as in the Dvāpara) it is necessary for people to he paired to beget children (द्वापरे मैथुनो धर्मः प्रजा-नाम् अभवन् नृप । तथा कलियुगे राजन् द्वन्द्वम् आपेदिरे जनाः ॥ ) 12. 200. 37; the ascetics born in the Kali age (as also in the Tretā and the Dvāpara) are beset with doubts (त्रेतायां द्वापरे चैव कलिजाश् च ससंशयाः । तपस्विनः) 12. 230. 7; evil tribes like the Talavaras, the Andhrakas and others which originate in the south (दक्षिणा-पथजन्मानः) and those like the Yaunas, the Kāmbojas, and other which have their origin in the north (उत्तरापथजन्मानः) roam on the earth in the Tretā and the follow-ing Yugas (i. e. also in the Kali) (त्रेता-प्रभृति वर्तन्ते ते जना भरतर्षभ) 12. 200. 39-42; Dyumatsena told Satyavān that if the Dasyus were not killed then in the Kaliyuga people would say to each other: “this is mine, not his”, it would then be difficult to carry on every day life (ममेदम् इति नास्यैतत् प्रवर्तेत कलौ युगे । लोकयात्रा न चैव स्यात्) 12. 259. 6; if one always recites the description of the origin of cows he is freed of the impurity of the Kali age (? or of evil spirit ?) (इमं गवां प्र-भवविधानम् उत्तमं पठन् सदा … विमुच्यते कलिकलुषेण मानवः) 13. 76. 32. I. Span of life: In the Puṣya (i. e. the Kali) Yuga there is no fixed span of life; people die (even) in the womb or immediately after they are born (न प्रमाणस्थितिर् ह्य् अस्ति पुष्ये ऽस्मिन् भरतर्षभ गर्भस्थाश् च म्रियन्ते ऽत्र तथा जाता म्रियन्ति च ॥ ) 6. 11. 7; the life-span, as also other faculties, of human beings decrease successively in each following Yuga (आयुर् वीर्यम् … । मनुस्याणाम् अनुयुगं ह्रसतीति निबोध मे ॥ ) 3. 188. 13; however, life is expected to be of a hundred years ( … त्रेतादिष्व् एते-सां पादशो ह्रसते वयः) 12. 224. 24, 25. J. Kali as a name of Sūrya: Kali occurs among the 108 names of Sūrya taught by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 22 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 3. 20: कलिः सर्वमलाश्रय इत्य् एकं नाम).
काम्याष्टमी: Kāmyāṣṭamī f.: Name of the eighth day (of the bright or the dark fortnight ?) of the month (?) One should give cows and then observe the गोव्रत (live like a cow ?) for three nights, spending one of the nights with cows; then from the Kāmyāṣṭamī he should live three nights on milk or on cow-dung and cow-urine (गा वै दत्त्वा गोव्रती स्यात् त्रिरात्रं निशां चैकां संवसेतेह ताभिः । काम्या-ष्टम्यां वर्तितव्यं त्रिरात्रं रसैर् वा गोः शकृता प्रस्नवैर् वा ॥ ) 13. 75. 19.
कार्तिक: Kārttika m.: Name of a month. A. Epic event related with this month: The wrestling match between Bhīma and Jarāsandha began on the first day of Kārttika 2. 21. 17. B. Religious rite performed in this month: Aṅgiras told Bhīṣma that if one took food only once a day in Kārttika he became brave, got many wives, and became famous (कार्त्तिकं तु नरो मासं यः कुर्याद् एकभोजनम् । शूरश् च बहु-भार्यश् च कीर्तिमांश् चैव जायते ॥ ) 13. 109. 29. [See Kaumuda]
कार्त्तिक: Kārttika m.: Name of a month. A. Epic event related with this month: The wrestling match between Bhīma and Jarāsandha began on the first day of Kārttika 2. 21. 17. B. Religious rite performed in this month: Aṅgiras told Bhīṣma that if one took food only once a day in Kārttika he became brave, got many wives, and became famous (कार्त्तिकं तु नरो मासं यः कुर्याद् एकभोजनम् । शूरश् च बहु-भार्यश् च कीर्तिमांश् चैव जायते ॥ ) 13. 109. 29. [See Kaumuda]
कार्त्तिकी: Kārttikī (Cr. Ed. also Kārtikī) f.: The night of full moon in the month of Kārttika. A. Description: Most holy among the पर्वन्स् (पुण्यतमा रात्रिः पर्वसन्धौ) 3. 179. 16; the best conjunction (योगम् उत्तमम्) 3. 179. 17. B. Epic events connected with this तिथि: (1) When the Pāṇḍavas lived near the river Sarasvatī there occurred the Kārttikī of the autumn season; the Pāṇḍavas spent that night of best con-junction in the company of the holy ascetics and when the darkness set in (तमिस्राभ्य्-उदये) they, with Dhaumya, went to the Kāmyaka forest 3. 179. 16-18; (2) Vidura reported to Yudhiṣṭhira that Dhṛtarāṣṭra had decided to retire to the forest on the following Kārtikī (गमिष्यति वनं राजन् कार्तिकीम् आगताम् इमाम्) 15. 17. 3; before setting for the forest Dhṛtarāṣṭra wished to give rich gifts on the Kārtikī (कार्तिक्याम्) 15. 19. 15; he gave those gifts for ten days preced-ing (the Kārttikī) (दशाहम् एवं दानानि दत्त्वा राजाम्बिकासुतः) 15. 20. 17; gifts given by him detailed in 15. 20. 3-16; the gifts were intended as a श्राद्ध or an और्ध्वदेहिक for Bhīṣma and the rest 15. 17. 4-5, 9, 17; 15. 19. 11; Dhṛtarāṣṭra there-by wanted to pay back the debt he owed to his sons and friends (बभूव पुत्रपौत्रा-णाम् अनृणो भरतर्षभ) 15. 20. 17; 15. 18. 11; he started for the forest when the Brāhmaṇas, at his instance, offered an इष्टि on the Kārttikī 15. 21. 2. C. Bad omens: Among the bad omens reported by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra before the start of the great war one was related to the night of the Kārttikī full moon when the moon having the colour of fire, shining in the sky of the same colour, became lustreless and could not be noticed (अलक्ष्यः प्रभया हीनः पौर्णमासीं च कार्त्तिकीम् । चन्द्रो ऽभूद् अग्निवर्णश् च समवर्णे नभस्तले ॥ ) 6. 2. 23. D. Religious importance: (1) Merit of a person who visits Puṣkara on the Kārtikī grows undecayingly 3. 80. 52; spending one full moon Kārtikī night at Puṣkara was equal to offering अग्निहोत्र for full hundred years 3. 80. 57; (2) Pilgrims bathe in the river Sarasvatī for a year following the occurrence of the Kārtikī (सरस्वत्यां महाराज अनु संवत्सरं हि ते । स्नायन्ते भरतश्रेष्ठ वृत्तां वै कार्तिकीं सदा) 3. 80. 121; with this bath one shone like a moon and obtained fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 80. 122; (3) Virūpākṣa, the king of the Rākṣasas used to feed a thousand excellent Brāhmaṇas on the autumnal full moon day of the Kārttika; according to the श्रुति texts Brāhmaṇas should be given preci-ous stones (रत्नानि) on that day; Virūpākṣa assured the Brāhmaṇas that they need have no fear from the Rākṣasas on that one day of Kārttikī and they need not be in a hurry to go away 12. 165. 9, 16, 23; details of how Virūpākṣa honoured Brāhmaṇas 12 165. 10-14, 17-19.
कुहू: Kuhū f.: Name of the second Amā-vāsyā day (if the Amāvāsyā extends over two days (see Ait. Br. 32. 9, Nirukta 11. 31) and on which the moon is not seen. Described as venerable (भगवती) and one whose only digit is very small (एकानंशा) 3. 208. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 218. 8: एका कला अनंशा अल्पांशवती); personified, she was the eighth daughter of Aṅgiras, and was called Kuhū because people, having seen her, were struck with wonder (यां तु दृष्ट्वा भगवतीं जनः कुहुकुहायते) 3. 208. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 218. 8: कुहुकुहायते विस्मितो भवति); Kuhū formed one of the four reins (योक्त्र) for the horses yoked to the chariot of Mahādeva when it was made ready for his fight with the Tripuras 8. 24. 74; she attended the investiture of Kumāra (Skanda) as the general of the gods which took place near the river Sarasvatī 9. 44. 12, 16; Brāhmaṇas call Devasenā, chief queen of Skanda, by different names, one of them being Kuhū (स्कन्दस्य महिषीम्  … षष्ठीं यां ब्राह्मणाः प्राहुः … सिनी-वालीं कुहूं चैव) 3. 218. 47.
कृत: Kṛta, Kṛtayuga nt.: Name of the first among the four Yugas; also called Devayuga (1. 14. 5; 2. 11. 1; 3. 92. 6; 10. 18. 1; 12. 3. 19; 13. 82. 24, Ādiyuga (6. 76. 18; 13. 135. 11), Prājāpatyayuga (12. 113. 4), and Dharmayuga (12. 308. 7). A. Description: Auspicious (शुभ) 1. 14. 5; 12. 336. 31; completely free from the three गुणस् (सत्त्व, रजस् and तमस्), (त्रैगुण्यपरिवर्जित) 13. 148. 22; the best period (श्रेष्ठः कालः) 5. 130. 14; 12. 324. 5; 12. 327. 73; the best among the Yugas (युगोत्तम) 13. 148. 11. B. Place among the Yugas: When Brahmā created the worlds, the first Yuga to occur was the Kṛta (ततः प्रावर्तत तदा आदौ कृत-युगं शुभम्) 12. 336. 31; 6. 11. 4; 14. 44. 8; first Yuga after the dissolution of the entire world (आदितः मनुजव्याघ्र कृत्-स्नस्य जगतः क्षये … ततो कृतं युगं) 3. 186. 17-18; hence called आदियुग and प्रथमकल्पित 12. 322. 51; hence also the words आदौ and पुरा (or पूर्वम्) often used with Kṛta (12. 59. 13; 12. 336. 31, and many other citations in section D below); Kṛta sets in again at the end of the fourth Kali Yuga; Yudhiṣṭhira asked Mārkaṇḍeya what would be the (final) stage of Kali when its end will have arrived and after which Kṛta will commence again (युगक्षये ॥ कां च काष्ठां समा-साद्य पुनः संपत्स्यते कृतम्) 3. 188. 6-7; 3. 186. 22. C. Duration: Mārka-ṇḍedya told Yudhiṣṭhira that the duration of the Kṛta Yuga was 4000 years; it had dawns of 400 years and twilights of the same duration (चत्वार्य् आहुः सहस्राणि वर्षाणां तत् कृतं युगम् । तस्य तावच्छती संध्या संध्यांशश् च ततः परम् ॥ ) 3. 186. 18 (cf. Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 188. 23 above Kali, section C, p. 234); the same duration of Kṛta told by Vyāsa to Śuka 12. 224. 18-19. D. Events occurring in the Kṛta Yuga: (1) All beings are produced from Viṣṇu at the advent of the Kṛta Yuga and are reabsorbed into him at the end of that Yuga 13. 135. 11; (2) The creation of the world, the creation of Saṃkarṣaṇa, Prad-yumna, Aniruddha and Brahman, Nārāyaṇa's incarnation as Varāha to reestablish the earth and kill Hiraṇyākṣa, as Nṛsiṃha to kill Hiraṇyakaśipu, and as Vāmana to make Bali a resident of Pātāla—all these events are said to have occurred in the Kṛta Yuga which is not named 12. 326. 67-76; (also cf. 12. 337. 29-36 where these three incarna-tions are mentioned without naming Kṛta-yuga); (3) Formerly, in the Kṛta Yuga of the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara, Nārā-yaṇa was born as Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Hari and Kṛṣṇa (नारायणो हि विश्वात्मा चतुर्-मूरतिः सनातनः । धर्मात्मजः संब-भूव … ॥ कृते युगे महाराज पुरा स्वा-यंभुवे ऽन्तरे । नरो नारायणश् चैव हरिः कृष्णस् तथैव च ॥ ) 12. 321. 8-9; (4) In the Devayuga when the Daityendras ruled the three worlds Viṣṇu entered the womb of Aditi (पुरा देवयुगे तात … ) 13. 82. 24-25; (5) In the Devayuga Prajā-pati had two daughters (पुरा देवयुगे … ) 1. 14. 5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 16. 5: देव-युगे सत्ययुगे); (6) In the Kṛta Yuga all gods approached Varuṇa and requested him to be the ruler of waters 9. 46. 5-6; (7) In the Devayuga, Āditya came down from the heaven to visit the world of mortals when he met Nārada (पुरा देवयुगे राजन् … ) 2. 11. 1; (8) In one of the past Devayugas, the gods, desirous of giving offerings, arranged the sacrifice following the prescriptions of the Vedas (ततो देवयुगे ऽतीते देवा वै समकल्पयन् । यज्ञम् वेद-प्रमाणेन विधिवद् यष्टुम् ईप्सवः) 10. 18. 1; (9) Lomaśa told Yudhiṣṭhira that formerly in the Devayuga he had seen that the gods liked the धर्म and the Asuras deserted it (पुरा देवयुगे चैव दृष्टं सर्वं मया विभो । अरोचयन् सुरा धर्-मं धर्मं तत्यजिरे ऽसुराः) 3. 92. 6; (10) Gods and demons churned the ocean in the Ādiyuga 6. 76. 18; (11) There were fierce Dānavas, known as Kāleyas, in the Kṛta Yuga 3. 98. 3; (12) Asura Gṛtsa carried away the wife of Bhṛgu in the Deva-yuga (पुरा देवयुगे तात … ) 12. 3. 19; (13) In the Kṛta Yuga Manu held the दण्ड (आसीत् कृतयुगे पूर्वं मनुर् दण्डधरः प्रभुः) 14. 4. 2; (14) God Nārāyaṇa told the seven sages (12. 322. 27, 31) that the अनुशासन promulgated by him and the शास्त्र, together with the अङ्गस् and the Upaniṣad, will be established by them in Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa in the Kṛta Yuga (not directly named) (उत्पन्ने ऽङ्गिरसे चैव युगे प्रथमकल्पिते । साङ्गोपनिषदं शास्त्रं स्थापयित्वा बृहस्पतौ) 12. 322. 51; (15) In the Kṛta there was a famous sage Taṇḍi who, as a devotee, propitiated god for ten thousand years by practising समाधि 13. 16. 12; (16) Formerly in the the Kṛta Yuga an excellent Brāhmaṇa called Ārṣṭiṣeṇa lived in a गुरुकुल; he studied diligently, but could not complete the study of either the विद्यास् or the Vedas (पुरा कृतयुगे … ) 9. 39. 3-4; (17) Formerly in the Kṛta Yuga there lived a king Avikam-paka who was overpowered in battle by enemies (पुरा कृतयुगे तात … ) 12. 248. 7; (18) In the Kṛta Yuga there was a famous sage Sāvarṇi who practised austerities for six thousand years to satisfy Rudra 13. 14. 70; (19) Formerly in the Kṛta Yuga there was a sage Vyāghrapāda who was versed in the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas (पुरा कृतयुगे तात … ) 13. 14. 75; (20) In the Dharmayuga, when Janaka ruled Mithilā, a certain भिक्षुकी called Sulabhā roamed alone on the earth 12. 308. 7; (21) In the Prājāpatyayuga (i. e. the Kṛtayuga) there once lived a large camel who remembered his previous lives (जातिस्-मरः); he observed scrupulously the vows and practised severe austerities in a forest 12. 113. 4; (22) Formerly in the Kṛta Yuga a Rākṣasa called Cārvāka practised austerities in the Badarī Āśrama and was blessed with a boon by Brahman (पुरा कृतयुगे … ) 12. 39. 39; (23) Nārāyaṇa told Nārada that formerly in the Kṛta Yuga when the Veda and the श्रुति were lost, he retrieved them and (the worlds) were again supplied with the Vedas and the श्रुतिस् (?) (यदा वेदश्रुतिर् नष्टा मया प्रत्याहृता पुरा । सवेदाः सश्रुतीकाश् च कृताः पूर्वं कृते युगे ॥ ) 12. 326. 94; (24) Formerly, during the second birth of Brahmā from the eyes of Nārāyaṇa in the Kṛta Yuga, Rudra, who received the धर्म of the Ekāntins from Soma and who practised योग, taught it to the Vālakhilyas ( … पुरा कृतयुगे नृप) 12. 336. 15-16; the practice of the धर्म of the Ekāntins formed such an important characteristic of the Kṛta Yuga that if in any other Yuga the world became full of the Ekāntins that would mean the advent of the Kṛta Yuga—this is what Vaiśaṃpāyana told Janamejaya (यद्य् एकान्-तिभिर् आकीर्णं जगत् स्यात् कुरुनन्दन ।  … भवेत् कृतयुगप्राप्तिः) 12. 336. 58; (25) Hari-Nārāyaṇa told Brahmā, born for the fourth time from his ears (12. 336. 23), to learn the Sātvata Dharma, from him and establish it in the Kṛta Yuga 12. 336. 27; this धर्म was hence called Kārtayugadharman 12. 336. 29; Brahmā, as instructed by Nārāyaṇa, initiated first the Kṛta Yuga and then the Sātvata धर्म spread among the people 12. 336. 31; (26) In the fifth birth of Brahman from the nose of Nārāyaṇa (12. 336. 36), at the beginning of the Kṛtayuga, Prajāpati Vīraṇa learnt the Sātvata Dharma from Sanatkumāra 12. 336. 37; (27) In the seventh birth of Brahman from a lotus (12. 336. 44), Nārāyaṇa him-self instructed Pitāmaba in the Sātvata धर्म at the beginning of the Kṛta Yuga (not named) तत्रैष धर्मः कथितः स्वयं नारायणेन हि ॥ पितामहाय शुद्-धाय युगादौ लोकधारिणे) 12. 336. 44-45; (28) At the request of Yudhiṣṭhira Bhīṣma told him how at the beginning, in the Kṛta Yuga, a kingdom first came into existence (यथा राज्यं समुत्पन्-नम् आदौ कृतयुगे ऽभवत्) 12. 59. 13; (29) Formerly in the Kṛta Yuga the ascetics residing in the Naimiṣa forest were engaged in a twelve-yearly sacrificial session (पूर्वं कृतयुगे राजन् … ) 9. 36. 39. F. Nārāyaṇa (Kṛṣṇa) and the Kṛta Yuga: Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa (who was the same as Kṛṣṇa-Janārdana 3. 187. 52, 50) told Mārkaṇḍeya that his colour in the Kṛta Yuga was white (श्वेतः कृतयुगे वर्णः) 3. 187. 31; Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that Kṛṣṇa was complete Dharma in the Kṛta Yuga (कृते युगे धर्म आसीत् समग्रः) 13. 143. 9. G. King and the Kṛta Yuga: The king is the creator of the Kṛta Yuga (राजा कृतयुगस्रष्टा) 5. 130. 16 = 12. 70. 25, (also cf. राजा कालस्य कारणम् 12. 70. 6); Kṛta and the remaining three Yugas depend on the conduct of the king and hence the king is identical with Yuga (राजवृत्तानि सर्वाणि राजैव युगम् उच्यते) 12. 92. 6; (राजमूलानि सर्वाणि) 12. 139. 10; when the king fully followed दण्डनीति then prevailed the Kṛta Yuga, the best of time (दण्डनीत्यां यदा राजा सम्यक् कार्त्स्न्येन वर्तते । तदा कृतयुगं नाम कालः श्रेष्ठः प्रवर्तते ॥ ) 5. 130. 14 = 12. 70. 7; Dyumatsena told Satyavān that in the Kṛta Yuga the king followed the instruc-tion (how a king should rule 12. 259. 24-30) as his primary principle (एतत् प्रथम-कल्पेन राजा कृतयुगे ऽभजत्) 12. 259. 32; a king, as the creator of Kṛta, enjoyed in the heaven endlessly (कृतस्य करणाद् राजा स्वर्गम् अत्यन्तम् अश्नुते) 5. 130. 17 = 12. 70. 26; king Yayāti was described by Aṣṭaka as the best among those born in the Kṛta Yuga (कार्तयुगप्रधान) 1. 85. 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 90. 1: कार्तयुगप्र-धान । कृतयुगे भवाः कार्तयुगाः॑अत्य-न्तनिष्पापा तेषां मुख्यतमेत्य् अर्थः). H. Kṛta and धर्म: In the Kṛta Yuga the ancient धर्म prevails (यत्र धर्मः सनातनः) 3. 148. 10; in that Yuga the eternal धर्म of the four वर्णस् stands on all its four feet (i. e. is in no way deficient) (कृते युगे चतुष्पादश् चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य शाश्वतः) 3. 148. 21; formerly in the Kṛta Yuga Dharma, the bull, without deceit and free from vices stood established in its entirety among men (कृते चतुष्पात् सकलो निर्व्याजोपाधिवर्-जितः । वृषः प्रतिष्ठितो धर्मो मनुष्येष्व् अभवत् पुरा ॥ ) 3. 188. 10 (Nī. on 3. 190. 9: वृष इव चतुष्पात्); 12. 327. 73; both धर्म, on its four feet, and truth are fully established in the Kṛta Yuga (चतुष्पात् सकलो धर्मः सत्यं चैव कृते युगे) 12. 224. 22; since धर्म is not contaminated by अधर्म (नाधर्मेणा-गमः कश्चित् 12. 224. 22) it does not get diminished (धर्मो न ह्रसते क्वचित्) 1. 58. 22; धर्म always prospers and अधर्म is destroyed 3. 189. 7; 12. 70. 8; धर्म in the Kṛta Yuga was established among the Brāhmaṇas who had mastered their self, who had practised austerities and who had studied the Vedas (आत्मवत्सु तपोवत्सु श्रुतवैसु प्रतिष्ठितः) 12. 224. 67; धर्म in different Yugas is different 12. 224. 26 = 12. 252. 8; austerity is the best धर्म for the Kṛta (तपः परं कृतयुगे) 12. 24. 27; in the Kṛta Yuga the only धर्म is renunciation (धर्मः संन्यास एव च) 3. 148. 13; one is not supposed to get angry in the Kṛta Yuga (न रोषं कर्तुम् अर्हसि । नैष धर्मः कृतयुगे यस् त्वं रोषम् अचीकृथाः) 12. 323. 17. I. Kṛta and the sacrifice: In the Kṛta Yuga performance of sacrifices is not pre-scribed (त्रेतायुगे विधिस् त्व् एषां यज्ञा-नां न कृते युगे) 12. 224. 62; the sages who assembled for a sacrifice told gods who wanted a goat to be killed that that was not the धर्म of good people; they reminded the gods that they were in the Kṛta Yuga when an animal was not offered (नैष धर्मः सतां देवा यत्र वध्येत वै पशुः । इदं कृतयुगं श्रेष्ठं कथं वध्येत वै पशुः ॥ ) 12. 324. 5; (अहिंस्या यज्ञपशवो युगे ऽस्मिन् नैतद् अन्यथा) 12. 327. 73; the offerings offered by Brahman and others to Viṣṇu in a Vaiṣṇava Kratu were offered according to the prescriptions meant for the Kṛta Yuga and, as a result, they reach-ed the Puruṣa who had the brightness of the sun and who was above darkness (ते कार्त-युगधर्माणो भागा परमसत्कृताः । प्रापुर् आदित्यवर्णं तं पुरुषं तमसः परम् ॥ ) 12. 327. 50 (commentator Vidyā-sāgara: कार्तयुगधर्माणः अहिंसादि-लक्षणकृतस्वभावाः मन्त्रलोपतन्त्रलोप-क्रियालोपहिंसादिरहिताः परमसंस्कृताः, cf. the note on this stanza in the Cr. Ed.); but according to Bhīṣma when the king, in any other Yuga, employed दण्डनीती properly, condition was as good as in the Kṛta Yuga (12. 70. 7); in such a Kṛta Yuga, all the three Varṇas offered Soma sacrifices according to rites (सोमे प्रयत्नं कुर्वन्ति त्रयो वर्णा यथाविधि) (Editor's note on the stanza: सोमे = देवतादीन् उद्दिश्य सोमयागे) and the Vedic rites were faultlessly performed (वैदिकानि च कर्माणि भवन्त्य् अविगुणान्य् उत) 12. 70. 9. J. Nature of the Kṛta Yuga, its effects on men: Hanūmant told Bhīma that the times in the Kṛta Yuga were different from those in the other Yugas (अन्यः कृतयुगे कालस् त्रेतायां द्वापरे परः) 3. 148. 6; Kṛta Yuga described by different persons: (1) by Hanūmant to Bhīma 3. 148. 11-22 (Kṛta Yuga was com-pletely free from the three qualities (viz. सत्त्व, रजस् and तमस्) (त्रैगुण्यपरि-वर्जितम् 3. 148. 22); (2) by Vaiśaṃpāyana to Janamejaya 1. 58. 8-24 (काले गावः प्रसूयन्ते नार्यश् च भरतर्षभ । फलन्त्य् ऋतुषु वृक्षाश् च पुष्पाणि च फलानि च ॥ 1. 58. 23); (3) by Mārka-ṇḍeya to the Pāṇḍavas 3. 189. 8-13 (षट्-कर्मनिरता विप्राः क्षत्रिया रक्षणे रताः ॥ शुस्रूषायां रताः शूद्रास् तथा वर्णत्र-यस्य च । एष धर्मः कृतयुगे … ॥ 3. 189. 12-13); (4) by Bhīṣma to Yudhi-ṣṭhira (when a king in any Yuga practised दण्डनीति properly) 12. 70. 8-13 (the quali-ties of Kṛta age are called कार्तयुगान् गुण्गान् 12. 70. 13, also कार्तयुगधर्माणो भागाः 12. 327. 50); (5) by Saṃjaya to Dhṛta-rāṣṭra 6. 11. 8-9; in general the people of the Kṛta Yuga were possessed of fortitude, were diligent in their duties, knew the proper time for the use of valour (धृतिमन्तश् च दक्षाश् च स्वे स्वे कर्मणि भारत । परा-क्रमविधानज्ञा नराः कृतयुगे ऽभवन्) 3. 159. 2; the ascetics of the Kṛta Yuga were calm and they remained steady in the सत्त्व quality (तपस्विनः प्रशान्ताश् च सत्त्वस्थाश् च कृते युगे) 12. 230. 7 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 238. 7: प्रशान्ताः निःसंशयाः); all the ascetics then made no distinction between पौरुष, दैव and स्वभाव as the cause of the success in कर्म and had neither love nor hatred for the ऋच्स्, the यजुसेस् and the सामन्स्; hence they practised austerities (and did not perform sacrifices) अपृथग्दर्शिनः सर्वे ऋक्सामसु यजुःषु च । कामद्वेषौ पृथग् दृष्ट्वा तपः कृत उपासते ॥ ) 12. 230. 8 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 238. 8: वेदत्रये ऽपि भेदम् अपश्यन्तः काम्यादीन् पृथक्कृत्य तपो ज्ञानम् उपासते श्रयन्ति); 12. 224. 63 (Kṛta not mentioned, but Nī., on Bom. Ed. 12. 232. 33 supplies it: अद्वैतनिष्ठा मर्त्यास् तप एव योगम् एव कृतयुगे ऽनुतिष्ठन्तीति शेषः); when Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura were born the country of the Kurus (कुरुजाङ्गलम्), the Kurus themselves and the Kurukṣetra, all prospered 1. 102. 1; at that time a condition similar to the Kṛta Yuga prevailed in the regions of the different kingdoms (प्रदे-शेष्व् अपि राष्ट्राणां कृतम् युगम् अवर्तत) 1. 102. 5; this condition is described in 1. 102. 2-11; people in the Kṛta Yuga did not have to cohabit to beget children, they could have them by mere thought (न चैषां मैथुनो धर्मो बभूव भरतर्षभ । संकल्पाद् एव चैतेषाम् अपत्यम् उदपद्-यत ॥ ) 12. 200. 35; in the Kṛta Yuga evil tribes like the Talavaras, the Andhrakas etc. in the south and the Yaunas (Yavanas), Kāmbojas etc. in the north did not exist on the earth 12. 200. 39-43; there were no भिक्षुस् and those who have sectarian marks (लिङ्गि-नः); similarly there were no alternatives to the four आश्रमस्; all this happened when the Kṛta Yuga passed away and the दण्डनीति was no longer practised—thus Indra told to Māndhātṛ 12. 65. 24-25. K. Expecta-tion of life: In the Kṛta Yuga people were free from diseases, succeeded in achieving all objectives and lived for four hundred years (अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्थाश् चतुर्वर्षशता-युषः । कृते) 12. 224. 24; however, according to Saṃjaya people lived for four thousand years (चत्वारि च सहस्राणि वर्षाणां कुरुसत्तम । आयुःसंख्या कृतयुगे सं-ख्याता राजसत्तम ॥ ) 6. 11. 5 (apparently there is confusion between the duration of the Kṛta Yuga (above section C) and life-expectancy of human beings); also cf. सहस्रशतजीविनः ताः प्रजाः … ॥ … एवं कृतयुगे सम्यग् वर्तमाने तदा नृप) 1. 58. 10, 24; men lived as long as they liked and they had no fear of Yama 12. 200. 34; (न क्षीयन्ते च वै प्रजाः) 3. 148. 11; (नाल्पायुर् दृश्यते नरः) 12. 70. 11; but the life expectation, virility etc. decrease successively in the Yugas that follow the Kṛta (आयुर् वीर्यम् अथो बुद्धिर् … मनु-ष्याणाम् अनुयुगं ह्रसतीति निबोध मे) 3. 188. 13. L. Kṛta as the name of Sūrya: Kṛta appears among the 108 names of Sūrya taught by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 22. M. Etymology: The etymology is implied when it is said that in the Kṛta Yuga (whatever needs be done) is done and does not remain undone (कृतम् एव न कर्त-व्यं तस्मिन् काले युगोत्तमे) 3. 148. 10 [Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 149. 11: कृतम् एव सर्वे कृतकृत्या एवेत्य् अर्थः । तत एव हेतोः कृतयुगं नाम ॥ ). [Nī., Bom. Ed. 3. 191. 3, who reads विप्रैश् चोरक्षयश् चैव कृते क्षेमं भविष्यति in place of the Cr. Ed. विप्रैश् चोरक्षये चैव कृते (3. 189. 3) interprets कृते युगे; the words कृत, त्रेता etc. occurring in 5. 140. 7-15 (= Bom. Ed. 5. 142. 7-15) are interpreted by Nī. as the Yuga names and not as names of the throws of dice in a dice game].
कृत्तिका: Kṛttikā f. (pl.): Name of a conste-llation (the Pleiads); (personified as the mothers of Skanda, said to be the wives of the six seers Aṅgiras and others 3. 214. 1-16; 3. 218. 30; 3. 207. 4; 3. 218. 27; 9. 43. 10-13; 9. 45. 86; 13. 84. 76; 13. 86. 5, 8, 10, 13; hence Skanda known as Kārtti-keya (कृत्तिकाभ्युपपत्तेश् च कार्त्तिकेय इति स्मृतः) 1. 60. 23; 9. 43. 16; 13. 84. 77; 13. 86. 14, 32). A. Formation of the constellation: When the constellation Abbhijit left her place in the sky and went to the forest to practise austerities there was confusion in the calcula-tion of time; Kṛttikās then went up to the heaven to fill in the gap; there they shine as a constellation, having the form of a cart, with god Fire as their regent (एवम् उक्ते तु शक्रेण त्रिदिवं कृत्तिका गताः । नक्षत्रं शकटाकारं भाति तद् वह्निदैवतम् ॥ ) 3. 219. 11. B. Number: Their number is six 3. 134. 12. C. Rites performed under the Kṛttikās: (1) Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if one satisfied the Brāh-maṇas under the Kṛttikās by feeding them with rice boiled with milk and sprinkled with clarified butter (पायसेन ससर्पिषा) one obtained the highest worlds 13. 63. 5; (2) Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that if one offered a काम्य श्राद्ध regularly under the Kṛttikās that was as good as perform-ing a sacrifice after establishing the fires; such a person was blessed with progeny and was free from affliction (विगतज्वरः) 13. 89. 2; (3) By bathing in Māhāgaṅgā at the conjunction of Mars with the Kṛttikās (महागङ्गाम् उपस्पृश्य कृत्तिकाङ्गारके तथा) and by fasting for a fortnight one was purified and obtained heaven 13. 26. 20; (4) Aṅgiras told Gautama that if one who was well composed went on the Urvaśī-kṛttikāyoga (?) to the Lauhitya तीर्थ and bathed there according to the rites one obtained the fruit of performing the Puṇḍa-rīka sacrifice (उर्वशीकृत्तिकायोगे गत्वा यः सुसमाहितः । लौहित्ये विधिवत् स्नात्वा पुण्डरीकफलं लभेत् ॥ ) 13. 26. 43 (Nī. reads उर्वशीं कृत्तिकायोगे (Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 46) and explains: उर्वशीं उर्वशी-तीर्थं कृत्तिकायोगे कार्तिक्यां पौर्णमा-स्याम्); D. Places named after the Kṛttikās: (1) An आश्रम (आश्रमे कृत्तिका-नां तु); if one, after bathing at this आश्रम and delighting Mahādeva, satisfied the पितृस् he obtained heaven 13. 26. 23; (2) A तीर्थ named jointly after the Kṛttikās and the Maghā (कृत्तिकामघयोश् चैव तीर्थम्); by visiting this तीर्थ one obtained the fruits of Agniṣṭoma and Atirātra sacrifices 3. 82. 46. E. The Kṛttikās and the sword: When Brahmā created the sword as a weapon the day was presided over by the Kṛttikās (कृत्तिकाश् चास्य नक्षत्रम् असेः) 12. 160. 80. F. Relationship with omens: Among the bad omens reported by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra before the war, there was one according to which the fierce ग्रह (i. e. Rāhu) blazed in the Kṛttikās, wiped out their appearance by its lustre and stood like a comet (कृत्तिकासु ग्रहस् तीव्रो नक्षत्रे प्रथमे ज्वलन् । वपूंष्य् अपहरन् भासा धूमकेतुर् इव स्थितः ॥ ) 6. 3. 26 (Nī. who reads कृत्तिकां पीडयंस् तीक्ष्णैः (Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 30) explains: तीक्ष्णैः क्रूरैः कर्मभिर् उपलक्षितो राहुर् इत्य् अर्थः). G. Simile: The king of the Prāgjyotiṣa (Bhagadatta), riding on an elephant, was covered with a parasol decorated with gar-lands of flowers and hence looking like a moon on the full moon night in conjunction with the Kṛttikās (कृत्तिकायोगयुक्तेन पौर्णमास्याम् इवेन्दुना) 7. 19. 18. [See Āgneya]
कौमुद: Kaumuda m.; adj.: Name of the month Kārttika; of the month of Kaumuda. Described as occurring in the autumn season (शारद) 13. 116. 70; Kṛṣṇa set out for Hāstinapura on his peace mission towards the end of the autumn season and at the ad-vent of the winter, in the month of Kaumuda, and under the constellation Revatī (कौमुदे मासि रेवत्यां शरदन्ते हिमागमे) 5. 81. 7; according to Bhīṣma, observance of धर्म consisted in avoiding all kind of meat in the Kaumuda month, especially in the bright fort-night (कौमुदे तु विशेषेण शुक्लपक्षे नराधिप । वर्जयेत् सर्वमांसानि धर्मो ह्य् अत्र विधीयते) 13. 116. 60; Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that many kings in the past like Nābhāga, Ambarīṣa and others (13. 116. 65-70) had given up meat in the (bright) fort-night of the month of Kaumuda (कौमुदं पक्षम्) 13. 116. 64; they gave up meat in the month of Kaumuda and attained heaven 13. 116. 70.
कौमुदी: Kaumudī f.: The full moon day of the Kaumuda month (i. e. of Kārttika). One who gives food on the full moon day of the bright half of the month of Kaumuda gets over difficulties and attains immense happiness after death (कौमुद्यां शुक्ल-पक्षे तु यो ऽन्नदानं करोत्य् उत) 13. 65. 60; also a festival celebrated on that day is called Kaumudī; the demons Sunda and Upa-sunda, when the two received the boon from Pitāmaha, observed it out of time with their friends and fulfilled every desire of the parti-cipant (अकालकौमुदीं चैव चक्रतुः सार्वकामिकीम् । दैत्येन्द्रौ परमप्रीतौ तयोश् चैव सुहृज्जनः) 1. 201. 29.
कनकपर्वत: Kanakaparvata m.: Name of a moun-tain (?) Name of a mountain, or an epithet (mountain of gold) of Meru (मेरौ कनक-पर्वते) 12. 122. 3; (महामेरुः स्वयं कनकपर्वतः) 12. 59. 122; this mountain gave gold to king Vainya 12. 59. 122. [See Meru]
कनखल: Kanakhala1 m. (pl.): Name of a moun-tain range. Loved by sages; the great river Gaṅgā shines there (एते कनखला राजन् ऋषीणां दयिता नगाः । एषा प्रकाशते गङ्गा युधि-ष्ठिर महानदी) 3. 135. 5.

Kanakhala2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near Gaṅgādvāra 3. 88. 18; 13. 26. 12; described as holy (पुण्य) 3. 88. 19; by bathing and fasting there for three nights one gets the fruit of performing an Aśva-medha sacrifice and, freed of sins, goes to heaven 3. 82. 26; (धूतपाप्मा दिवं व्रजेत्) 13. 26. 12 (Acc. to Nī. the तीर्थस् listed in 13. 26. 12 are all on the river Gōdāvarī; for his remark see Kuśāvarta below).
कन्याकूप: Kanyākūpa m.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who bathes in this well becomes famous among gods and shines with fame (देवेषु कीर्तिं लभते यशसा च विराजते) 13. 26. 18.
कन्यातीर्थ: Kanyātīrtha1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the river Sarasvatī 3. 81. 93; one who bathes there secures the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 81. 94.

Kanyātīrtha2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One of the तीर्थस् on the Gomatī 3. 93. 2; described as holy (पुण्य) 3. 93. 2; the Pāṇḍavas after bathing there gave away cows and riches; they repeatedly gave offer-ings to gods and manes and satisfied the Brāhmaṇas 3. 93. 3.
Kanyātīrtha3 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। On the shore of the (southern ?) ocean (तीरे समुद्रस्य); having bathed there, one is freed of all sins 3. 83. 21.
कन्यासंवेद्य: Kanyāsaṃvedya nt.: Name of a तीर्थ, also called Kanyā. Restrained and subsisting on limited food (नियतो नियताशनः), if one visits Kanyā-saṃvedya तीर्थ one gets the worlds of Prajā-pati Manu 3. 82. 117; (the merit of those) who give food and drink at Kanyā तीर्थ becomes inexhaustible—this is what the sages of strict vows have declared (कन्यायां ये प्रयच्छन्ति पानम् अन्नं च भारत । तद् अक्षयम् इति प्राहुर् ऋषयः संशित-व्रताः) 3. 82. 118.
कन्याह्रद: Kanyāhrada m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Aṅgiras had told Gautama that one who lived at Kanyāhrada never went (after death) to the abode of Vaivasvata (Yama) but went to the world of gods 13. 26. 50.
कपिञ्जला: Kapiñjalā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa, its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 25, 13; all the rivers listed here are called mothers of the universe (विश्वस्य मातरः) and very strong (महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35.
कपिलस्य: Kapilasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ; also called Nāgatīrtha. Described as famous among all the worlds (सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतम्); it was sacred to Kapila, the chief of the Nāgas (नाग-राजस्य कपिलस्य) 3. 82. 28; hence also known as Nāgatīrtha 3. 82. 29; by bathing there one obtained the fruit of giving a thousand tawny cows (कपिलानां सहस्रस्य फलम्) 3. 82. 29 (this perhaps explains the name of the तीर्थ). [See Kapilātīrtha]
कपिला: Kapilā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa, its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 27, 13; all the rivers listed here are called mothers of the universe (विश्व-स्य मातरः) and very strong (महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35; listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are proclaimed to be the mothers of sacrificial hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 222. 27: या-वन्तः पावका धिष्ण्याः सन्ति तावन्तः सोमाः सोमयागाः । एतच् च याज्ञिकेष्व् एव प्रसिद्धम्); mentioned also in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 15, 2.
कपिलातीर्थ: Kapilātīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who has observed chastity and has a concentrated mind (ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः), if he bathes in this तीर्थ and worships gods and manes he gets the fruit of giving a thou-sand tawny cows (कपिलानां सहस्रस्य फलम्) 3. 81. 38 (this perhaps explains the name of the तीर्थ). [See Kapilasya tīrtham]
कपिलाह्रद: Kapilāhrada m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in Vārāṇasī; by bathing there and by worshipping Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva) one obtains the fruit of performing a Rājasūya sacrifice 3. 82. 69.
कपिष्ठलस्य: Kapiṣṭhalasya kedāraḥ m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Sacred to the high-souled Kapiṣṭhala 3. 81. 59; described as very difficult of access (सुदुर्लभ) 3. 81. 61; one who is pure and has controlled his mind, if he bathes in the Kedāra of the high-souled Kapiṣṭhala (के-दारे … कपिष्ठलमहात्मनः), his soul is cleansed of all sins, reaches Brahman and goes to the world of Brahman (ब्रह्माणम् अभिगम्याथ शुचिः प्रयतमानसः । सर्व-पापविशुद्धात्मा ब्रह्मलोकं प्रपद्-यते ॥ ) 3. 81. 60; one who reaches this sacred place burns his sins by practising austerities and becomes invisible (कपिष्ठ-लस्य केदारं समासाद्य … अन्तर्धानम् अवाप्नति तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषः) 3. 81. 61.
कपोतक: Kapotaka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing in this तीर्थ and by fasting there for twelve days one obtains the fruit of performing a Naramedha 13. 26. 39 (नर-मेधफलं लभेत्) (situated on the river Sabarmati, Editor's note on the stanza Cr. Ed. Vol. 17, part II, p. 1067).
कम्पना: Kampanā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 24, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be the mothers of the world (विश्वस्य मातरः) and very strong (महा-बलाः) 6. 10. 35; described as frequented by the Siddhas (सिद्धनिषेविता); by visiting it one obtains the fruit of offering a Puṇḍa-rīka sacrifice and goes to the world of Sūrya 3. 82. 99.
कम्पुना: Kampunā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 95; finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 15, 2.
करतोया: Karatoyā f.: Name of a river. Flowing through the Kuraṅga country (करतोयां कुरङ्गेषु) 13. 26. 11; listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhārata-varṣa; its water used for drinking by the people 6. 10. 34, 13; all the rivers listed here are called the mothers of the world (विश्व-स्य मातरः सर्वाः) and very strong (सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35; finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 15, 2; one who is pure and self-controlled and bathes in the river Karatoyā and fasts for three nights obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha by offering worship to Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) (कृते पैतामहे विधौ) 3. 83. 3; 13. 26. 11. [See Karatoyinī]
करतोयिनी: Karatoyinī f.: Name of a river (identi-cal with Karatoyā ?). Those who visit this river, become aus-picious, and wearing heavenly garlands, and rich in holy fragrance they reach there (i. e. the Goloka ? गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44) (तत्र ते दिव्यसंस्थाना दिव्यमाल्यधराः शिवाः । प्रयान्ति पुण्यगन्धाढ्याः) 13. 105. 45, 48 (= Sadānīrā (?), Edititor's note on the stanza, Cr. Ed. Vol. 17, part II, p. 1099). [See Sadānīrā]
करीषिणी: Karīṣiṇī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used for drinking by people 6. 10. 16, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong (विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35.
कर्दमिल: Kardamila nt.: Name of a तीर्थ (?) Situated on the river Madhuvilā Samaṅgā; it was the bathing place of Bharata (? एतत् कर्दमिलं नाम भरतस्याभिषेचनम्) 3. 135. 1.
कलशी: Kalaśī f.: Name of a river. If a person who has controlled his sense organs and has faith (श्रद्दधानो जितेन्-द्रियः) bathes (उपस्पृश्य) in the river Kalaśī he obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 81. 66; by bathing (उपस्पृश्य) there a person becomes one with Brahman (ब्रह्म-भूतो विराजते) 13. 26. 41.
कल्माषी: Kalmāṣī f.: Name of a river (identical with Yamunā ?). Situated near the Gaṅgā; Drupada, in search of priests who would agree to officiate at his sacrifice to obtain a son, while wandering near Kalmāṣī came across a holy settlement of the Brāhmaṇas (अभितः सो ऽथ कल्माषीं गङ्गाकूले परिभ्रमन् । ब्राह्मणावस-थं पुण्यम् आससाद महीपतिः) 1. 155. 5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 167. 5: कल्माषीं कृष्ण-वर्णां यमुनाम् अभितः … । कल्माषपाद्-अस्य कल्माषीम् अभितः समीपे इत्य् अन्ये).
काञ्चनशैल: Kāñcanaśaila m.: Name of a mythical mountain. Situated in the west (5. 108. 1-2), near the coast of the mythical ocean Kāñcanā-mbuvaha; reaching its foot (?), Surabhi yields milk 5. 108. 10 (for citation see Kāñcanā-mbuvaha).
काञ्चनाक्षी: Kāñcanākṣī f.: One of the seven names of Sarasvatī. Described as the best of rivers (सरितां श्रेष्ठा) 9. 37. 18; the sages once assembled at the Naimiṣa forest to perform a सत्र; when they thought of Sarasvatī, the river came to the Naimiṣa forest for the sages and was called Kāñcanākṣī; the river was revered by them (नैमिषे काञ्चनाक्षी तु मुनीनां सत्रयाजिनाम् । आगता सरीतां श्रेष्ठा तत्र भारत पूजिता) 9. 37. 15-18; the seven names of Sarasvatī are given in 9. 37. 4.
काञ्चनाम्बुवह: Kāñcanāmbuvaha m.: Name of a my-thical ocean. Situated in the west (5. 108. 1-2), near the mountain Kāñcanaśaila; after reaching its coast Surabhi pours out milk (अत्र काञ्चन-शैलस्य काञ्चनाम्बुवहस्य च । उदधेस् तीरम् आसाद्य सुरभिः क्षरते पयः) 5. 108. 10.
काम: Kāma nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Sacred to Rudra (कामाख्यं तत्र रुद्रस्य तीर्थम्); it was visited by the divine sages (देवर्षिसेवितम्); by bathing there one obtained सिद्धि quickly (क्षिप्रम्) 3. 80. 113.
काम्यक: Kāmyaka1 nt.: Name of a lake. The Vaṅgas, the Kaliṅga kings, the Tāmraliptas and the Puṇḍrakas gave to Yudhi-ṣṭhira as tribute elephants, having pole-long tusks (ईषादन्तान्), who were gold-girdled (हेमकक्षान्), lotus-coloured (पद्मवर्णान्), covered with painted cloth (कुथावृतान्), huge like mountains (शैलाभान्) and always in rut (नित्यमत्तान्) to gain entry for the Rāja-sūya sacrifice; these elephants hailed from the Kāmyaka lake (अभितः काम्यकं सरः) 2. 48. 19-20, 17.

Kāmyaka2 nt.: Name of a forest, and of the आश्रम of the Pāṇḍavas in this forest (3. 146. 10-11; 3. 162. 12; 3. 244. 15). A. Location: It was to the west, some forests away, of the Yamunā, in the desert plains on the bank of the Sarasvatī (यमु-नां च निषेव्य ते । ययुर् वनेनैव वनं सततं पश्चिमां दिशम् ॥ ततः सरस्वती-कूले समेषु मरुधन्वसु । काम्यकं नाम ददृशुर् वनम्) 3. 6. 2-3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 5. 3: मरुषु निर्जलदेशेषु । धन्वसु जाङ्गलदेशेषु); ययौ सरस्वती-तीरे काम्यकं नाम काननम्) 3. 37. 37; a part of Kurujāṅgala (प्राप्तो ऽस्मि कुरुजाङ्-गलम् । यद्दृच्छया धर्मराजं दृष्टवान् काम्यके वने) 3. 11. 11; famed as the ‘head’ of the desert near the lake Tṛṇabindu (काम्-यकं काननोत्तमम् । मरुभूमेः शिरः ख्यातम् तृणबिन्दुसरः प्रति) 3. 244. 13; it took Pāṇḍavas three days and nights to reach the Kāmyaka forest from Hāstinapura (इतः प्रयाताः … पाण्डवाः । जग्मुस् त्रिभिर् अहोरात्रैः काम्यकं नाम तद् वनं) 3. 12. 3. B.
