Description: Large forest (महावन 3. 248. 3; 3. 13. 1 (not named); 3. 253. 2 (not named); (महत्य् अरण्ये) 3. 253. 9; best forest (काननोत्तम) 3. 244. 13; holy (पुण्यम् आश्रमम्) 3. 244. 15; beautiful (रम्य) 3. 244. 13; prosperous (ऋद्धिमन्त्) 3. 6. 5; with trees in blossom (कुसुमितद्रुम) 3. 79. 13; having many wonders (बह्वाश्चर्य) 3. 79. 13; liked by ascetics (मुनिजनप्रिय) 3. 6. 3; (आश्र-मम् तापसायुतम्) 3. 244. 15; resounding with the sounds of birds (विहगोपघुष्ट) 3. 253. 2; full of many deer (बहुमृग) 3. 244. 13; 3. 248. 1; full of many deer and birds (बहुमृगद्विज) 3. 6. 4; full of deer and beasts of prey (मृगव्यालगणानुकीर्ण) 3. 253. 2; desolate (शून्य) 3. 12. 23. C. Epic events: (1) The Pāṇḍavas lived there intermittently during the term of exile: when स्वस्ति was pronounced on the Pāṇḍavas, they proceeded toward the Kāmyaka forest for their वनवास 3. 4. 10; when Dhṛtarāṣṭra blamed Vidura for siding with the Pāṇḍavas and asked him to leave, if he so desired, he went to the Kāmyaka anxious to meet the Pāṇḍavas there 3. 6. 5; later, Saṃjaya went to the Kāmyaka to bring Vidura back to Hāstinapura 3. 7. 10; from the Kāmyaka the Pāṇḍavas proceeded to the holy lake Dvaitavana (ततस् ते प्रययुः सर्वे … पुण्यं द्वैतवनं सरः) and entered the forest of the same name (पुण्यं द्वैत-वनं रम्यं विविशुर् भरतर्षभाः) 3. 25. 13, 16; 3. 26. 1; 3. 37. 31; from there they returned to the Kāmyaka under instruc-tions of Vyāsa; they were followed by learned Brāmhaṇas; having reached Kāmyaka again the Pāṇḍavas settled down there with their counsellors and followers (ततः काम्यकम् आसाद्य पुनस् ते भरतर्षभाः । न्यविशन्त महात्मानः सामात्याः सपदानुगाः) 3. 37. 31, 37, 39; even after Arjuna left for the Śakraloka to acquire divine weapons, the rest of the Pāṇḍavas continued to live with Draupadī in the Kāmyaka forest 3. 49. 2; 3. 80. 1; after Arjuna's departure from the Kāmyaka to acquire divine weapons (3. 79. 1), the Pāṇḍavas felt dejected 3. 79. 4-7; 3. 161. 15; neither Draupadī (3. 79. 12-14), nor Bhīma (3. 79. 22), nor Nakula (3. 79. 25), nor Sahadeva (3. 79. 29) found the forest as beautiful as before; the divine sage Nārada came there to meet them 3. 80. 2; since the Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī were no longer properly attentive (अवधानं न गच्छामः काम्यके 3. 84. 16) and found no delight in their continued stay in the Kām-yaka in the absence of Arjuna, Yudhiṣṭhira asked Dhaumya to suggest to him some other forest rich in food and fruits 3. 84. 17, 20; before the Pāṇḍavas left for their तीर्थयात्रा, they lived in the Kāmyaka for three nights with the sage Lomaśa 3. 90. 24; when Arjuna had left the Pāṇḍavas to go to the Indraloka, Ghaṭotkaca arrived at the Kāmyaka to help the Pāṇḍavas to proceed to the Gandhamādana mountain; he remained with them till Arjuna's return 7. 158. 28 (a reference to 3. 144. 23-27); Draupadī desired Bhīma to carry the heavenly सौगन्धिक flower to the Kāmyaka आश्रम, since she wanted to present it to Yudhiṣṭhira; she would also take with her other flowers which Bhīma might collect (हरेर् इदं मे कामाय काम्यके पुनर् आश्रमे । … तान्य्-अहं नेतुम् इच्छामि काम्यकं पुनर् आश्रमम्) 3. 146. 10-11; when Arjuna came back to the Pāṇḍavas on the Gandhamādana mountain from the Indraloka in the company of Indra, the latter advised Yudhiṣṭhira to return to the hermitage Kāmyaka (स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि कौन्तेय काम्यकं पुनर् आश्र-मम्) 3. 162. 12; on their way back, they stayed at the Dvaitavana lake on the river Sarasvatī (3. 174. 21) from where they reached the holy Kāmyaka आश्रम full of ascetics (ददृशुः काम्यकं पुण्यम् आश्र-मं तापसायुतम् 3. 244. 15) and the Kām-yaka forest where they settled down again 3. 179. 18; (काम्यकं प्राप्य कौन्तेयाः  … निषेदुः सह कृष्णया) 3. 180. 1; a certain Brāhmaṇa, friend of Arjuna, told the Pāṇḍavas that Kṛṣṇa and the sage Mārkaṇ-ḍeya would come there to visit them 3. 180. 3-6, 39; while the Pāṇḍavas were in the Kāmyaka forest (not named) they completed eleven years of their exile (वने निवसतां तेषां … वर्षान्य् एकादशातीयुः) 3. 245. 1; the Pāṇḍavas lived delightfully in the Kām-yaka which was full of deer 3. 248. 1; Vār-dhakṣatri (Jayadratha), the king of the Sindhus, on his way to the Śālveyas, happened to pass through the Kāmyaka 3. 248. 6-7; when Draupadī was being forcibly carried away by Jayadratha she was confident that she would return to the Kāmyaka to meet her husbands 3. 252. 21; the Pāṇḍavas conti-nued to live in the Kāmyaka after the Jaya-dratha episode 3. 256. 30; it was here that the sage Mārkaṇḍeya narrated to the Pāṇḍa-vas the story of Rāma and of Sāvitrī 3. 283. 16; at the end of the twelfth year (द्वादशे ऽब्दे व्यतीते 3. 294. 41), the Pāṇḍavas, to-gether with the Brāhmaṇas, once again went to the Dvaitavana from the Kāmyaka forest 3. 294. 42-43; 3. 295. 2-3; (2) The Bhojas, the Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas, and many others, under the leadership of Vāsudeva, had gone to the Kāmyaka to meet the Pāṇḍavas 3. 13. 1-4; (3) A demon, Kirmīra by name and brother of Baka, lived there 3. 12. 22; the forest was always avoided from a distance by ascetics and other forest-dwellers due to the fear of man-eating demons (पुरुषादभयात् किल) 3. 12. 4-5. D. Similies: (1) When Arjuna left, the (Kāmyaka) forest was to the Pāṇḍavas like the Caitraratha वन in the absence of Kubera 3. 79. 6; (2) The Pāṇḍavas entered the Kāmyaka as do the righteous the heaven 3. 244. 16; (3) When Draupadī was abducted, Yudhiṣṭhira, noticing certain omens, said that the Kāmyaka appear-ed to him like a lake from where serpents had been taken away, a kingdom without prospe-rity in the absence of a king, or (an empty) jar from which wine had been drunk by drun-kards (सरः सुपर्णेन हृतोरगं यथा राष्ट्रं यथाराजकम् आत्तलक्ष्मि । एवं-विधं मे प्रतिभाति काम्यकं शौण्डैर् यथा पीतरसश् च कुम्भः ॥ ) 3. 253. 5.
कायशोधन: Kāyaśodhana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing there one's body was without doubt purified (शरीरशुद्धिः स्नातस्य तस्-मिंस् तीर्थे न संतयः) 3. 81. 35 (which justifies the name of the तीर्थ).
कारंधम: Kāraṃdhama nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as serene (प्रसन्न) 1. 208. 3; one of the five तीर्थस् on the southern ocean (समुद्रे तीर्थानि दक्षिणे) 1. 208. 1, 3; they were formerly thronged by ascetics but later avoided by them due to the presence of crocodiles there 1. 208. 2, 4-6; by bathing there one obtained the fruit of an Aśvamedha 1. 208. 3. [See Nārītīrtha]
कारपचन: Kārapacana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as best (उत्तम) and the most excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थप्रवर) 9. 53. 11; Balarāmā took bath in its cold water and gave gifts 9. 53. 12; from there he went to the आश्रम of Mitra and Varuṇa on the Yamunā 9. 53. 12-13.
कारापतन: Kārāpatana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as the best (उत्तम) 3. 82. 2; (by bathing there) one got the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and went (after death) to the world of the Munis (मुनिलोकं च गच्छति) 3. 82. 2.
कालकूट: Kālakūṭa m.: Name of a mountain. Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and Bhīma, while pro-ceeding to the Magadha country from the Kuru country, crossed the Kālakūṭa 2. 18. 26; the Kālakūṭa mountain is mentioned among the places overrun by the army of the Kauravas as there was not enough room for it in the Hāstinapura 5. 19. 28, 30.

Kālakūṭa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Living in the north; Arjuna defeated them in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् अजयत् पाकशासनिः) 2. 23. 9; (कालकूटांश् च … विजित्य सः) 2. 23. 14.
कालञ्जर: Kālaṃjara m.: Name of a mountain. A. Description: Famous in the world (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 83. 53; B. तीर्थस् and आश्रमस् on the mountain: (1) There was the holy lake Devahrada on this mountain; by bathing in it one got the fruit of giving the gift of a thousand cows 3. 83. 53; there was also the holy lake Ṣaṣṭihrada; the gift given after bathing in this lake was equalled by no other gift (दानं नान्यद् विशिष्यते) 13. 26. 34; (2) On this mountain there was the excellent आश्रम of Agastya known as Hiraṇyabindu (अगस्त्यस्य च राजेन्द्र तत्राश्रमवरो महान् । हिरण्यबिन्दुः कथितो गिरौ कालंजरे नृप) 3. 85. 15. C. Importance: One who controls one's self on this mountain is glorified in the heaven (आत्मानं साधयेत् तत्र गिरौ कालं-जरे नृप । स्वर्गलोके महीयेत नरो नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः ॥ ) 3. 83. 54. D. Simile: When one gave up all desires and fixed his mind in the सत्त्व quality, one became (like) the mountain Kālaṃjara 12. 238. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 246. 9: सत्त्वे सूक्ष्मायां बुद्धौ चित्तं स्थूलबुद्धिं । कालञ्जर-पर्वतवद् अप्रकम्प्यो भवेत् । कालं क्षणमुहूर्तादिरूपम् जरयति नाशयति तथा आत्मविद् एव कालं नाशयति न तु तं काल इत्य् अर्थः).
कालंजर: Kālaṃjara m.: Name of a mountain. A. Description: Famous in the world (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 83. 53; B. तीर्थस् and आश्रमस् on the mountain: (1) There was the holy lake Devahrada on this mountain; by bathing in it one got the fruit of giving the gift of a thousand cows 3. 83. 53; there was also the holy lake Ṣaṣṭihrada; the gift given after bathing in this lake was equalled by no other gift (दानं नान्यद् विशिष्यते) 13. 26. 34; (2) On this mountain there was the excellent आश्रम of Agastya known as Hiraṇyabindu (अगस्त्यस्य च राजेन्द्र तत्राश्रमवरो महान् । हिरण्यबिन्दुः कथितो गिरौ कालंजरे नृप) 3. 85. 15. C. Importance: One who controls one's self on this mountain is glorified in the heaven (आत्मानं साधयेत् तत्र गिरौ कालं-जरे नृप । स्वर्गलोके महीयेत नरो नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः ॥ ) 3. 83. 54. D. Simile: When one gave up all desires and fixed his mind in the सत्त्व quality, one became (like) the mountain Kālaṃjara 12. 238. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 246. 9: सत्त्वे सूक्ष्मायां बुद्धौ चित्तं स्थूलबुद्धिं । कालञ्जर-पर्वतवद् अप्रकम्प्यो भवेत् । कालं क्षणमुहूर्तादिरूपम् जरयति नाशयति तथा आत्मविद् एव कालं नाशयति न तु तं काल इत्य् अर्थः).
कालतीर्थ: Kālatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the city Kośalā; by bath-ing there (उपस्पृश्य) one got without doubt the fruit of letting loose eleven bulls (वृष-भैकादशफलं लभते नात्र संशयः) 3. 83. 11.
कालपर्वत: Kālaparvata1 m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the Laṅkā; Rāvaṇa crossed Trikūṭa and Kālaparvata before he reached the ocean 3. 261. 53.

Kālaparvata2 m.: Name of a mountain, also called Kālaśaila. Situated in the north; described as having the form of a heap of glistening collyrium (स्निग्धाञ्जनचयाकार); Arjuna crossed it before reaching the foot of the Himālayas 7. 57. 27, 23; Lomaśa pointed out to the Pāṇḍavas that they had crossed Kālaśaila and were about to reach the Śvetagiri 3. 140. 1, 4.
कालाम्र: Kālāmra m.: Name of a tree. Situated to the east of Meru 6. 8. 12; described as tall (महाद्रुम) 6. 8. 13; auspicious (शुभ) and having flowers and fruit all the time (नित्यपुष्पफल) 6. 8. 14; by drinking the juice of the Kālāmra fruit the people of that Dvīpa (Kālāmra ?) stay ever young (कालाम्ररसपीतास् ते नित्यं संस्थितयौवनाः) 6. 8. 17.
कालिकासङ्गम: Kālikāsaṃgama m.: Name of a con-fluence. A self-controlled (यतः) wise man (विद्वान्), having bathed at this confluence of the rivers Kauśikī and Aruṇā (text has Āruṇā म्। च्। ? कालिकासंगमे स्नात्वा कौ-शिक्यारणयोः) and having fasted for three nights, becomes freed of all sins 3. 82. 135.
कालिकासंगम: Kālikāsaṃgama m.: Name of a con-fluence. A self-controlled (यतः) wise man (विद्वान्), having bathed at this confluence of the rivers Kauśikī and Aruṇā (text has Āruṇā म्। च्। ? कालिकासंगमे स्नात्वा कौ-शिक्यारणयोः) and having fasted for three nights, becomes freed of all sins 3. 82. 135.
कालिन्दी: Kālindī f.: Another name of the river Yamunā. The Pāṇḍavas, at the end of their वन-वास, and before proceeding to the Virāṭa-nagara, first went along the southern bank of the river Kālindī (कालिन्दीम् अभितो ययुः । ततस् ते दक्षिणं तीरम् अन्वगच्छन् पदा-तयः) 4. 5. 1-2; Kālindī, in bodily form, along with many other rivers wait upon god Varuṇa in his सभा 2. 9. 18. [See Yamunā]
कालोद: Kāloda nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Śaunaka recommends it, among many others, to king Janamejaya; by visiting the तीर्थ one would again live long in this life (? लब्धायुर्जीविते पुनः) 12. 148. 11.
कावेरका: Kāverakā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers in the Śākadvīpa 6. 12. 30, 26; its water is holy (नद्यः पुण्यजलास् तत्र) 6. 12. 29.
कावेरी: Kāverī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 19, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong (विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35; favourite river of the Apsarases (वृताम् अप्स-रसां गणैः) 3. 83. 20; by bathing there one obtained the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 83. 20; listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are famous as the mothers of the fire-hearths (i. e. sacrifices were performed on the banks of these rivers; for Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 222. 27 see Kapilā; एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24; finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 17, 2.
काष्ठवत्: Kāṣṭhavant m.: Name of a mountain. One of the mountains described as kings of mountains (एते पर्वतराजानः); listed by Brahman for the information of the sages Bṛhaspati and others (14. 35. 15-16) among the principal mountains 14. 43. 4-5; (These mountains also are to be looked upon as having the मध्यम गुण (i. e. the quality रजस्) ? 14. 43. 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 43. 1: मध्यमो गुणः रजोगुणप्रधानः).
काष्ठवन्त्: Kāṣṭhavant m.: Name of a mountain. One of the mountains described as kings of mountains (एते पर्वतराजानः); listed by Brahman for the information of the sages Bṛhaspati and others (14. 35. 15-16) among the principal mountains 14. 43. 4-5; (These mountains also are to be looked upon as having the मध्यम गुण (i. e. the quality रजस्) ? 14. 43. 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 43. 1: मध्यमो गुणः रजोगुणप्रधानः).
किङ्कीणिकाश्रम: Kiṅkīṇikāśrama m.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing there one is able to go any-where at will and is glorified in the heavenly abode of the Apsarases (निवासे ऽप्सरसां दिव्ये कामचारी महीयते) 13. 26. 21.
किंजप्य: Kiṃjapya nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing there (the merit of one's) prayers becomes unlimited (अप्रमेयम् अवा-प्नोति … जप्यं) 3. 81. 65 (this explains the name of the तीर्थ). [See Kiṃdāna]
किंदत्त: Kiṃdatta m.: Name of a sacred well (कूप). Having visited the well and having offered a प्रस्थ of sesame seeds, one is freed of debts and attains the greatest perfection (तिलप्रस्थं प्रदाय च । गच्छेत पर-मां सिद्धिम् ऋणैर् मुक्तः) 3. 81. 83.
किंदान: Kiṃdāna nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Having bathed there one's gifts become unlimited (अप्रमेयम् अवाप्नोति दानं) 3. 81. 65 (this explains the name of the तीर्थ). [See Kiṃjapya]
कुक्षिमन्त्: Kukṣimant m.: Name of a mountain. Situated near the country (?) Unnāṭa; conquered by Bhīma in his expedition before the Rājasūya (उन्नाटम् अभितो जिग्ये कुक्षि-मन्तं च पर्वतम्) 2. 27. 5.
कुचरा: Kucarā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 26, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā) 6. 10. 35.
कुण्डला: Kuṇḍalā f.: Name of a river. Described as holy (पवित्रा) 6. 10. 20; listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 20, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā) 6. 10. 35.
कुण्डोद: Kuṇḍoda m.: Name of a mountain. Pleasing (रम्य); having many roots, fruits and water (बहुमूलफलोदक) 3. 85. 20; thirsty Nala got water and happiness there (नैषधस् तृषितो यत्र जलं शर्म च लब्धवान्) 3. 85. 20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 87. 26 gives the following information: नैषधो नलः तत्रैव लोलार्कदक्षिणे नलग्रामस्य दर्शनात्).
कुबेरनलिनी: Kuberanalinī f.: Name (?) of Kubera's pond. Situated on the Gandhamādana mountain 3. 142. 22; pleasing (रम्या) and guarded by demons (राक्षसैर् अभिरक्षिताम्); the Pāṇḍavas desired to go there on foot (पद्-भिर् एव गमिष्यामः) to meet Arjuna 3. 142. 24.
कुब्जाम्रक: Kubjāmraka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A pilgrim (तीर्थसेवी), by visiting this तीर्थ, obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows and goes to the heaven 3. 82. 36.
कुमारकोटि: Kumārakoṭi f.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who is controlled (नियत) should bathe in this तीर्थ and offer worship to manes and gods (पितृदेवार्चने रतः); he thereby obtains the fruit of performing a Gavāmayana sacrifice and lifts up his family 3. 80. 123.
कुमारधारा: Kumāradhārā f.: Name of a river. A. Source: Flows from the lake Pitā-mahasaras situated on the Śailarāja (Hima-vant) 3. 82. 128-129. B. Description: Purifying the worlds (लोकपावनी); famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता) 3. 82. 129. C. Importance: Bathing there one feels to have achieved the purpose of one's life (यत्र स्नात्वा कृतार्थो ऽस्मीत्य् आत्मानम् अवगच्छति) 3. 82. 130; by eating there only the sixth meal in three days one is freed from the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa (षष्ठकालोपवासेन मुच्यते ब्रह्मह-त्यया) 3. 82. 130.
कुमारिकाणां: Kumārikāṇāṃ tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One can reach there after visiting Bra-hmatuṅga 3. 80. 97; sacred to Śakra (Indra) (शक्रस्य), it is frequented by the Siddhas (सिद्धनिसेवित); by bathing there one quickly attains the world of Śakra 3. 80. 97; (Identical with the next (?) which is situated in the south). [See Kumārī1]
कुमारी: Kumārī1 f. (pl.): Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Situated in the Pāṇḍya country 3. 86. 11. B. Description: They are famous for their holiness (कुमार्यः कथिताः पुण्याः) 3. 86. 11. C. Import-ance: One who bathes in Kokāmukha, visits Caṇḍālikāśrama and observes other व्रतस् gets the merit of having bathed in the Kumārī तीर्थ ten times (?) (कुमारीर् विन्दते दश) 13. 26. 49. [See Kumārikāṇāṃ tīrtham]

Kumārī2 f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 34, 13; all these rivers are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā) 6. 10. 35.
Kumārī3 f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Śākadvīpa; water of these rivers is holy (नद्यः पुण्य-जलास् तत्र) 6. 12, 30, 29, 26.
कुरुक्षेत्र: Kurukṣetra nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Description: Holy (पुण्यम् आहुः कुरुक्षेत्रम्) 3. 81. 125; (पुण्य) 3. 81. 177; 12. 148. 10; very holy (महापुण्य) 3. 81. 4; full of holy तीर्थस् (पुण्यतीर्थैश् च कलिलम्) 13. 151. 19; praised (अभिष्टुत) 3. 81. 1; resorted to by brahmanical sages (ब्रह्मर्षिसेवित) 3. 81. 177; called ब्रह्-मक्षेत्र 3. 81. 4; altar of Brahman (ब्र-ह्मवेदी) 3. 81. 177. B. Importance: (1) Kurukṣetra is distinguished in all the three worlds (त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानां कुरु-क्षेत्रं विशिष्यते) 3. 81. 173; (2) Brah-man and other gods, the sages, the Siddhas, the Cāraṇas, the Gandharvas and the Apsa-rases, the Yakṣas and the mythical serpents (Uragas) visit Kurukṣetra 3. 81. 3-4; (3) Pulastya told Bhīṣma that one should live at Kurukṣetra for a month 3. 81. 3; those who live in Kurukṣetra are not reduced to a lamentable condition in any way (न ते शोच्याः कथंचन) 3. 81. 177; all crea-tures who repair there are released from their sins 3. 81. 1; one who always simply says, ‘I shall visit Kurukṣetra, I shall live in Kurukṣetra’ (कुरुक्षेत्रं गमिष्यामि कुरुक्षेत्रे वसाम्य् अहम्), even he is freed of all sins 3. 81. 2; one who says this just once is freed of all sins (अप्य् एकां वाचम् उत्सृज्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते) 3. 81. 176; one who mentally longs (मनसाप्य् अभिकामस्य) for Kurukṣetra, his sins are destroyed and he goes to the world of Brah-man 3. 81. 5; one who visits Kurukṣetra with faith (श्रद्धया) obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha and a Vājapeya 3. 81. 6; if one bathes in Kurukṣetra or drinks its water he will never (?) have an occasion to repent a premature death (यत्रावगाह्य पीत्वा वा नैवं श्वोमरणं तपेत्) 12. 148. 10; (4) There are many holy places in the vicinity of Kurukṣetra 3. 81. 8-20; a pilgrim (तीर्थसेवी) should make a round of these holy places (प्रदक्षिणम् उपावृत्य) 3. 81. 20; the तीर्थ is mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 19, 2. [See Samantapañcaka and Kurukṣetra in 1. 5 A]

Kurukṣetra (nt.): The country of the Kurus; also part of it where the great battle was fought; also called Kurukṣetra-samantapañcaka. A. Location: Close to the river Sarasvatī (अभ्यगच्छत् ततो रामः … कुरुक्षेत्रं … न्यविशन्त ततः सर्वे परि-गृह्य सरस्वतीम्) 5. 177. 23-24; (ततो गच्छेत … कुरुक्षेत्रम् … तत्र मासं वसेद् वीर सरस्वत्याम्) 3. 81. 1, 3; not far from Gaṅgā—Rāma wanted the river Gaṅgā to see Bhīṣma killed by him at Kurukṣetra (अयं गच्छामि कौरव्य कुरुक्षेत्रं त्वया सह । … तत्र त्वां निहतं माता … जाह्नवी पश्यतां भीष्म) 5. 179. 2-3; along the river Ikṣumatī (कुरुक्षेत्रे निवसतां नदीम् इक्षुमतीम् अनु) 1. 3. 145; near the river Hiraṇvatī (आसाद्य सरितं पुण्यां कुरुक्षेत्रे हिरण्-वतीम्) 5. 149. 73; (युद्धं कुरुक्षेत्रे बभूव ह । … नद्यास् तीरे हिरण्वत्याः) 1. 95. 7-8; the boundaries of Kurukṣetra were marked by Tarantuka, Arantuka, the (five) lakes of Rāma and Macakruka— this whole area was called Kurukṣetra-samantapañcaka (also called Brahmavedi, Uttaravedi of Pitāmaha, Uttaravedi of Prajāpati) (ब्रह्मवेदी कुरुक्षेत्रं … तरन्तुकारुन्तकयोर् यद् अन्तरं राम-ह्रदानां च मचक्रुकस्य । एतत् कुरु-क्षेत्रसमन्तपञ्चकं पितामहस्योत्तर-वेदिर् उच्यते) 3. 81. 177-178; 9. 52. 20 (प्रजापतेर् उत्तरवेदिर् उच्यते); the five lakes of Rāma could be seen from a dis-tance while reaching Kurukṣetra from Hāstinapura (कुरुक्षेत्रं … गच्छन्न् एव  … अमी रामह्रदाः पञ्च दृश्यन्ते पार्थ दूरतः) 12. 48. 6-8; Muñjavaṭa तीर्थ, sacred to Mahādeva, was the famous gate of Kurukṣetra (मुञ्जवटम् … कुरुक्षेत्र-स्य तद् द्वारं विश्रुतम्) 3. 81. 18, 20; the Plakṣāvataraṇa तीर्थ on Yamunā river was also called the gate of Kurukṣetra (द्वारम् एतद् धि कौन्तेय कुरुक्षेत्रस्य … । एतत् प्लक्षावतरणं यमुनातीर्थम् उच्यते) 3. 129. 11, 13; Naimiṣeya कुञ्ज was located in Kurukṣetra (एवं स कुञ्जो राजेन्द्र नैमिषेय इति स्मृतः । कुरुक्षेत्रे) 9. 36. 54; the Bāhlīka country lay outside Kuru-kṣetra (बहिष्कृता … कुरुक्षेत्रेण चापि ये ।  … तान् … बाह्लीकान्) 8. 30. 10-11. B. Name and history: The great royal sage Kuru ploughed the Kuru land for many years, hence called Kurukṣetra (पुरा च राजर्षि-वरेण … बहूनि वर्षाण्य् … । प्रकृष्टम् एतत् कुरुणा … । ततः कुरुक्षेत्रम् इतीह पप्रथे ॥ ) 9. 52. 2 (Rāma asked the sages why Kuru ploughed the land; the sages told him the reason 9. 52. 3 ff.); the place known after the pious Kuru, son of Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī (ततः संवरणात् सौरी सुषुवे तपती कुरुम् । … तस्य नाम्ना-भिविख्यातं पृथिव्यां कुरुजाङ्गलम् । कुरुक्षेत्रम्) 1. 89. 42-43. C. Descrip-tion: very famous (अभिविख्यात) 1. 89. 43; pleasing (रमणीय) 9. 22. 23; holy (पुण्य) 9. 22. 23; very holy (महत्पुण्य) 9. 52. 21; most holy in the three worlds (पुण्यतमे त्रैलोक्यस्यापि) 5. 139. 53 (also see the next section D); auspicious (शिव) 9. 52. 21; place suitable for austerities (तपःक्षेत्र) 6. 1. 2; honoured by gods (दिवौकसां सुसंमतम्) 9. 52. 21; place where people practise धर्म (धर्मक्षेत्र) 6. 23. 1; 14. 93. 2; chosen by many who were conversant with धर्म (धर्मज्ञैर् भहुभिर् वृते) 14. 93. 2; place of the whole धर्म (क्षेत्रम् धर्मस्य कृत्स्नस्य) 12. 53. 23; having heavenly qualities (स्वर्गगुणैः समन्-वितम्) 9. 52. 21; battlefield (रणक्षेत्र) 5. 179. 15; (after the war) full of hair, marrow, and bones (केशमज्जास्थिसं-कुल) 12. 48. 3 (also stanzas 4-6). D. Holy: King, Kuru made the place holy by his austerities (कुरुक्षेत्रं स तपसा पुण्यं चक्रे) 1. 89. 43; it was desirable for the Kṣatriyas to get killed by weapons on Kurukṣetra (शस्त्रेण निधनं गच्छेत् समृद्धं क्षत्रमण्डलम् । कुरुक्षेत्रे पुण्यतमे) 5. 139. 53; all kings killed here would obtain the condition of the high-souled ones 9. 52. 21; fruit obtained by people by visiting Kurukṣetra (कुरुक्षेत्र-स्य यत् फलम्) 9. 51. 25-26; Śakra him-self sang a गाथा in praise of the holi-ness of Kurukṣetra: even the dust parti-cles carried by wind were capable of leading a sinner to the highest condition (पांसवो ऽपि कुरुक्षेत्राद् वायुना समुद्-ईरिताः । अपि दुष्कृतकर्माणं नयन्ति पर-मां गतिम्) 9. 52. 18; chief gods (सुर-र्षभाः) and excellent Brāhmaṇas, simi-larly great kings like Nṛga and others obtained good condition after death by offering costly sacrifices at Kurukṣetra 9. 52. 19. E. Epic events: (1) Takṣaka and his son Aśvasena used to live in Kurukṣetra 1. 3. 144-145; 1. 218. 4; 1. 219. 13; (2) Citrāṅgada and the Gandharva king of the same name fought a battle at Kurukṣetra on the river Hiraṇvatī for three years 1. 95. 7; (3) When Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura were born, the Kurus, Kurukṣetra and Kurujāṅgala pros-pered 1. 102. 1 (the way they prospered described in stanzas 2-14); (4) The Pāṇḍavas, at the start of their life in the forest, proceeded towards Kurukṣetra from the bank of Gaṅgā (प्रययुर् जाह्नवीकूलात् कुरुक्षेत्रम्) 3. 6. 1; (5) Before going to Virāṭa, Yudhiṣṭhira unstrung his bow with which he formerly protected Kurukṣetra 4. 5. 18; (6) Duryodhana asked the kings to proceed towards Kuru-kṣetra under the Puṣya nakṣatra (प्रया-ध्वं वै कुरुक्षेत्रं पुष्यो ऽद्येति); accordingly the kings started for Kuru-kṣetra 5. 148. 3, 18; he also asked them to establish camps at Kurukṣetra 5, 150. 14; Duryodhana himself with his brothers, led by Bhīṣma, went to Kuru-kṣetra with his large army; he made a round of Kurukṣetra with Karṇa and measured on level ground the land required for his camp (कुरुक्षेत्रं जगाम ह । … परिक्रम्य कुरुक्षेत्रं कर्णेन सह … । शिबिरं मापयाम् आस समे देशे) 5. 153. 33-34; he and his allies got ready for the war on the western half of Kurukṣetra (कुरु-क्षेत्रस्य पश्चार्धे) 5. 196. 11 (should this be कुरुक्षेत्रस्य पूर्वार्धे ? see 6. 1. 5* and the editor's note on 6. 1. 5 (p. 755)); (7) The Pāṇḍavas too reached Kurukṣetra; reaching there, they blew their conches; there, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Sātyaki measured the land for raising the camp of the Pāṇḍavas (शिबिरं मापयाम् आस धृष्ट-द्युम्नश् च … । सात्यकिश् च); Kṛṣṇa ordered the digging of a ditch at Kurukṣetra for the protection of the camp (खानयाम् आस परिखां केशवस् तत्र … । गुप्त्यर्-थम्) 5. 149. 63-64; 72-74; the place of the camp of Pāṇḍavas described in 5. 149. 67-69; (the camp of Pāṇḍavas was outside the Samantapañcaka 6. 1. 6); Pāṇḍavas were encamped on the western side (of the Kurukṣetra) and faced east (प्राङ्मुखाः पश्चिमे भागे) 6. 1. 5; (8) The two armies were arrayed against each other at Kurukṣetra (तथा व्यूढेष्व् अनी-केषु कुरुक्षेत्रे) 5. 156. 1; (9) Duryo-dhana informed Yudhiṣṭhira through Ulūka that Kurukṣetra was free from mud and that the road to it was even (कुरुक्षेत्रम् अकर्दमम् । समः पन्था … ) 5. 157. 18; 5. 158. 11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 160. 93: अकर्दमम् इति युद्धयोग्यत्वं भूमेर् उक्तम्); (10) Rāma (Bhārgava) took Ambā to Kurukṣetra (to meet Bhīṣma) 5. 177. 23; (11) Bhīṣma agreed to fight with Rāma at Kurukṣetra and asked him to return there (कुरुक्षेत्रे योत्स्ये) 5. 178. 31; (विनिवर्तस्व कुरुक्षेत्रम्) 5. 178. 33; Rāma agreed to return to Kurukṣetra and he went there (अयं गच्छामि कौरव्य कुरुक्षेत्रम्) 5. 179. 2; (ययौ रमः कुरुक्षेत्रम्) 5. 179. 8; later, Bhīṣma too reached Kurukṣetra from Hāstinapura (निष्क्रम्य गजसाह्वयात् । कुरुक्षेत्रम् उपायाम्) 5. 179. 15, 17; (apparently the earlier meeting between Rāma and Bhīṣma did not take place at Kurukṣetra but on the outskirts of Hāstinapura); the fight between Bhīṣma and Rāma at Kurukṣetra referred to in 12. 27. 8; 13. 154. 25; (12) Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas were encamped at Kurukṣetra and were eager to fight 6. 1. 2-3, 23; (13) Vaiśaṃpāyana began the narration of what the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas did at Kurukṣetra as was done earlier by Saṃjaya 6. 1. 2; 6. 23. 1; (14) After the death of Śalya, the Kṣatriyas, in spite of bad omens, were ready to fight at Kurukṣetra desirous of reaching the heaven (if killed in war) (कुरुक्षेत्रे … स्वर्-गं यियांसवः) 9. 22. 23; (15) Bala-rāma in his तीर्थयात्रा went to Kuru-kṣetra 9. 34. 32; (16) From Kurukṣetra he went to the आश्रम where formerly Viṣṇu practised austerities 9. 53. 1, 5; (17) On reaching Kurukṣetra, the Kuru women saw their near relatives lying dead 11. 16. 11; (18) Kṛṣṇa, along with the Pāṇḍavas, went to Kurukṣetra to meet Bhīṣma lying on the bed of arrows 12. 48. 2-3, 6; 12. 53. 23; 12. 57. 2; (19) When Uttarāyaṇa set in, Yudhiṣṭhira, with Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and others, went from Hāstinapura to Bhīṣma lying at Kurukṣetra 13. 153. 12; (20) Dhṛtarāṣṭra first went to Kurukṣetra from the river Bhāgīrathī where there was the आश्रम of Śatayūpa 15. 25. 8-9; (21) Yudhiṣṭhira and others started for the आश्रम of Dhṛtarāṣṭra which was at Kuru-kṣetra (कुरुक्षेत्राश्रमं प्रति) 15. 29. 21; he reached Kurukṣetra after crossing the river Yamunā (कुरुक्षेत्रम् अवातरत् । क्रमेणोत्तीर्य यमुनाम्) 15. 30. 16; (22) The great sages, Śatayūpa and others, living at Kurukṣetra arrived to meet Dhṛta-rāṣṭra and the Pāṇḍavas (शतयूपप्रभृ-तयः कुरुक्षेत्रनिवासिनः) 15. 34. 21; (23) Vyāsa told Gāndhārī that Gandhar-vas, Apsarases, and the rest, born as human beings, met their death at Kuru-kṣetra (गन्धर्वाप्ररसश् चैव त … एते निधनं प्राप्ताः कुरुक्षेत्रे) 15. 39. 6-7; (24) Dhṛtarāṣṭra went from Kuru-kṣetra to Gaṅgādvāra (where he was reduced to ashes by forest fire) (कुरु-क्षेत्रात् पिता तुभ्यं गङ्गाद्वारं ययौ) 15. 45. 10; (25) Arjuna arrived at Kuru-kṣetra from Dvārakā after he was attacked by Dasyus on his way 16. 8. 85. F. Past events: (1) Viṣṇu once told Pṛthivī that the kings who would gather at Kurukṣetra would kill each other (कुरुक्षेत्रे समा-गताः । अन्योन्यं घातयिष्यन्ति) 11. 8. 25; (2) Janamejaya, son of Parikṣit, with his brothers performed a long sacrificial session at Kurukṣetra (जनमेजयः पारि-क्षितः सह भ्रातृभिः कुरुक्षेत्रे दीर्घ-सत्रम् उपास्ते) 1. 3. 1; (3) The place where king Māndhātṛ offered sacrifices was situated in the middle of Kurukṣetra (तस्यैतद् देवयजनं … कुरुक्षेत्रस्य मध्यतः) 3. 126. 42; (4) Sudarśana, with his wife Oghavatī, decided to lead the life of a householder at Kurukṣetra 13. 2. 39; (5) When king Kuru offered a sacrifice at Kurukṣetra, Sarasvatī appeared at Ṛṣabha-dvīpa as Suveṇu (सुवेणुर् ऋषभद्वीपे … कुरोश् च यजमानस्य कुरुक्षेत्रे … आज-गाम … सरस्वती) 9. 37. 24; (6) When Vasiṣṭha invited her at Kurukṣetra, Sara-svatī appeared there as Oghavatī (ओघवत्य् अपि … वसिष्ठेन … । समाहूता कुरुक्षेत्रे … सरस्वती) 9. 37. 25; (7) When the sages of the Nimiṣa forest decided to go on a pilgrimage, they went to Kurukṣetra 3. 81. 92; (8) In the Kṛtayuga (9. 36. 39), when the ascetics from the Nimiṣa forest went to Kurukṣetra, they found no place there as it was already full of sages (ते ऽवकाशं न ददृशुः कुरुक्षेत्रे) 9. 36. 48; (9) Pious Mudgala, who lived only by gleaning ears of corn, lived at Kurukṣetra (शिलोञ्छवृत्तिर् धर्मात्मा मुद्गलः … । आसीद् … कुरुक्षेत्रे) 3. 246. 3; (10) A cer-tain noble Brāhmaṇa (name not mention-ed), who lived the life of a pigeon by gleaning ears of corn, lived at Kuru-kṣetra (उञ्छवृत्तेर् वदान्यस्य कुरुक्षेत्र-निवासिनः) 14. 92. 9, 19, 21; (कुरुक्षेत्रे … । उञ्छवृत्तिर् द्विजः कश्चित् कापोतिर् अभवत् पुरा) 14. 93. 2; (11) Sunda and Upa-sunda, after conquering the whole earth, settled down at Kurukṣetra (निःसपत्नौ कुरुक्षेत्रे निवेशम् अभिचक्रतुः) 1. 202. 27 [See Kurukṣetra (holy place) Vol. 1. 5. pp. 312-313 and Kurujāṅgala (below)].
कुरुक्षेत्रस्य: Kurukṣetrasya dvāram nt.: Gate or entrance of the Kurukṣetra. Among the holy places near about Kuru-kṣetra, the place where the world-famous Yakṣī stands is known as the Gate of Kuru-kṣetra (तत्रैव च महाराज यक्षी लोक-परिश्रुता । … कुरुक्षेत्रस्य तद् द्वारं विश्रुतं भरतर्षभ) 3. 81. 19-20.
कुरुतीर्थ: Kurutīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated to the east of the Aujasa तीर्थ; by bathing there, one who observes chastity and has controlled his senses (ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः) is cleansed of all sins and obtains Kuruloka (the world obtained by the Kurus ?) (कुरुलोकं प्रपद्यते; v. l. ब्रह्म-, रुद्र-, देव- for कुरु-) 3. 81. 144.
कुलंपुन: Kulaṃpuna nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing there one purifies one's family (पुनाति स्वकुलं नरः) 3. 81. 88 (this explains the name of the तीर्थ).
कुल्या: Kulyā f.: Name of a river. By bathing there, by repeating the अघ-मर्षण prayer (ṚV. 10. 190) and by fast-ing for three nights a person becomes pure (शुचिः) and gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha 13. 26. 53.
कुशधारा: Kuśadhārā f.: Name of a river. Described as a great river (महानदी); listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6, 10. 23, 13; all the rivers listed here are called mothers of the universe and very strong (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
कुशप्लवन: Kuśaplavana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who practises chastity and is com-posed (ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः), if he bathes in this तीर्थ and lives there for three nights, he gets the reward of an Aśvamedha 3. 83. 33.
कुशवत्: Kuśavant m.: Name (?) of a lake. On the mountain Himavant there is the lake Kuśavant (or a lake full of कुश grass ?) (ह्रदश् च कुशवान् एषः) where are found lotuses of the water-lily type (यत्र पद्मं कुशेशयम्) 3. 130. 15.
कुशवन्त्: Kuśavant m.: Name (?) of a lake. On the mountain Himavant there is the lake Kuśavant (or a lake full of कुश grass ?) (ह्रदश् च कुशवान् एषः) where are found lotuses of the water-lily type (यत्र पद्मं कुशेशयम्) 3. 130. 15.
कुशस्तम्ब: Kuśastamba m.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who bathes there is waited upon by a host of Apsarases 13. 26. 26.
कुशावर्त: Kuśāvarta m.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing there one's sins are destroyed and one goes to heaven 13. 26. 12 (Accord-ing to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 13 the तीर्थस् listed in the stanza are the ones on the river Godāvarī on the Brahmagiri; for his remark see Gaṅgādvāra).
कुशेशय: Kuśeśaya1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। If a person, having controlled his mind, does obeisance to Kuśeśaya and bathes there his sin is cleansed and he (obtains ?) god-hood (विक्षोभ्य प्रयतश् चाभिवाद्य तम् । कुशेशयं च देवत्वं पूयते तस्य किल्-बिषम् ॥ ) 13. 26. 10.

Kuśeśaya2 m.: Name of a mountain. Name of the fifth among the six moun-tains in the Kuśadvīpa 6. 13. 10, 6, 9; all these mountains are said to be excellent (पर्वतोत्तमाः); the distance between them doubles as one moves from one to the other (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रवि-भागशः) 6. 13. 11.
कूप: Kūpa1 m.: A sacred well, not named, in the Gaṅgā. Situated near the Gaṅgāhrada; there are three crores of तीर्थस् in that well (तिस्रः कोट्यस् तु तीर्थानां तस्मिन् कूपे); by bathing there one goes to heaven 3. 81. 153. [See Udapāna and Kūpa2]

Kūpa2 m.: A sacred well, not named. It is near the sacred place called Jyeṣṭha-sthāna 3. 83. 59-60; described as famous (विश्रुत) 3. 83. 60; all the four oceans are present in this Kūpa; by bathing there (उपस्पृश्य) and by circumambulating it (कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्), a person who has controlled his self (नियतात्मा) is purified and acquires the highest state (after death) (परमां गतिम्) 3. 83. 61. [See Udapāna and Kūpa1]
कृतशौच: Kṛtaśauca nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A pilgrim (तीर्थसेवी), by reaching this तीर्थ, will have purified himself (कृतशौचो भवेन् नरः—which explains the name of the तीर्थ); he will also obtain the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice 3. 81. 17.
कृत्तिकाङ्गारक: Kṛttikāṅgāraka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ (? or of the conjunction of Kṛttikā and Aṅgā-raka). By bathing at this तीर्थ and by fasting there for a fortnight one is purified and goes to heaven (महागङ्गाम् उपस्पृश्य कृत्तिकाङ्-गारके तथा) 13. 26. 20.
कृत्तिकामघयोस्: Kṛttikāmaghayos tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting this तीर्थ, one gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and an Atirātra sacrifice 3. 82. 46.
कृत्या: Kṛtyā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used for drinking by people 6. 10. 17, 13; all the rivers listed here are called mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Ati-kṛṣṇā).
कृष्णवेण्णा: Kṛṣṇaveṇṇā, Kṛṣṇaveṇā f.: Name of a river. The holy lake Devahrada is formed in the Kṛṣṇaveṇṇā (देवह्रदे रम्ये कृष्ण-वेण्णाजलोद्भवे) 3. 83. 34; the sage Mār-kaṇḍeya, while moving in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 i. e. Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3), saw, among other rivers, Kṛṣṇaveṇā 3. 186. 95; listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa (twice, once as Kṛṣṇaveṇā and again as Kṛṣṇaveṇṇā) 6. 10. 15 (निम्नगा), 27; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 13; all the rivers listed here are called mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); men-tioned among the rivers who, along with other watery places, in bodily form (देह-वन्तः 2. 9. 21), wait upod god Varuṇa in his Sabhā 2. 9. 17, 20; listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are known as mothers of the fire-hearths (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्याणां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24 (i. e. Soma sacrifices were performed on their banks; for Nī.'s remark on Bom. Ed. 3. 222. 27 see Kapilā above); finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 17 (अद्रिजा), 2.
कृष्णा: Kṛṣṇā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are famous as mothers of the sacrificial hearths i. e. on the banks of which Soma sacrifices were performed (धिष्ण्यानां मा-तरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24 (for Nī. comm. on Bom. Ed. 3. 222. 27 see Kapilā above).
केतुमाला: Ketumālā f.: Name of a river. Mentioned by Dhaumya among the holy and purifying places of the west 3. 87. 12, 1 (यानि तत्र पवित्राणि पुण्यान्य् आयतनानि च); described as most holy (पुण्यतमा), always frequented by ascetics (सततं ताप-सायुता) 3. 87. 12.
केसर: Kesara, Kesarin m.: Name of a moun-tain. It is the seventh of the seven mountains of the Śākadvīpa 6. 12. 21, 13; the distance in योजनस् between these mountains doubles as one moves from one to the other (तेषां योजनविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 12. 22; the wind blowing from it is laden with filaments of flowers (केसरयुतो यतो वातः प्रवायति) 6. 12. 21 (which explains the name of the mountain); the Modākin Varṣa belongs to the mountain Kesara (केस-रस्य तु मोदाकी) 6. 12. 24.
कैलास: Kailāsa m.: Name of a mountain, once identified with Hemakūṭa (6. 7. 39). A. Situation: Situated in the north 3. 145. 15; part of Himavant 13. 20. 2, 6; 5. 109. 1, 8; 2. 48. 6; beyond the Uttara Kurus 3. 145. 15; mountain Maināka lay to its north 2. 3. 2, 8; 6. 7. 40. B. Extent: It is six hundred योजनस् in extent (कैलासः पर्वतो राजन् षड् योजनशतान्य् उत) 3. 140. 10. C. Description: Very big (सु-महन्त्) 6. 7. 40; (महागिरि) 14. 76. 16; (महाशैल) 13. 20. 29; excellent, best mountain (पर्वतश्रेष्ठ) 3. 108. 15; (पर्-वतोत्तम) 3. 145. 15; has splendid forests (शुभकानन) 3. 151. 1; shining with clouds (? वारिधरप्रकाश) 3. 174. 2; loved by Kubera (कुबेरकान्त) 3. 174. 2; of unima-ginable form (अचिन्त्यरूप) 3. 174. 6; having various wonders (विविधाश्चर्य) 3. 145. 15; having many caves (बहुकन्दर) 3. 141. 15; its peaks are lovely (रम्य) 3. 151. 1; 13. 82. 27; visited by gods and Gandharvas (देवगन्धर्वसेवित) 13. 82. 27; most in accessible (दुर्गतम) 3. 140. 15; (दुर्-गम) 3. 140. 8, 10; (दुर्गेषु विषमेषु) 3. 141. 11; one cannot reach there driving in chariots (अशक्यो रथैर् गन्तुम्) 3. 141. 15; there were invisible and strong Bhūtas and Rākṣasas and hence one could reach there with the help of fire (by worshipping fire ?) and by practising austerities (अन्तर्हितानि भूतानि रक्षांसि बलवन्ति च । अग्निना तपसा चैव शक्यं गन्तुं वृकोदर) 3. 141. 1; house of powerful herbs 2. 48. 6 (see D (1) (ii) below); Kailāsa and other mountains described 3. 140. 4-11; 3. 141. 11. D. Events: (1) Epic: (i) Since the mountain was not easy to reach, Yudhiṣṭhira suggested that all, except him-self, Lomaśa and Nakula, might return to Gaṅgādvāra and wait there 3. 141. 1-7; however, they all proceeded with the help of Ghaṭotkaca and his Rākṣasas; the Pāṇḍavas were delighted to see the Kailāsa on their way to the Śveta and the Gandha-mādana 3. 145. 15, and again on their return 3. 174. 2; they saw the Kailāsa along with the Maināka, the Meru, and the slopes of the Gandhamādana 3. 155. 14; while returning from the Kailāsa the Pāṇḍavas went to the आश्रम of Vṛṣaparvan 3. 174. 6; the Kro-dhavaśa Rākṣasas who were guarding the Pond of Kubera, when routed by Bhīma, fled through the sky towards the peaks of Kailāsa 3. 152. 20; while on the Kailāsa, Bhīma had challenged the friend of Maheśvara (i. e. Ku-bera) with his mace 9. 10. 48; (ii) Power-ful herbs from the Kailāsa in the north were brought as tribute by the Pārvatīyas when they came to attend the Rājasūya of Yudhi-ṣṭhira (उत्तराद् अपि कैलासाद् ओषधीः सु-महाबलाः) 2. 48. 6; (2) Past and My-thological: (i) King Sagara, with his two wives, resorted to the Kailāsa for practising austerities since he desired to have a son 3. 104. 9; (ii) Bhagīratha went to the Kailāsa and propitiated Śiva 3. 107. 24; (iii) Śiva went to the Kailāsa after holding Gaṅgā on his head 3. 108. 15; (iv) Vasiṣṭha brought Gaṅgā, flowing towards the Kailāsa, to the (Mānasa 13. 140. 16) lake; the banks of the lake were shattered by Gaṅgā; 13. 140. 23; Gaṅgā then became Sarayū (सरो भिन्नं तया नद्या सरयूः सा ततो ऽभवत्) 13. 140. 24; (v) Divine Surabhi, the daughter of Dakṣa, practised austerities on the peak of the Kailāsa 13. 82. 27; (vi) Aṣṭāvakra moved around the Kailāsa after reaching the Himavant (कैलासम् अभितो ययौ) 13. 20. 2, 6; when Aṣṭāvakra left the residence of Kubera he went further north and crossed the mountains Kailāsa, Mandara and Haima before reaching the Kairātasthāna 13. 20. 28-29; (vii) Nahuṣa, as the king of gods (देवराज 5. 11. 10), enjoyed the company of the Apsarases and the Devakanyās on the mountains Kailāsa, Himavatpṛṣṭha, Mandara, Śveta and others 5. 11. 9; (viii) Bhara-dvāja asked the great sage Bhṛgu seated on the peak of the Kailāsa: “Who created the world ?” 12. 175. 6; (ix) Rising from the peak of the Kailāsa (कैलासपृष्ठाद् उत्-पत्य) Śuka, the son of Vyāsa, soared to the heaven moving through the mid-region (अन्त-रिक्षचरः) 12. 319. 10. E. Importance: (1) Śiva lives on its peak (कैलासशिखरा-वासिन् is one of the 1000 names of Śiva) 13. 17. 106; (2) Dhanada (Kubera) was conse-crated on the Kailāsa as the chief of the Rā-kṣasas, the Yakṣas and the Gandharvas (आधि-पत्येन कैलासे धनदो ऽप्य् अभिषेचितः) 5. 109. 8; hence Kailāsa is known to be the residence (स्थानम्) of Ailavila (Kubera) 5. 109. 18; 12. 44. 13; Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera) is called कैलासनिलय 12. 274. 9; 3. 42. 31 (Dhanādhyakṣa = Kubera); 2. 6. 11 (Ku-bera); King Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera) enjoys himself on the Kailāsa in the company of the Guhyakas 6. 7. 39; there are innumerable Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Kinnaras, Nāgas, Suparṇas and Gandharvas in the residence of Kubera (कुबेरसदनं प्रति) (on the Kailāsa) 3. 140. 11; there is the beautiful pond (नलिनी), full of Saugandhika flowers, on the peak of the Kailāsa near the abode of Kubera 3. 151. 1, 2; (3) Kailāsa visited by gods (यत्र देवाः समायान्ति) 3. 140. 10; (4) There is the Viśālā (Badarī) tree there 3. 140. 10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 139. 11: विशाला बदरी; also cf. विशालां बदरीं प्रति 3. 145. 10, 18); (5) The आश्रम of Nara and Nārāyaṇa stands in its vicinity (तस्याभ्याशे) 3. 145. 16. F. Figures in bad omens: (1) Among the bad omens noticed by Vyāsa before the start of the war, there was one according to which hundreds of summits of the mountains Kailāsa, Mandara and Hima-vant fell down with great thunder 6. 3. 35; (2) When the Sindhu heroes encircled Arjuna there occurred bad omens one of which was that the Kailāsa experienced trembling (वे-पथुश् चाभवन् राजन् कैलासस्य) 14. 76. 16. G. Similes: (1) Persons: (i) Bala-rāma who was wearing a blue silk garment (नीलकौशेयवसनः) is compared with the summit of the Kailāsa 5. 154. 18; 1. 212. 20; 7. 10. 31; (ii) Bhīmasena with his raised गदा looked like the Kailāsa with its (raised) summit (कैलासम् इव शृङ्गिणम्) 6. 58. 30; 6. 90. 22; (iii) Duryodhana with his raised गदा is similarly compared 9. 32. 36; 9. 55. 27; (iv) Śalya, with the सर्वायसी गदा in his hand, looked like the Kailāsa with its (raised) peak (सशृङ्गम् इव कैलासम्) 9. 11. 2; (v) Soma gave to Skanda his two companions Maṇi and Sumaṇi who both looked like the peaks of the Kailāsa 9. 44. 29; (2) Elephant: The white elephant Airāvata having four tusks looked like the Kailāsa with its peaks 3. 43. 36; (3) Objects: (i) Chariot: Kṛṣṇa's chariot compared with the peak of the Kailāsa (कैलासशिखरोपमात्) 5. 92. 30; (ii) Structures: (a) The सभा of Kubera, a hundred योजनस् long and seventy योजनस् wide, was comparable with the Kailāsaśikhara 2. 10. 2; (b) Sahadeva having received the excellent residence (वेश्माग्र्यम् 12. 44. 12) of Durmukha was delighted as was Dhanada (Kubera) when he received the Kailāsa 12. 44. 13; (c) The arena of Draupadī's स्व-यंवर was adorned with palatial buildings which looked like the peaks of the Kailāsa (कैलासशिखरप्रख्यैः) 1. 176. 19; (d) The dwelling places (आवसथान्) created for the kings who attended the Rājasūya looked like the Kailāsa peaks 2. 31. 19-20; (e) The Pāṇḍavas entered their residence at the Vāraṇāvata as the Guhyakas the Kailāsa 1. 134. 12.
कोका: Kokā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 33, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
कोकामुख: Kokāmukha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Caṇḍālikāśrama 13. 26. 49; described as holy (पुण्य) 3. 82. 137; if one who observes chastity and has observed vows (ब्रह्मचारी यतव्रतः) bathes there, he remembers his past lives— this is known from an ancient text (?) (जाति-स्मरत्वं प्राप्नोति दृष्टम् एतत् पुरातने) 3. 82. 137; if one who lives on vegetables and puts on bark garments (शाकभक्षश् चीरवासाः) bathes in the Kokāmukha he obtains the merit of bathing ten times in the Kumārītīrtha (?) (कुमारीर् विन्दते दश) 13. 26. 49 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 52: कुमारीः कुमारीसंज्ञकं तीर्थम्).
कोटितीर्थ: Koṭitīrtha1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Located near Mahākāla (in Ujjayinī ?); one who is restrained and eats limited food (नियतो नियताशनः) obtains by bathing there (उपस्पृश्य) the fruit of a horse sacri-fice 3. 80. 68. [See Tīrthakoṭi]
Koṭitīrtha2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Near the Pañcanada; one who is restrain-ed and eats limited food obtains hy bathing there (उपस्पृश्य) the fruit of a horse sacri-fice 3. 81. 14. [See Tīrthakoṭi]

Koṭitīrtha3 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Near the Gaṅgādvāra 3. 82. 23; one who is composed gets by bathing there (तत्रा-भिषेकं कुर्वीत) the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice and lifts up his family (कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्) 3. 82. 24. [See Tīrthakoṭi]

Koṭitīrtha4 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Near the Bhartṛsthāna, a place sacred to Mahāsena (Skanda) 3. 82. 68; 3. 83. 57; by bathing there and by worshipping Guha (Skanda) one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows and is full of splendour (तेजस्वी) 3. 82. 68; 3. 83. 57. [See Tīrtha-koṭi]
कोटिरूप: Koṭirūpa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the vicinity of the Gaṅgā-hrada (गङ्गाह्रदश् च तत्रैव) 3. 81. 172; by bathing there (उपस्पृश्य) one gets much gold (लभेद् बहु सुवर्णकम्) 3. 81. 171.
कोलाहल: Kolāhala m.: Name of a mountain. Described as having consciousness (चे-तनायुक्त) 1. 57. 32; due to his love (कामात्) for the river Śuktimatī, flowing by his side, the mountain blocked her course; then king Vasu struck the mountain with his foot; the stroke produced a hole in the mountain through which the blocked river began to flow again; the mountain begot a pair - a male and a female - on the river; the river, happy to get past the mountain, informed the king about the birth of two children 1. 57. 32-34.
कोल्लगिरि: Kollagiri m.: Name of a mountain. Sahadeva in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya brought under control the region of the entire Kollagiri (कृत्स्नं कोल्लगिरिं चैव … वशे चक्रे महामतिः) 2. 28. 45-46.
कोशेश्वरस्य: Kośeśvarasya tīrthāni nt. (pl.): Name of a number of तीर्थस् (sacred to Kubera ?) Near the place Ambuvaśya; by bathing there (कोशेश्वरस्य तीर्थेषु) one is freed of all diseases and is glorified in the world of Brahmadeva (सर्वव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो ब्र-ह्मलोके महीयते) 3. 81. 46. [See Kaubera1, Kaubera2]
कौबेर: Kaubera1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ sacred to Kubera. God Ailabila (Kubera) became the lord of wealth (धनाधिपत्यं संप्राप्तः) by practising austerities at this तीर्थ; while Kubera was at this तीर्थ riches and trea-sures waited on him (तत्रस्थम् एव तं (i. e. ऐलबिलम्) राजन् धनानि निधयस् तथा । उपतस्थुः) 9. 46. 22-23; Balarāma visited this तीर्थ, bathed there according to the rites, and gave wealth to Brāhmaṇas 9. 46. 23, 28. [See Kaubera2 and Kośeśva-rasya tīrthāni]

Kaubera2 nt.: Name of a forest sacred to Kubera. Described as excellent (काननोत्तम) 9. 46. 24; Balarāma saw in this forest that place where in ancient times Kubera practi-sed severe austerities and received many boons, as also lordship of wealth and friend-ship with Rudra; Kubera became there a god and a guardian of the world (सुरत्वं लोकपालत्वम् … यत्र लेभे) and got a son Nalakūbara 9. 46. 26; Kubera was conse-crated there by the Marudgaṇas and was given the Puṣpaka vimāna 9. 46. 24-27. [See Kaubera1]
कौशन्त: Kauśanta nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। According to the Tīrthavaṃśa (13. 26. 3) one who bathes in this तीर्थ is waited upon by a number of Apsarases (सेव्यते सो ऽप्सरोगणैः) 13. 26. 26.
कौशिकस्य: Kauśikasya hradaḥ m.: Name of a holy lake. Named after the sage Kauśika (Viśvā-mitra); situated on the river Kauśikī (3. 82. 124); Viśvāmitra attained there the highest perfection (यत्र सिद्धिं परां प्राप्तो विश्वामित्रो ऽथ कौशिकः) 3. 82. 123.

Kauśikasya āśramaḥ m.: A hermitage founded by Kauśika (Viśvāmitra). (1) Epic event: One of the आश्रमस् visited by Ambā for bathing and for practi-sing austerities in order to be able to kill Bhīṣma (कौशिकस्याश्रमे तथा … एतेषु तीर्थेषु तदा काशिकन्या … आप्लावयत गा-त्राणि तीव्रम् आस्थाय वै तपः) 5. 187. 26, 28. (2) Past event: When Indra asked Menakā to cause disturbance to the austeri-ties of Viśvāmitra (1. 65. 25), she went to the आश्रम of Kauśika; she saw Viśvāmitra practising तपस् in his आश्रम (ययौ साश्र-मं कौशिकस्य) 1. 65. 42; 1. 66. 2.
कौशिकी: Kauśikī f.: Name of a river, also called Pārā 1. 65. 32. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya twice among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 17, 28, 13; in the east 3. 85. 3; 1. 207. 5; near the आश्रम of Bharata 3. 82. 113. B. Origin: The river, created by Viśvāmitra for his purification, came to be known as Kauśikī (शौचार्थं यो नदीं चक्रे … तां पुण्यतमां लोके कौशिकीति विदुर् जनाः) 1. 65. 30. C. Description: Auspicious (शिवा) 13. 3. 10; (शिवजला) 3. 109. 20; holy, most holy (पुण्या) 3. 109. 20; 3. 110. 1; 13. 3. 10; (पुण्यतीर्था) 13. 96. 6; (पुण्यतमा) 1. 65. 30; river of the gods (देवनदी) 3. 110. 1; Kauśikī and other rivers contain waters of all the तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युताः) 13. 134. 12; de-stroyer of great sins (महापातकनाशिनी) 3. 82. 113; river of Viśvāmitra (विश्वामित्रस्य  … नदी) 13. 3. 10; frequented by hosts of Brahmanical and royal sages (ब्रह्मर्षि-गणसेविता, राजर्षिसेविता) 13. 3. 10; broad (विपुला) 13. 3. 10; difficult to cross due to ample waters (दुर्गमां बहुभिर् जलैः) 1. 65. 30; charming (रम्या) 3. 109. 20; famous (यशस्विनी) 1. 207. 7; full of roots and fruit (बहुमूलफला) 3. 85. 9; Kauśikī is among those described as excellent rivers (सरिद्वराः) 13. 134. 14; (सरितां वराः) 13. 134. 19; these rivers were proficient in their knowledge of the duties of women (स्त्रीधर्मकुशलाः) 13. 134. 19; Kauśikī (and other rivers) described as mothers of the universe and very strong (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā) 6. 10. 35. D. Events: (1) Epic: (i) Arjuna, during his exile, saw Kauśikī while proceeding to the east 1. 207. 7; (ii) Bhīma, in his eastern expedition (2. 26. 1) conquered the king who took resort on the marshy land of Kauśikī (कौशिकीकच्छ-निलयं राजानम् … निर्जित्य) 2. 27. 20-21; (iii) Yudhiṣṭhira was advised by Lomaśa to take bath in the river Nandā and then proceed to Kauśikī which he did 3. 109. 19-20; from Kauśikī he went to different sacred places (in the east) 3. 114. 1; (2) Past and mythological: (i) Viśvāmitra practised austerities on the bank of Kauśikī 3. 109. 19; here Viśvāmitra acquired the status of a Brāhmaṇa (अभ्यगाद् यत्र ब्राह्मणत्वम्) 3. 85. 9; in ancient times, during a difficult period, the royal sage Mataṅga supported here the wife of Viśvāmitra; when the period of famine was over, Viśvāmitra returned to his आश्रम on this river and gave the river the name Pārā (मुनिः पारेति नद्या वै नाम चक्रे तदा प्रभुः); on this river Viśvāmitra acted as priest in Mataṅga's sacrifice 1. 65. 31-33; (ii) the sages Śukra, Aṅgiras and others while visiting different तीर्थस् reached the river Kauśikī on the full moon day of the month of Māgha 13. 96. 6; (iii) Mṛtyu, conceived as a maiden, while trying to avoid Brahmadeva's command to deprive people of their lives, practised severe austerities at different places, one of them being the river Kauśikī 12. 250. 21 (Nī. on 12. 258. 21: कौशिकीं गण्डकीं नदीम्). E Importance: (i) Umā consulted Kauśikī and other rivers on the duties of a women (स्त्रीधर्म) before ex-pounding it to Śaṅkara 13. 134. 13, 18-20; (ii) Kauśikī and other rivers wait upon Maheśvara for his bath (उपस्पर्शनहेतोस् त्वा समीपस्था उपासते) 13. 134. 12; (iii) Mārkaṇḍeya saw Kauśiki, among other rivers, in the belly of Bāla (3. 186. 83, i. e. Nārā-yaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 93; (iv) listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among rivers famous as mothers of fire-hearths, i. e. sacrifices were performed on their banks (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24 (For Nī. see Kapilā); (v) on its banks there are आश्रमस् of Viśvāmitra and Kāśyapa 3. 110, 1-2 and of Bharata 3. 82. 113; (vi) finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2. F. Holy: By waiting upon Kauśikī (कौशिकीं तत्र सेवेत) one obtains the fruit of a Rājasūya 3. 82. 113; by staying at Kauśikī for a month one gets the merit of per-forming an Aśvamedha (अश्वमेधस्य यत् पुण्यम्) 3. 82. 124; by observing total fast and by remaining uncovetous (वायुभक्षस् त्व् अलोलुपः) at the gate of Kauśikī (कौशिकी-द्वारम्) for twenty one nights one goes to heaven 13. 26. 30; if one takes limited food (नियताहारः) and bathes at the confluence of the rivers Kauśikī and Dṛṣadvatī one is freed of all sins 3. 81. 80; if one who is controlled (यतः) and is learned (विद्वान्) fasts for three nights and bathes at the con-fluence of the Kauśikī and the Aruṇā he is freed of all sins 3. 82. 135; Kauśikī is one of those rivers by visiting which the high-souled persons who have observed vows, go to the Goloka (?) (ते तत्र मोदन्ति गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44) after assuming heavenly form, wearing heavenly garlands, holy, and rich in auspicious fragrance (दिव्यसंस्थाना दिव्य-माल्यधराः शिवाः । प्रयान्ति पुण्यगन्-धाढ्याः) 13. 105. 47-48.
क्रौञ्चपादी: Krauñcapādī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting (?) Krauñcapādī one is freed of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa (मुञ्-जपृष्ठं गयां चैव निरृतिं देवपर्व-तम् । तृतीयां क्रौञ्चपादीं च ब्रह्महत्या विशुध्यति) 13. 26. 40.
कक्षसेनस्य: Kakṣasenasya āśramaḥ m.: Name of an आश्रम established by Kakṣasena. Listed among the holy places in the west 3. 87. 1; on the mountain Asita (असितो नाम पर्वतः । आश्रमः कक्षसेनस्य … तत्र) 3. 87. 9-10; described as holy (पुण्य) 3. 87. 10; men obtain perfection there by practising austerities even for a short period (तत्राल्पेनैव सिध्यन्ति मा-नवास् तपसा विभो) 3. 87. 10.
कण्वाश्रम: Kaṇvāśrama1 m.: Name of an आश्रम where Kaṇva (Kāśyapa) lived (काश्यप-स्यायतनम् 1. 64. 42. A. Location: Along the river Mālinī (मालिनीम् अभितो … नदीम्) 1. 64. 18; (अलं-कृतं मालिन्या) 1. 64. 24. B. Descrip-tion: Isolated (विविक्त) 1. 64. 42; holy (शिव) 1. 64. 42; auspicious (शुभ) 1. 64. 41; excellent आश्रम (आश्रमप्रवर) 1. 64. 15, 41; best (उत्तम) 1. 64. 29; pleasing (रम्य) 1. 64. 15; attractive, very attractive (मनोरम) 1. 64. 15; (सुमनो-हर) 1. 64. 19; (अत्यर्थमनोहर) 1. 64. 42; protected by the austerities of Kāśyapa (काश्यपतपोगुप्त) 1. 64. 41; full of asce-tics who observed rigid vows (महाव्रतैर् वृतं समन्ताद् ऋषिभिस् तपोधनैः) 1. 64. 42; (तपोधनगणैर् युतम्) 1. 64. 41; resembling the world of gods (देवलोक-प्रतीकाश) 1. 64. 19; resembling the world of Brahman (ब्रह्मलोकप्रतीकाश) 1. 64. 30; (ब्रह्मलोक इव) 1. 64. 34, 40; for other details regarding trees, birds, animals, and ascetics engaged in their ritual practices and Vedic recitations see 1. 64. 16-18; 30-39; 41-42. C. Past events: (1) Duḥ-ṣanta did not find Kāśyapa in the आश्रम when he visited it since the sage had gone to collect fruits (नापश्यद् आश्रमे तस्मिन् ऋषिम्) 1. 65. 1-2; (फलाहारो गतो राजन् पिता मे इत आश्रमात्) 1. 67. 5; Kāśyapa's daughter (Śakuntalā) came out of the आश्रम to receive the king and offered him guest worship (कन्या … निश्चक्रामाश्रमात् तस्मात्) 1. 65. 3-6; later Śakuntalā reminded the king about their meeting in the आश्रम of her father (अहम् आसादिता राजन् कुमारी पितुर् आश्रमे) 1. 68. 66; Duḥṣanta, while he was in the आश्रम, asked the girl who she was (कासि कस्यासि सुश्रोणि … एवम् उक्ता तदा कन्या तेन राज्ञा तदाश्रमे) 1. 65. 12-14; Kaṇva returned to his आश्रम from the forest (कण्वो ऽप्याश्रमम् आगमत्) 1. 67. 23; when Śakuntalā's son was six years old he bound tigers, lions, boars, elephants and buffaloes to trees all around in the surroundings of the आश्रम; he mounted them, tamed them and ran hither and thither playing with them in the precincts of the आश्रम (षड्वर्ष एव बालः स कण्वाश्रमपदं प्रति । व्याघ्रान् सिंहान् वराहांश् च गजांश् च महिषांस् तथा ॥ बद्ध्वा वृक्षेषु बलवान् आश्रमस्य समन्-ततः । आरोहन् दमयंश् चैव क्रीडंश् च परिधावति ॥ ) 1. 68. 5-6; the residents of the Kaṇvāśrama (कण्वाश्रमनिवासिनः) named the child Sarvadamana since he tamed all (अस्त्व् अयं सर्वदमनः सर्-वं हि दमयत्य् अयम्) 1. 68. 7; Kaṇva asked his pupils to take Śakuntalā and her son from the आश्रम to her husband's place (इतो ”श्रमात् । भर्त्रे प्रापयत) 1. 68. 10; when disowned by the king, Śakuntalā decided to return to the आश्रम (गमि-ष्याम्य् अहम् आश्रमम्) 1. 68. 71. [See Kāśyapāśrama]

Kaṇvāśrama2 m.: Name of an आश्रम established by Kaṇva. A. Location: On the west coast (?) (mentioned after Jambūmārga and Agastya-saras and before one reached Narmadā) 3. 80. 60, 63, 71. B. Description: Adorn-ed with glory (श्रीजुष्ट) and honoured by people (लोकपूजित) 3. 80. 64. C. Holi-ness: Called an excellent holy forest for observing religious practices (धर्मारण्-यं हि तत् पुण्यम् आद्यं च) 3. 80. 65; by just entering it one was freed of all sins (यत्र प्रविष्टमात्रो वै पापेभ्यो विप्र-मुच्यते) 3. 80. 65; by satisfying manes and gods there, one who is controlled and takes limited food gets the fruit of a sacri-fice performing which all desires are ful-filled (अर्चयित्वा पितॄन् देवान् नियतो नियता-शनः । सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलम् अश्नुते) 3. 80. 66.

Kaṇvāśrama3 m.: Name of an आश्रम of Kaṇva. Listed among the holy places of the south 3. 86. 1; near the river Praveṇī (?) (प्रवेण्युत्तरपार्श्वे तु पुण्ये कण्वाश्रमे तथा) 3. 86. 8; described as holy (पुण्य) 3. 86. 8; Dhaumya told Yudhiṣṭhira that he had heard that there were many forests of ascetics near the आश्रम (तापसानाम् अरण्यानि कीर्तितानि यथाश्रुति) 3. 86. 8.
कन्यकुब्ज: Kanyakubja nt.: Name of a city. A. Location: Near Gaṅgā, where on its bank there is a तीर्थ known to men as Aśvatīrtha (अदूरे कन्यकुब्जस्य गङ्गा-याष् तीरम् उत्तमम् । अश्वतीर्थं तद् अद्यापि मानवाः परिचक्षते) 13. 4. 17; 3. 115. 17. B. Past events: (1) There was once a king called Gādhi(n) who ruled at Kanya-kubja (कन्यकुब्जे महान् आसीत् पार्थिवो भरतर्षभ । गाधीति विश्रुतो लोके) 1. 165. 3; 3. 115. 9; formerly at Kanyukubja Ṛcīka Bhārgava, chose Satyavatī, daughter of Gādhi, for his wife (पुरा हि कन्यकुब्जे वै गाधेः सत्यवतीं सुताम् । भार्यार्थे ऽवरयत् कन्याम् ऋचीकः) 5. 117. 4; at Kanyakubja, near the river Gaṅgā, Gādhi gave his daughter Satyavatī to Ṛcīka, son of Bhṛgu; in this marriage gods acted as companions of the bridegroom (गङ्गायां कन्यकुब्जे वै ददौ सत्यवतीं तदा । ततो गाधिः सुतां तस्मै जन्याश् चासन् सुरास् तदा) 3. 115. 17; (2) Jāmadagnya sang in an अनुवंश stanza that Kau-śika (Viśvāmitra) drank Soma with Indra at Kanyakubja (यत्रानुवंशं भगवाञ् जामदग्न्यस् तदा जगौ । … कन्यकुब्जे ऽपि-बत् सोमम् इन्द्रेण सह कौशिकः) 3. 85. 11-12.
कन्याश्रम: Kanyāśrama1 m.: Name of an आश्रम। One reaches Kanyāśrama from Soma-tīrtha and Dadhīcatīrtha 3. 81. 162-163, 165; one should visit it with a controlled mind and observe chastity; intent on fasting, if he fasts there for three nights he gets a hundred heavenly maidens and goes to the world of Brahman (ततः कन्-याश्रमं गच्छेन् नियतो ब्रह्मचर्यवान् । त्रिरात्रोपोषितो राजन्न् उपवासपरायणः । लभेत् कन्याशतं दिव्यं ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ॥ ) 3. 81. 165.

Kanyāśrama2 m.: Name of an आश्रम। A. Location: Situated near Devahrada on the confluence of Kṛṣṇā and Veṇṇā 3. 83. 34. B. Holiness: By living there for three nights and by bathing there one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha (त्रिरात्रम् उषितः स्नात्वा अश्वमेधफलं लभेत् … तथा कन्याश्रमे नृप) 3. 83. 33-34; just by visiting the place (गमनाद् एव) one gets the fruit of performing a hundred Agni-ṣṭoma sacrifices 3. 83. 35. C. Past event: By offering there a hundred sacrifices the king of gods (Indra) went to heaven (कन्याश्रमे नृप । यत्र क्रतुशतैर् इष्ट्वा देवराजो दिवं गतः) 3. 83. 34-35.
कपिलावट: Kapilāvaṭa m.: Name of a holy place. A pilgrim should visit Kapilāvaṭa; by staying there for a night he gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows (कपिलावटं च गच्छेत तीर्थसेवी नराधिप । उष्यैकां रजनीं तत्र गोसहस्रफलं लभेत् ॥ ) 3. 82. 27.
करहाटक: Karahāṭaka nt.: Name of a city (? country ?). Sahadeva, in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya, subjugated Karahā-ṭaka just by sending messengers and he made the people pay tribute (करहाटकं दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदा-पयत्) 2. 28. 47.
कवाट: Kavāṭa nt.: Name of a city. Kṛṣṇa killed the Pāṇḍya king at Ka-vāṭa (अयं कवाटे निजघान पाण्ड्यम्) 5. 47. 70.
कान्तिपुर: Kāntipura nt.: Name of a city. It was near this city that the earth received the child conceived by the six Kṛttikās and which (after delivery) was united into one (ततस् तं षडधिष्ठानं गर्भम् एकत्वम् आगतम् । पृथिवी प्रति-जग्राह कान्तीपुरसमीपतः ॥ ) 13. 86. 11.
काम्पिल्य: Kāmpilya nt.: Name of a city; also referred to as Drupadasya nagarī or pura 1. 156. 11; 3. 13. 101. A. Location: Capital of Mākandī (southern Pāñcāla country) on the south bank of Gaṅgā (राजासि दक्षिणे कूले भागी-रथ्या(ः) 1. 128. 12; (माकन्दीम् अथ गङ्-गायास् तीरे … । दक्षिणांश् चैव पाञ्चालान्) 1. 128. 15. B. Description: Excellent town (पुरोत्तम) 1. 128. 15. C. Epic events: (1) When Droṇa gave half of the Pāñcāla country to Drupada, the latter went to Kāmpilya and settled down there (सो ऽध्यावसद् … काम्पिल्यम्) 1. 128. 15; hence referred to as द्रुपदस्य नगरी 1. 56. 11; द्रुपदस्य पुर 3. 13. 101; (2) Kuntī and the Pāṇḍavas took leave of the Brāhmaṇa at Ekacakrā and went to the town of Drupada 1. 156. 11; 3. 13. 101; (3) Śikhaṇḍin, after his marriage with the daughter of the king of Daśārṇas, re-turned to Kāmpilya 5. 190. 13; the king of Daśārṇas arrived at Kāmpilya to find out whether Śikhaṇḍin was a man or a woman and sent his messenger to Drupada 5. 193. 13. D. Past event: When Brahmadatta ruled at Kāmpilya there lived with him for a long time a female bird, Pūjanī by name, in his inner apartment (अन्तःपुर-निवासिनी) 12. 137. 5. [See Pāñcālanagara]
कालिकाश्रम: Kālikāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। On the bank of the river Vipāśā; by reaching Kālikāśrama and by bathing in Vipāśā, one who observes chastity and one who has mastered his wrath is freed of rebirth after three nights (काइइकाश्र-मम् आसाद्य विपाशायां कृतोदकः । ब्र-ह्मचारी जितक्रोधस् त्रिरात्रान् मुच्यते भवात् ॥ ) 13. 26. 22.
कश्यपाश्रम: Kaśyapāśrama m. An आश्रम where Kāśyapa and his son Ṛṣyaśṛṅga lived. A. Location: Near the river Kauśikī and near Viśvāmitrāśrama; the Pāṇḍavas, with Lomaśa, were to reach it from the river Nandā (ततो नन्दाप्लुताङ्गस् त्वं कौशि-कीम् अभियास्यसि । … ततस् तत्र समाप्लुत्य गात्राणि सगणो नृपः । जगाम कौशिकीम्) 3. 109. 19-20; (एषा देवनदी पुण्या कौशिकि  … विश्वामित्राश्रमः … अत्र प्रकाशते । आश्रमश् चैव … काश्यपस्य) 3. 110. 1-2. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 113. 25; known to be holy (प्न्ण्याख्य) 3. 110. 2; Sarja, Aśoka and Tilaka trees, in full blossom, in its precincts (सर्जान् अशोकांस् तिलकांश् च वृक्षान् प्रपुष्पितान् अवनाम्याव-भज्य) 3. 111. 16; beautifies the great lake near it (महाह्रदं शोभयन्) 3. 113. 25. C. Holiness: By bathing there one becomes pure and has done all his duties (अत्र स्नातः कृतकृत्यो विशुद्धः) 3. 113. 25. D. Epic event: Lomaśa asked Yudhiṣṭhira to bathe in the lake near the आश्रम and then proceed to other तीर्थस् 3. 113. 25. E. Past event (related to the Rāmāyaṇa): Ṛśya-śṛṅga, son of Kāśyapa by a female deer, born here 3. 110. 2, 4; the old courtesan who, with her daughter, went to seduce Ṛśyaśṛṅga tied her boat not far from the Kāśyapā-śrama (अदूरे काश्यपाश्रमात्) 3. 111. 4; her daughter reached the आश्रम (आश्रमं समासाद्य) and saw there the son of Kāśyapa 3. 111. 6: Kāśyapa returned to his आश्रम after collecting fruits and roots from the forest (अथोपायात् … स्वम् आश्रमं फल-मूलानि गृह्य) 3. 113. 14; after Ṛśyaśṛṅga's wife Śāntā gave birth to a child, he, having done all what the king desired, was expected to return with his wife to the forest and the place of his father (i. e. to the आश्रम) (जाते पुत्रे वनम् एवाव्रजेथाः … ययौ च यत्रास्य पिता बभूव) 3. 113. 21-22. [See Ṛśyaśṛṅgasya āśramaḥ]
किङ्किणीकाश्रम: Kiṅkiṇīkāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। One who bathes at this आश्रम can move at will and is glorified in the heavenly abode of the Apsarases (निवासे ऽप्सरसां दिव्ये कामचारी महीयते) 13. 26. 21.
किष्किन्धा: Kiṣkindhā f.: Name of the city where first Vālin, and next Sugrīva ruled. Rāmāyaṇa events: (1) After Rāma and Sugrīva entered into a covenant they all proceeded to Kiṣkindhā (अभ्येत्य सर्वे किष्किन्धाम्) looking forward to the fight between Vālin and Sugrīva; Sugrīva having reached the city (सुग्रीवः प्राप्य किष्किन्-धाम्) roared (challenging Vālin for a duel) 3. 264. 15-16; (2) Rāma asked Lakṣmaṇa to go to Kiṣkindhā and find out what Sugrīva's plans were (regarding the search of Sītā); Rāma doubted Sugrī-va's sincerity about carrying out the terms of the covenant after the death of Vālin by Rāma in the forest bordering on Kiṣkindhā (किष्किन्धोपवने); Lakṣmaṇa started for Kiṣkindhā and having rea-ched its gate (किष्किन्धाद्वारम् आसाद्य) enterd the city without any opposition 3. 266. 5, 7, 12; (3) After honouring the monkey chiefs, the Gopucchas and the bears and after allowing them to leave, Rāma, along with Sugrīva, reached Kiṣkindhā (किष्किन्धां पुनर् आगमत्); at Kiṣkindhā (किष्किन्धाम् तु समासाद्य) Rāma conse-crated Aṅgada as crown prince 3. 275. 55, 57.
कुण्डिन: Kuṇḍina nt.: Name of a city. A. Epic event: Rukmin, after he suffer-ed the defeat at the hands of Kṛṣṇa, did not return to Kuṇḍina but established another town Bhojakaṭa 5. 155. 14-15. B. Past events (from Nala story): Dama-yantī sent away her two sons with Nala's charioteer to her kinsmen at Kuṇḍina 3. 57. 17; When Damayantī announced her second स्वयंवर, Ṛtuparṇa reached Vidarbha and entered Kuṇḍina after his arrival was reported to king Bhīma 3. 71. 2; After Nala's meeting with Damayantī and after the departure of Ṛtuparṇa, he did not stay very long in the city of Kuṇḍina 3. 76. 19.
कुम्भकर्णाश्रम: Kumbhakarṇāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। Near Urvaśītīrtha and Somāśrama; by bathing there one is honoured in the world (पूज्यते भुवि मानवः) 3. 82. 136.
कुशवति: Kuśavati f.: Name of a town. When gods once held counsel at Kuśa-vatī it was attended by Kubera with his Yakṣas in very large numbers (देवतानाम् अभून् मन्त्रः कुशवत्याम् नरेश्वर । वृतस् तत्राहम् अगमं महापद्मशतैस् त्रिभिः । यक्षाणाम्) 3. 158. 51 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 161. 54: कुशवत्यां कुश-स्थली संज्ञे देशविशेषे).
कुशस्थल: Kuśasthala nt.: Name of a village (ग्राम). One of the five villages (ग्रामाः) for which Yudhiṣṭhira was willing to come to terms with the Kauravas; he named four of these five villages and left the fifth to be named by Duryodhana 5. 31. 19-20; 5. 70. 15; 5. 80. 7 (for the names of the other three villages see Āsandī).
कृत्तिकानाम्: Kṛttikānām āśramaḥ m.: Name of an आश्रम। By bathing there, by offering libations to manes and by satisfying god Mahādeva one becomes clean and goes to heaven (आश्रमे कृत्तिकानां तु स्नात्वा यस् तर्प-येत् पितॄन् । तोषयित्वा महादेवं निर्मलः स्वर्गम् आप्नुयात् ॥ ) 13. 26. 23.
कोशला: Kośalā f.: Name of a city (or river ?) Two तीर्थस् Ṛṣabhatīrtha and Kāla-tīrtha located near Kośalā 3. 83. 10-11.
कङ्क: Kaṅka m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: Mentioned along with Śakas and Tukhāras, they seem to belong to the northwest (शकास् तुखाराः कङ्काश् च) 2. 47. 26. B. Description: Leading the life of Dasyus, they live on the country-side (सर्वे विषयवासिनः … सर्वे ते दस्यु-जीविनः) 12. 65. 15. C. Epic event: They brought tribute of various kinds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira; the tribute con-sisted of an अर्बुद of horses of noble descent and running long distances (?), (other tributes) in crores and large num-bers and a पद्म of gold; they were stopped at the gate (महागमान् दूरगमान् गणितान् अर्बुदं हयान् ॥ कोटिशश् चैव बहुशः सुवर्णं पद्मसंमितम् । बलिम् आदाय विविधं द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ ) 2. 47. 26-27. D. Past event: King Māndhātṛ once asked Indra what the धर्म of the Kaṅkas and others who lived as Dasyus was like and how they should be restrained by kings like him (कथं धर्मं चरे-युस् ते … मद्विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः) 12. 65. 15; Indra then told him the धर्म of the Dasyus 12. 65. 17-22.
कच्छ: Kaccha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas (also called देशाः सं-कीर्तिताः 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कच्छा गोपालकच्छाश् च) 6. 10. 55.
करण्ठ: Karaṇṭha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called देशाः संकीर्तिताः 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणाः) 6. 10. 56; (करण्ठाः कुरकास् तथा) 6. 10. 61.
करभञ्जक: Karabhañjaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called देशाः संकीर्तिताः 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणाः) 6. 10. 56; (तथैव करभञ्जकाः) 6. 10. 68.
करीषक: Karīṣaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37. 5; (उद्देशमात्रेण मया देशाः संकीर्ति-ताः) 6. 10. 68; (वध्राः करीषकाश् चापि) 6. 10. 54.
करूष: Karūṣa, Karūṣaka, Kārūṣa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; often mentioned along with Kāśis and Cedis. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the (northern) Janapadas (also called Deśas देशाः संकीर्तिताः 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (चेदिवत्साः करूषाश् च) 6. 10. 39. B. King: The king of the Karūṣa country referred to as Karūṣādhipati 2. 4. 25. once named as Vakra (वक्रः कुरूषा-धिपतिः) 2. 13. 10; another king Alarka called Kāśikarūṣarāja (अलर्कम् … काशि-करूषराजम्) 3. 26. 12; a king, not named (करूषराजप्रमुखाः) 5. 22. 26; C. Des-cription: Their warriors, who were great fighters, were of noble birth, willing to die in battle without showing their backs, had banners decorated with gold (महारथाः समाख्याताः कुलपुत्रास् तनुत्यजः । अपरावर्तिनः सर्वे सुवर्णविकृतध्वजाः) 6. 102. 17; brave (शूर) 7. 8. 27; of fierce prowess (उग्रविक्रम) 8. 21. 27. D. Epic events: (1) A voice, not coming from a visible body, declared at the time of Arjuna's birth that he will subjugate among others, Cedis, Kāśis and Karūṣas, (एष … वशे कृत्वा … चेदिकाशिकरूषांश् च) 1. 114. 31; (2) King of Karūṣas, mentioned among the best Kṣatriyas who waited on Yudhiṣṭhira in his new Sabhā (तथैव क्षत्रियश्रेष्ठा धर्मराजम् उपासते … करूषाधिपतिस् तथा) 2. 4. 18, 25; (3) Vakra, the king of Karūṣas was, like a pupil, in attendance of Jarāsandha (शिष्य-वत् समुपस्थितः । वक्रः करूषाधिपतिः) 2. 13. 10; (4) Dhṛtarāṣṭra mentions Cedis and Karūṣakas who, with their kings, sided with Yudhiṣṭhira for the war; the kings, headed by the king of the Karūṣas, highly respected Śiśupāla; but when Kṛṣṇa formerly attacked him in war, they fled away (अपाश्रिताश् चेदिकरूषकाश् च … भूमि-पालैः समेताः । … शिशुपालं … यस्य सर्वे वर्धयन्ति स्म मानं करूषराजप्रमु-खाः नरेन्द्राः ॥ तम् असह्यं केशवं तत्र मत्वा … संप्राद्रवंश् चेदिपतिं विहाय) 5. 22. 24, 26-27; (5) Karṇa boasted that he alone would kill the Karūṣa warriors (पाञ्चालकरूषमत्स्यान् । निहत्य) 5. 61. 5; (6) Yudhiṣṭhira ordered Dhṛṣṭaketu, the leader of the army of Cedis, Kāśis and Karūṣas, to march out for Kurukṣetra (चेदिकाशिकरूषाणां नेतारं … धृष्टकेतुम् अथादिशत् ॥ ) 5. 197. 2; (7) On the first day of the war Bhīṣma was seen moving in the army of the Cedis, Kāśis, Karūṣas and Pāñcālas (चेदीकाशि-करूषेषु । बहुधा तालश् चरन् केतुर् अदृश्यत) 6. 45. 4; (8) On the second day of the war, Cedis, Matsyas and Karūṣas, led by Bhīma, dashed towards Niṣādas and their kings (चेदिमत्स्यकरूषाश् च भीम-सेनपुरोगमाः । अभ्यवर्तन्त सहसा निषा-दान् सह राजभिः ॥ ) 6. 50. 8; (9) On the third day of the war, Cedis, Kāśis and Karūṣas were stationed at the place of the right tip of the Ardhacandravyūha (दक्षिणं शृङ्गम् आस्थाय … चेदिकाशिक-रूषैश् च) 6. 52. 11, 13; (10) Towards the end of that day, Cedis, Pāñcālas, Karūṣas and Matsyas, seeing the havoc caused by the Aindrāstra of Arjuna (6. 55. 110), roared loudly which caused distress to the enemies (चेदिपाञ्चालकरूषमत्स्याः … प्र-णेदुः । वित्रास्य सेनां ध्वजिनी पतीनाम्) 6. 55. 126; (11) On the eighth day of the war, during the night, Duryodhana remin-ded Bhīṣma of his vow to kill the Pāṇḍavas along with the Somakas, Pāñcālas and Karūṣas (पूर्वम् उक्तं महाबाहो निह-निष्यामि सोमकान् । पाञ्चालान् पाण्डवैः सार्धं करूषांश् चेति) 6. 93. 37; (12) On the ninth day of the war, fourteen thousand Cedi, Kāśi and Karūṣa warriors attacked Bhīṣma and were destroyed along with their horses, chariots and elephants (चेदिकाशीकरूषाणां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश … संग्रामे भीष्मम् आसाद्य … निमग्नाः परलोकाय सवाजिरथकुञ्जराः) 6. 102. 17-18; (13) On the tenth day of the war, fourteen thousand Cedi, Kāśi and Karūṣa warriors attacked Bhīṣma and perished (चेदिकाशिकरूषाणां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश … जग्मुस् ते परलोकाय) 6. 112. 73-74; (14) Dhṛtarāṣṭra felt that Droṇa must have been killed by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, surrounded by Kekaya, Cedi, Karūṣa and Matsya kings (वृतः … केकयैश् चेदिकारूषाइर् मत्स्यैर् अन्यैश् च भूमिपैः) 7. 8. 27; (15) Among the exploits of Kṛṣṇa recounted by Dhṛtarāṣṭra one referred to his victory in war over Kāśis, Karūṣas and many others (काशिकोसलान् °करूषांश् च … अजयद् रणे) 7. 10. 15; (16) On the eleventh day of the war, among those who attacked Droṇa are mentioned Cedis and Kārūṣas; he scattered them away, as does wind a heap of cotton, and burnt their armies and defeated them again and again (चेदिकारूष-कोसलाः । … हृष्टा द्रोणम् उपाद्रवन् ॥ … आचार्यः … व्यधमत् तान्य् अनीकानि तूल-राशिम् इवानिलः ॥ निर्दहन्तम् अनीकानि तानि तानि पुनः पुनः । … अजयच् चेदीन् कारूषान्  … भारद्वाजः पुनः पुनः ॥ ) 7. 20. 18-20, 23; (17) On the sixteenth day of the war, when Bhīma, riding an elephant and surrounded by elephant drivers (or warri-ors) of the Karūṣa, Kosala, Kāśi and Magadha countries, marched into the large Kaurava army, the other warriors riding chariots, and excellent foot-soldiers rushed with them dancing and laughing (करूषाः काश्या … दुद्रुवुः ॥ तेषां रथाश् च नागाश् च प्रवराश् चापि पत्तयः ॥ … हृष्टा नृत्यन्ति च हसन्ति च ॥ तस्य सैन्यस्य महतो महामात्रवरैर् वृतः । मध्यं वृकोदरो ऽभ्यागात् त्वदीयं नागधूर्गतः ॥ ) 8. 8. 19-21; (18) Towards the end of the same day, the army of Cedis, Kārūṣas and others, riding their chariots, horses and elephants and also foot-soldiers, all of fierce prowess, surrounded Karṇa and, bent on killing him, showered on him different weapons while speaking harsh words; Karṇa blew them away as does wind the trees after breaking them (चेदिकारूषमत्स्यानां … यद् बलम् ।  … एते रथाश्वद्विरदैः पत्तिभिश् चोग्र-विक्रमैः । परिवार्य रणे कर्णं नाना-शस्त्रैर् अवाकिरन् । भाषन्तो वाग्भिर् उग्रा-भिः सर्वे कर्णवधे वृताः ॥ … अपोवाह स्म तान् सर्वान् द्रुमान् भङ्क्त्वेव मारुतः ॥ ) 8. 21. 26-28; (19) On the seventeenth day of the war, Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman and Śakuni fought with the brave Kāśi, Matsya-Kārūṣa, and other soldiers (काशिमत्स्यैश् च कारूषैः … । … शूरवीरैर् युयुधुर् युद्धदुर्मदाः ॥ ) 8. 32. 17; (20) On the same day, Kārūṣa, Kāśi and other warriors encircled Vasuṣeṇa (कारूषा … काशिकोस-लाः । … वीरा वसुषेणम् अवारयन्) 8. 33. 22; (21) The same day, Karṇa held back Bhīmasena along with Karūṣas and others (भीमसेनं करूषांश् च … । कर्णो … वारयाम् आस) 8. 38. 16; (22) The same day, angered, Karṇa killed great Cedi and Kārūṣa warriors in the presence of Bhīma (चेदिकारूषान् … महारथान् । कर्णो जघान संक्रुद्धो भीमसेनस्य पश्यतः ॥ ) 8. 40. 2; (23) Kārūṣas, Cedis and others, protected by Arjuna, had destroyed hosts of enemies (कारूषैश् चेदिकेकयैः । त्वया गुप्तैर् … कृतः शत्रुगणक्षयः) 8. 51. 6; (24) Kṛṣṇa had to remind Arjuna that Bhīṣma had killed Cedis, Kāśis, Pāñcalas and Karūṣas among others with his arrows (स चेदिकाशिपाञ्चालान् करूषान् … । शरैः … निधनम् अनयत्) 8. 51. 27; (25) Śalya drove Karṇa's chariot to the Cedis, Pāñcā-lās and Karūṣas (शल्यः श्वेतान् अश्वान् महाजवान् । प्राहिणोच् चेदिपाञ्चालान् करू-षांश् च) 8. 56. 9.
कर्णप्रावरण: Karṇaprāvaraṇa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Epic events: (1) Sahadeva in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ 2. 28. 8; प्रायाद् … दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 37) subjugated, among others, the Karṇaprāvaraṇas (कर्ण-प्रावरणान् अपि । … वशे चक्रे) 2. 28. 44, 46; (2) Karṇaprāvaraṇas mentioned among those who, led by Bhāradvāja (Droṇa), followed Bhīṣma on the second day of the war (तम् अन्वयान् … भारद्वा-जः … । … कर्णप्रावरणैर् अपि॑सहिताः … भीष्मम्) 6. 47. 12-13.
कर्णिक: Karṇika m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56; (कर्णिकाः कुन्तिकाश् चैव) 6. 10. 58; also called Deśas (देशाः संकीर्तिताः) 6. 10. 68.
कलिङ्ग: Kaliṅga1 m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people; Kaliṅga often mentioned along with Aṅga and Vaṅga; the people of Kaliṅga also referred to as Kāliṅga 6. 50. 19, 77, 82, 108; 6. 67. 13; 8. 17. 20; 16. 7. 10, or as Kaliṅgaka (8. 30. 75); the country is also referred to as Kaliṅga-rāṣṭra (1. 207. 10), or as Kaliṅgaviṣaya 12. 4. 2), or as Sarvakaliṅga (6. 17. 32). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (अङ्गा वङ्गाः कलिङ्गाश् च) 6. 10. 44; towards the east (प्राचीं दिशम् अभिप्रेप्सुर् जगाम) 1. 207. 5; on the eastern coast, where Vaitaraṇī river flew (ततः समुद्रतीरेण जगाम … कलिङ्गान् प्रति); (एते कलिङ्गाः कौन्तेय यत्र वैतरणी नदी) 3. 114. 3-4; a little to the south, as Aṅgas are mentioned among the countries which Sahadeva subjugated in the south (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1; (दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 8; (प्रायाद् … दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 37. B. King and princess of the country: The king Śrutāyus of Kaliṅgas is referred to as कलिङ्गराज 6. 50. 112, कलिङ्गानां जनाधिपः 6. 50. 7, 23, or simply Kaliṅga (sg.) 6. 49. 37; 6. 50. 1-2, 26, 28, 62-63, 65, 67-69; 7. 6. 2 (different from Śrutāyus); princess Karaṇḍu referred to as Kāliṅgī 1. 90. 21; another Kaliṅga princess (not named) wife of Taṃsu also referred to as Kāliṅgī 1. 90. 28. C. Description: (1) The Kaliṅga warriors were Kṣatriyas 6. 50. 71; energetic (तरस्विन्) 6. 50. 60; their army made use of large weapons (प्रगृहीत-महायुध) 6. 50. 4, and it was difficult to go beyond it (सेनाम् … कलिङ्गानां दुर-त्ययाम्) 7. 116. 11; (2) The people of Kaliṅga country knew what was eternal धर्म (कलिङ्गा … ॥ … धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्) 8. 30. 60-61; the elders among them lived according to the धर्म taught to them (कलिङ्गकाश् … शिष्टान् धर्मान् उपजीवन्ति वृद्धाः) 8. 30. 75. D.
