Epic Events: [For citations common to Aṅga and Kaliṅga, see Aṅga] (1) Arjuna, during the term of his exile visited all holy places in Aṅga, Vaṅga and Kaliṅga 1. 207. 9; Brāhmaṇas, who followed him up to the gate of the Kaliṅga country, permitted him to go further and returned; Arjuna then went beyond the Kaliṅga country (कलिङ्गराष्ट्रद्वारेषु ब्राह्मणाः … उपा-वर्तन्त); (स कलिङ्गान् अतिक्रम्य … ययौ) 1. 207. 10, 12; (2) Sahadeva, in his expedition to the south, subjugated the Kaliṅgas merely by sending envoys and made them pay tribute (कलिङ्गान् … दूतईर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत्) 2. 28. 48-49; the event is referred to while mentioning the exploits of Sahadeva where he is said to have conquered the Kaliṅgas at Dantakūra (सहदेवः कलिङ्गान् समा-गतान् अजयद् दन्तकूरे) 5. 23. 23 (Nī., however, on 5. 23. 24: दन्तकूरः सङ्ग्रा-मः); the event is also referred to by Saṃjaya while listing the heroes on the side of the Pāṇḍavas (यः … कलिङ्गांश् च युधाजयत्) 5. 49. 28 (in 2. 28. 48 Sahadeva is said to have won them without a battle); (3) The kings of Vaṅgas and Kaliṅgas brought fine cloth, silk, cotton cloth and covers as tribute for the Rāja-sūya of Yudhiṣṭhira; they were asked to give more to get entrance; each one of them then gave one thousand elephants who were lotus-coloured, mountain-high, always in rut, and had pole-long trunks, and were cloth decked, gold-gilded and armoured, patient and of good breed; they were from near the Kāmyaka lake (वङ्गाः कलिङ्गपतयस् … । दुकूलं कौशिकं चैव पत्रोर्णं प्रावरान् अपि ॥ … कृतकाराः(?) सुबलयस् ततो द्वारम् अवाप्स्यथ ॥ ईषा-दन्तान् हेमकक्षान् पद्मवर्णान् कुथा-वृतान् । शैलाभान् नित्यमत्तांश् च अभितः काम्यकं सरः ॥ दत्त्वैकैको दशशतान् कुञ्जरान् कवचावृतान् । क्षमावतः कुली-नांश् च द्वारेण प्राविशंस् ततः ॥ ) 2. 48. 17-20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 52. 20: ईषा-दन्तान् लाङ्गलतुल्यदन्तान्; हेमकक्षाः सुवर्णवस्त्राः); (4) Yudhiṣṭhira, in his pilgrimage with Lomaśa, went to the Kaliṅ-gas from the place where Gaṅgā meets the ocean; he went along the coast; Lomaśa pointed out the country to him (स सागरं समासाद्य गङ्गायाः संगमे नृप । … ततः समुद्रतीरेण जगाम … कलिङ्गान् प्रति); (एते कलिङ्गाः कौन्तेय) 3. 114. 2-4; (5) Drupada suggested to the Pāṇḍavas to send a messenger to the ruling prince of the Kaliṅgas, known for his arrogance in battle, to seek his help for war (कुमारश् च कलिङ्-गानाम् ईश्वरो युद्धदुर्मदः) 5. 4. 25; (6) Kṛṣṇa crushed the Kaliṅgas at Danta-kūra (तथा कलिङ्गान् दन्तकूरे ममर्द) 5. 47. 70; (7) Śikhaṇḍin had attacked the Kaliṅgas (यः कलिङ्गान् समापेदे पाञ्चालो युद्धदुर्मदः) 5. 49. 33; (8) The king of Kalingas, with his son Ketumant, joined the side of the Kauravas with sixty thousand chariot-fighters and an अयुत of elephant warriors (षष्ट्या रथसहस्रैस् तु नागानाम् अयुतेन च । पतिः सर्वकलिङ्गानां ययौ केतुमता सह) 6. 17. 32; (9) On the second day of the war, the Kaliṅga king and his army attacked Bhīma and an extre-mely fierce battle took place between them (कलिङ्गं समचोदयत् । … ततः सा महती सेना कलिङ्गानां … भीमम् अभ्युद्ययौ तूर्णं … ॥ ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तुमु-लं लोमहर्षणम् । कलिङ्गानां च समरे भीमस्य च … । जगतः प्रक्षयकरं घोररूपं भयानकम् ॥ ) 6. 49. 37-38, 40; 6. 50. 1-3; Bhīma met the sudden advance of the large force of the Kaliṅgas which was full of chariots, elephants and horses and fighting with large weapons (ताम् आपतन्तीम् सहसा कलिङ्गानां महा-चमूम् । रथनागाश्वकलिलां प्रगृहीत-महायुधाम् । ) 6. 50. 4-5; (रथैर् अनेक-साहस्रैः कलिङ्गानां जनाधिपः) 6. 50. 7; the battle was fierce 6. 50. 9-14; the large army of the Kaliṅgas and the Niṣādas was engaged with the small one of the Cedis (अल्पानां बहुभिः सह । कलिङ्गैः सह चेदीनां निषादईश् च) 6. 50. 14; when the Cedis retired, Bhīma did not leave the battle but showered arrows on the Kaliṅga army (सर्वैः कलिङ्गैर् आसन्नः संनि-वृत्तेषु चेदिषु । … न न्यवर्तत पाण्डवः  … शितैर् अवाकिरन् बाणैः कलिङ्गानां वरू-थिनीम् ॥ … योधयाम् आस कालिङ्गान्) 6. 50. 16-17, 19; the king of the Kaliṅgas obstructed Bhīma on all sides with his many thousands of chariots (कलिङ्गानां जनाधिपः । रथैर् अनेकसाहस्रैर् भीम-स्यावारयद् दिशः) 6. 50. 23; Bhīma frigh-tened the army of the Kaliṅgas by loud roars; the army thought him to be super-human (तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता कलिङ्गानां वरूथिनी न भीमं समरे मेने मानु-षम्) 6. 50. 33, 27; the fierce battle in which the king of the Kaliṅgas died des-cribed in 6. 50. 39-59; the Kaliṅga army, then led by Śrutāyus, attacked Bhīma (सा बहुला सेना कलिङ्गानाम् तरस्विनाम् । … भीमसेनम् उपाद्रवत्); (कलिङ्गसैन्या-नां प्रमुखे … श्रुतायुषम् अभिप्रेक्ष्य) 6. 50. 60-61; they used शक्ति, गदा, तोमर, ऋष्टि and परश्वध against Bhīma 6. 50. 71-72; Bhīma killed with his गदा first seven hundred of them (सप्तशतान् वीरान् 6. 50. 73) and then two thousand of them (द्विसाहस्रान् कलिङ्गान् … । प्राहिणोन् मृत्यु-लोकाय) 6. 50. 73-75; while fighting with Bhīma, the Kaliṅga army was confused and it trembled (मोहश् चापि कलिङ्गानाम् आविवेश  … प्राकम्पत च सैन्यानि) 6. 50. 77-78, 80; they fled, but returned again in groups (पुनर् आवर्तमानेषु विद्रवत्सु च सं-घशः) 6. 50. 81; Dhṛṣṭadyumna ordered his army to fight with the Kaliṅga warriors (सर्वकालिङ्गयोधेषु … युध्यध्वम्) 6. 50. 82; Dhṛṣṭadyumna went to help Bhīma who was attacked by the Kaliṅgas, (कलिङ्-गेषु चरन्तम् … कलिङ्गैः समभिद्रुतम्) 6. 50. 87, 90; Sātyaki saw both of them fighting with the Kaliṅgas; he himself killed some of the adversaries (कलिङ्गान् समरे वीरौ योधयन्तौ … जघान समरे परान्) 6. 50. 91, 93; Bhīma caused a river of blood rising from the fallen Kaliṅgas to flow between the army of the Kaliṅgas and of the Pāṇḍavas; it appeared as if it was Kāla fighting with the Kaliṅgas (कलिङ्गप्रभवां … रुधिरस्यन्दिनीम् तत्र भीमः प्रावर्तयन् नदीम् । अन्तरेण कलिङ्गानां पाण्डवानां च वाहिनीं … प्राक्रोशंस् तावका … । कालो ऽयं भीम-रूपेण कलिङ्गैः सह युध्यते ॥ ) 6. 50. 94-96; Bhīma succeeded in killing all the Kaliṅga warriors (स हत्वा सर्वकालिङ्गान्) 6. 50. 108; (कालिङ्गाश् च मृधे हताः) 6. 50. 112; Sātyaki congratulated Bhīma for pounding single-handed the महाव्यूह of Kaliṅgas (महाव्यूहः कलिङ्गानाम् एकेन मृदितस् त्वया) 6. 50. 113; (10) On the eleventh day of the war, Kaliṅga king stood (with his army) on the right side of Droṇa's Śakaṭavyūha (कलिङ्गश् च … दक्षि-णम् पार्श्वम् आस्थाय 7. 6. 2; अस्माकं शकटव्यूहः 7. 6. 15); (11) On the twelfth day of war, the Kaliṅgas were placed at the ‘neck’ and the ‘back’ of the Suparṇavyūha (7. 19. 4) of Droṇa (कलिङ्गाः … ग्रीवायाम् 7. 19. 7-8; पृष्ठे कलिङ्गाः 7. 19. 11); (12) On the four-teenth day of the war, Sātyaki while moving forward towards Arjuna, had to fight with the Kaliṅgas; he broke their resistance, went beyond their irresistible army, and reached Arjuna (ततः कलिङ्गैर् युयुधे  … तां च सेनाम् अतिक्रम्य कलिङ्गानाम् दुरत्ययाम्) 7. 116. 10-11; (13) During the night war on the fourteenth day, the brave Kaliṅga prince, with the Kaliṅga army, attacked Bhīma; he was killed by Bhīma with his fist (कलिङ्गानां च सैन्येन कलिङ्गस्य सुतो रणे 7. 130. 18; कलिङ्गानाम् तु तं शूरं … मुष्टिनाभि-जघान ह 7. 130. 20); (14) Kaliṅgas mentioned among those who ran away from the battle-field after the fall of Droṇa (कलिङ्गारट्टबाह्लिकैः) 7. 165. 79; (15) Karṇa in his earlier exploits had won the Kaliṅgas and made them pay tribute (कलिङ्गान् … यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 20; (16) On the sixteenth day of the war, Kaliṅgas rushed towards Arjuna to kill him (कलिङ्ग° … जिघांसवः पाण्डवम् अभ्यधावन्) 8. 12. 59; (17) On the same day, many warriors from different countries like Aṅga, Vaṅga etc., skilled in elephant warfare, along with the Kaliṅgas showered Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna with arrows, तोमरस् and नाराचस् (अङ्गा … गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः कलिङ्गैः सह … । शरतोमरनाराचैर् … सिषिचुस् ते … पाञ्चालाचलम् आहवे) 8. 17. 2-4; they later showered Nakula with arrows and तोमरस् to kill him (मेकलोत्कलोकालिङ्गा … शर-तोमरवर्षाणि विमुञ्चन्तो जिघांसवः) 8. 17. 20; (18) A voice in the mid-region, a week after Arjuna's birth, predicted that he was destined to win the Kaliṅgas (अयं जेता मद्रकलीङ्गकेकयान्) 8. 48. 7; (19) Arjuna told Yudhiṣṭhira that only Bhīma, who killed Kaliṅga warriors and their elephants, could find fault with him (Arjuna) (कलिङ्ग° … सदामदान् … । निहन्ति) 8. 49. 79; (20) Kaliṅgas men-tioned among those who fell on the battle-field during the first seventeen days of the war (कलिङ्गसहिता हताः) 8. 4. 37; (21) Before the गदायुद्ध, Kṛṣṇa reminded Bhīma that earlier Kaliṅgas and others were killed by him (कलिङ्गाः … त्वाम् आसाद्य महायुद्धे निहताः) 9. 32. 22; (22) While recalling Kṛṣṇa's earlier exploits, Vasudeva mentioned Kṛṣṇa's killing the Kaliṅgas (चक्रे काइइङ्गमागधान् (विदेहान्)) 16. 7. 10; Kṛṣṇa's victory over Kaliṅgas also mentioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra (कलिङ्गांश् च  … अजयद् रणे) 7. 10. 15. E. Some other events: (1) Once, kings had assembled for the स्वयंवर of the Kaliṅga princess in the Kaliṅga country of Citrāṅgada (this was attended by Duryodhana) (ततः कदाचिद् राजानः समाजग्मुः स्वयंवरे । कलिङ्ग-विषये … राज्ञश् चित्राङ्गदस्य ह ॥ ) 12. 4. 2; (2) Vārdhakṣemi fought and carried away the Kaliṅga girl (वार्धक्षेमिः कलिङ्-गानां यः कन्याम् आहरद् युधि) 7. 9. 51. [Perhaps this and the following two Kaliṅgas are meant by Trikaliṅga]

Kaliṅga2 m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas देशाः संकीर्तिताः 6. 10. 68) of the Bhārata-varṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (शूरसेनाः कलिङ्गाश् च) 6. 10. 38; these seem to be the Kaliṅgas of the mid-region and are to be distinguished from Kaliṅga1 and Kaliṅga3. [See Kaliṅga1, 3]

Kaliṅga3 m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: They probably lived in the north-west since they are listed by Saṃ-jaya along with Kāśmīras, Tukhāras and the Kirāta tribes (काश्मीराः … तुखारश् च  … ॥ … कलिङ्गाश् च किरातानां च जातयः । ।) 6. 10. 67. B. Characterization: (1) They were probably reckoned by Saṃjaya as म्लेच्छस् (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छाः) 6. 10. 63; (2) Bhīṣma counted Kaliṅgas among those who became degraded since they did not respect Brāhmaṇas (कलिङ्गाश् च … । … वृषलत्वं परिगता ब्राह्मणानां अदर्श-नात्) 13. 30. 20-21; (3) A certain Brāh-maṇa told the Kuru assembly that Kaliṅga people were to be avoided as they followed wrong धर्म (कलिङ्गान् … दुर्धर्मांश् च विवर्जयेत्) 8. 30. 45. [See Kaliṅga1, 2]
कल्कल: Kalkala m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas, (also called Deśas देशः सं-कीर्तिताः 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणाः) 6. 10. 56; (पुलिन्दाः कल्कलैः सह) 6. 10. 60.
कश्यपद्वीप: Kaśyapadvīpa nt: Name of a द्वीप। Two parts of the Sudarśanadvīpa are like a large hare; the Kaśyapadvīpa forms one of the two ‘ears’ of this hare (एवं सुदर्शनद्वीपो … । … द्विरंशे च शशो महान्) 6. 6. 15-16; (कर्णौ तु नागद्वीपं च कश्यपद्वीपम् एव च) 6. 7. 52.
कह्व: Kahva m. (pl.): Name of a people. According to king Māndhātṛ they lived in the countryside but led the life of Dasyus (कह्वाश् च … सर्वे विषयवासिनह् … सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः) 12. 65. 13, 15; he asked Indra the nature of their धर्म and how they were to be controlled by kings like him (कथं धर्मं चरेयुस् ते … मद्विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः … ) 12. 65. 15; Indra then told Māndhātṛ the धर्म of the Dasyus 12. 6. 17-21.
काक्ष: Kākṣa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. One of the (northern) Janapadas (also called Deśas (उद्देशमात्रेण मया देशाः संकीर्तिताः 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (काक्षाः सामुद्रनिष्कुटाः) 6. 10. 47.
कञ्च्य: Kañcya m. (pl.): Name of a people. Listed by Ulūka among those warriors who joined the army of Duryodhana (राज-चमूं समेताम् । … द्रविडान्ध्रकाञ्च्यैः) 5. 158. 19-20.
कानन: Kānana m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the third day of the war, Kānanas were stationed at the left wing of the Garuḍavyūha of the Kaurava army (गारु-डम् च महाव्यूहं चक्रे) 6. 52. 2; (काननाश् च … वामं पक्षम् उपाश्रिताः) 6. 52. 9.
कान्तीक: Kāntīka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas, also called Deśas (उद्देश-मात्रेण मया देशाः संकीर्तिताः 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56; (हृषी-विदर्भाः कान्तीकाः) 6. 10. 63.
कापिल: Kāpila nt.: Name of a Varṣa. One of the seven Varṣas of the Kuśa-dvīpa (सप्तमं कापिलं वर्षं सप्तैते वर्षपुञ्जकाः) 6. 13. 13, 9.
काम्बोज: Kāmboja m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people; their horses also referred to as Kāmboja. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the Mleccha people of the north (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … । यवनाश् च सकाम्बोजाः) 6. 10. 63-64; lived in the north (उत्तरापथजन्मानः … यौन-काम्बोजगान्धाराः) 12. 200. 40; (उदीच्य-काम्बोजशकैः) 5. 158. 20; in the north-east (दरदान् सह काम्बोजैर् अजयत् … ॥ प्रागुत्तरां दिशं ये च वसन्त्य् आश्रित्य दस्यवः) 2. 24. 22-23; capital town Rāja-pura (कर्ण राजपुरं गत्वा काम्बोजा निहतास् त्वया) 7. 4. 4; around Mathurā (?) (यवनकाम्बोजा मथुराम् अभितश् च ये) 12. 102. 5. B. King and princes of this country: King Sudakṣiṇa of Kāmboja country referred to as Kāmboja (काम्बोजश् च सुदक्षिणः) 7. 19. 10; (काम्बजं च सुदक्षिणम्) 8. 50. 51; (काम्बोजं निह-तं दृष्ट्वा) 7. 125. 21; Sudakṣiṇa's younger brother (सुदक्षिणाद् अवरजम् काम्बोजम्) 8. 40. 106; referred to as the great warrior of the Kāmbojas (काम्बोजानां महा-रथम्) 6. 43. 63, 65. C. Famous for its horses: (1) Their description: (i) Exce-llent (परमवाजिनः) 13. 119. 12; (पर-मकाम्बोजैः) 7. 22. 35; 10. 13. 1; (अश्व-वर) 7. 35. 39; (ii) fast moving (जवन) 7. 22. 35; 7. 35. 36; (शीघ्रगामिन्) 10. 13. 9; (iii) wearing gold garlands (हेममालिन्) 7. 22. 35; 10. 13. 1; (iv) white (श्वेत) 2. 49. 5; (v) drawing carriages well (शाधु-वाहिन्) 7. 35. 36; (2) Their importance: One who gave a hundred Kāmboja horses to a Brāhmaṇa was freed of sins (शतं वै यस् तु काम्बोजान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रय-च्छति । … स च पापात् प्रमुच्यते 12. 36. 11. D. Characteristics of the people: (1) Classed as Mlecchas (यवनाश् च सकाम्बोजा … म्लेच्छजातयः) 6. 10. 64; mentioned among the Mleccha kings on this earth towards the end of the Kali-yuga (बहवो म्लेच्छराजानः … काम्बो-जाः) 3. 186. 29-30; 24, 27; called Dasyus (सह काम्बोजैर् … ये च … दस्यवः) 2. 24. 23-24; (2) Appearance: Their hair was shorn (मुण्डान् एतान् … । … काम्बोजान् । … मुण्डानीके हते) 7. 95. 20-21; (3) Non-believers: They did not believe in Bhūtapati being the superinten-dent of the world (निरध्यक्षांस् … । … यौनकाम्बोजगान्धाराः) 12. 200. 38, 40; (4) Behaviour: Cruel (दारुण) 6. 10. 64; sinful (पापकृत्) 12. 200. 41; (पाप) 3. 186. 29; teaching false beliefs (मिथ्यानु-शासिन्) 3. 186. 29; given to falsehood (मृषा-वादपरायण) 3. 186. 29; they lead the life of dogs, crows, बलस् (a kind of crow ?) and vultures (श्वकाकबलगृध्राणां सधर्माणः) 12. 200. 41; they roamed around the whole earth (चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम्) 12. 200. 41; they did not exist in the Kṛta age, but were to be met with from the Tretā age onwards (नैते कृतयुगे तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । त्रेताप्रभृति वर्तन्ते) 12. 200. 42. E. Warriors: Brave (शूर) 7. 87. 43; 7. 88. 54; respected by the brave in war (संग्रामे शूरसंमताः) 7. 66. 39; irresistible (दुर्वारण) 7. 87. 42; their army was invincible in war (दुर्जयं युधि) 7. 95. 45; watchful (अप्रमत्त) 7. 87. 45; who learnt the sciences, and were proficient in the science of archery (कृतविद्याश् च धनुर्-वेदे च निष्ठिताः) 7. 87. 43; keeping close to each other, they sought the welfare of each other (in war) (संहताश् च भृशं ह्य् एते अन्योन्यस्य हितैषिणः) 7. 87. 43; cruel and arrogant in battles (क्रूरकर्-माणः काम्बोजा युद्धदुर्मदाः) 7. 95. 12; while fighting, they were irritated like ser-pents (क्रुद्धैर् आशीविषोपमैः) 7. 87. 48; they had a variety of arms and they fought with different weapons (नानाशस्त्र-समावापैर् विविधायुधयोधिभिः) 7. 87. 48; the banners on their chariots were golden (रथिनः काञ्चनध्वजाः) 7. 87. 42; they were proficient in close combats (नियुद्धकुशलाः) 12. 102. 5 (however, Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 101. 5: नियुद्धं बाहु-युद्धम्). F. Epic events: (1) Arjuna in his conquest of the north-east conquer-ed the Kāmbojas (दरदान् सह काम्बोजैर् अजयत् पाकशासनिः) 2. 24. 22; (2) Suda-kṣiṇa yoked white Kāmboja horses to Yudhiṣṭhira's chariot (सुदक्षिणस् तं युयुजे श्वेतैः काम्बोजजैर् हयैः) 2. 49. 5; (3) Mentioned among those to whom messengers were to be sent for help in war (दूता गच्छन्तु शीघ्रगाः ॥ … काम्-बोजा ऋषिका ये च … एतेषाम् प्रेष्यतां शीघ्रम्) 5. 4. 8, 15, 25; (4) They joined the army of Duryodhana (राजच-मुं समेताम् । … गुप्तां … उदीच्यकाम्बो-जशकैः) 5. 158. 19-20; (5) On the sixth day of the war, Kāmbojas were stationed at the head of the Krauñca vyūha (काम्बोजारट्टबाह्लिकैः । शिरस्य् आसीत्) 6. 71. 16, 14; (6) On the eighth day of the war, many Kāmbojas accompanied Trigarta (Suśarman) (त्रिगर्तः प्रस्थलाधिपः ॥ काम्बोजैर् बहुभिः सार्धं) 6. 83. 10; (7) On the eleventh day of the war, Kām-bojas stood at the extremity of the left side of the Śakaṭavyūha of the Kaura-vas (तेषां प्रपक्षाः काम्बोजाह्) 7. 6. 5, (सव्यं पार्श्वं) 4, (अस्माकं शकट-व्यूहः) 15; (8) On the twelfth day of the war, Kāmbojas were stationed at the neck of the Suparṇa vyūha (यवनकाम्-बोजाः … ग्रीवायाम्) 7. 19. 7-8, (व्यूहं दृष्ट्वा सुपर्णं तु) 4; (9) On the twelfth day of the war, Kāmboja horses were yoked to the chariots of Satyadhṛti, Śreṇimant, Vasudāna, and Kāśyaputra (युक्तैः परमकाम्बोजैः) 7. 22. 34-35; (10) On the thirteenth day of the war, Abhimanyu killed many excellent Kāmboja horses whose straps (?) and armours were cut off (काम्बोजारट्टबाह्लिकान् … निकृत्त-वर्मकवचान् … अश्ववरान्) 7. 35. 36, 39; they were mounted by warriors who were well-trained (स्वारूढाञ् शिक्षितैर् योधैः) 7. 35. 37; their tails, ears and eyes were steady (स्थिरवालधिकर्णाक्षान्) 7. 35. 36; their pitiable plight, when they fell down, described in 7. 35. 37-39; (11) On the fourteenth day of the war, Arjuna, while rushing towards Jayadratha, was checked by Kāmbojas and others (काम्बोजा-नां च ये गणाः । … अवारयन्) 7. 66. 38, 41; Arjuna attacked their army (अभ्यगात्  … काम्बोजानाम् अनीकिनीम्) 7. 67. 26; (12) Sātyaki expected to face them while trying to reach Arjuna (काम्बोजैर् हि समेष्यामि) 7. 87. 48; he did encounter their large army of brave warriors who tried to obstruct him (युयुधानो ऽपि … प्रययौ … काम्बोजानां महाचमूम् ॥ स तत्र बहुभिः शूरैः संनिरुद्धो महारथैः) 7. 88. 53-54; they wore armours, were well-equipped and fought with bows and arrows; they were led by Suyodhana (सतनुत्राणाः सुयोधन-पुरोगमाः ॥ दंशिताः … काम्बोजा … । शर-बाणासनधराः) 7. 95. 11-12; Sātyaki asked his charioteer to drive him to Kām-bojas; he wanted to kill the warriors whose heads were shorn of hair and show his prowess to the Kauravas (चोदयाश्वान् असंभ्रमम् । … यत्रैते … काम्बोजा … ) 7. 95. 1, 5, 12; मुण्दान् एतान् हनिष्यामि … काम्बोजान् एव मां वह । अद्य द्रक्ष्यन्ति मे वीर्यं कौरवाः … । मुण्डानीके हते सुत) 7. 95 20-21; Sātyaki killed thousands of them and put the rest to flight (काम् बोजानां सहस्रैस् तु … अगम्यरूपां पृथिवीं … कृतवांस् तत्र शैनेयः … ॥ … काम्बोजसैन्यं विद्राव्य) 7. 95. 38, 39, 45; Sātyaki went beyond the Kāmboja army; after defeating them, he reached Arjuna (तीर्त्वा … काम्बोजानां च वाहि-नीम्; जित्वा यवनकाम्बोजान्) 7. 96. 8, 1; Duryodhana led the Kāmbojas to attack Sātyaki once more (दुर्योधन-पुरोगमाः । शकाः काम्बोजबाह्लीका … ॥ … अभ्यद्रवन्त शैनेयम्) 7. 97. 12, 13, 17; (13) Bhīma too went beyond the army of the Kāmbojas to reach Arjuna (अति-क्रम्य काम्बोजानां च वाहिनीम्) 7. 103. 22; (14) On the sixteenth day of the war, the Kāmbojas were among those who were stationed at the extremity of the left side of the Bārhaspatya vyūha (तेषां प्रपक्षः काम्बोजाः) 8. 31. 15, (वामं पार्श्वम्) 8. 31. 14, (बार्हस्पत्यः … महा-व्यूहः) 8. 31. 26; (15) On the seven-teenth day of the war, while fighting with the Saṃśaptakas, Arjuna, when he attacked the extremity of the side guarded by the Kāmbojas, killed many of them; he killed the Kāmboja prince, the younger brother of Sudakṣiṇa; but the Kāmbojas conti-nued their fight with Arjuna (प्रपक्षं स समासाद्य पार्थः काम्बोजरक्षितम् । प्रममाथ बलाद् बाणैर्; ततो ऽभवत् पुनर् युद्धम् … काम्बोजैः) 8. 40. 100, 107-108; (16) On the same day, during the fight between Karṇa and Arjuna, Kām-bojas attacked Arjuna; they were equipp-ed with excellent weapons; Arjuna killed them (अथाभ्यधावंस् त्वरिताः … सहैव काम्बोजवरैर् … वरायुधान् … धनं-जयः शत्रुगणं तम् अक्षिणोत्) 8. 64. 16-17; (17) Mentioned by Saṃjaya among those who were alive after the death of Karṇa (नदीजकाम्बोजवनायु-बाह्लिकैः) 8. 4. 96; (18) On the last day of the war, Aśvathāman, together with the Kāmbojas stood at the back of the Vyūha (not named) (प्र्ष्ठतो ऽभूत् काम्बोजैः परिवारितः) 9. 7. 25; (19) At the end of the war, all Kāmbojas were killed— Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra (हताः सर्वे काम्बोजाश् च) 9. 1. 26; (20) When the Pāṇḍavas started to reach Bhīma who had left to kill Aśvathāman, excellent Kām-boja horses, wearing golden garlands, were yoked to the chariot of Kṛṣṇa (युक्तं परमकाम्बोजैस् तुरगैर् हेममालिभिः) 10. 13. 1; (21) Gāndhārī showed to Kṛṣṇa the dead body of Jayadratha watched over by Kāmboja and other women (तम् एताः पर्युपासन्ते रक्षमाणा महाभु-जम् । … °काम्बोजयवनस्त्रियः) 11. 22. 11. G. Events referred to but not reported in the epic: (1) Karṇa's victory over the Kāmbojas mentioned by Saṃjaya (काम्बो-जानां च ये गणाः । कर्णेन विजिताः पूर्-वं संग्रामे शूरसंमताः) 7. 66. 38-39; the feat also referred to by Bhīṣma (काम्बोजा निहतास् त्वया) 7. 4. 4; by Śalya (°काम्बोजास् … जिताः संख्ये सुदुर्जयाः) 8. 57. 31; (2) Kṛṣṇa had once defeated the Kāmbojas (काम्बोजान् … जितवान् पुण्द-रीकाक्षः) 7. 10. 17-18. H. Other event: The Kīṭa (a worm), when he became a prince, rode in chariots drawn by excellent Kāmboja horses (वहन्ति माम् … स्यन्द-नेषु च काम्बोजा युक्ताः परमवाजिनः) 13. 119. 12.
कायव्य: Kāyavya m. (pl.): Name of a people. Probably lived in the north-west; the Kṣatriyas among them brought wealth by hundreds as tribute for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (कायव्या दरदा … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 12, 16.
कारस्कर: Kāraskara m. (pl.): Name of a people. Duryodhana saw Kāraskaras and some other peoples in the residence of Yudhi-ṣṭhira as if they were made slaves and were under his control (आवर्जिता इवाभान्ति निघ्नाश्  … । कारस्करा … युधिष्टिरनिवेशने) 2. 46. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 50. 20: आवर्जिताः दासवद् वशगाः); a certain Rākṣasī told a pilgrim that one should avoid Kāraskaras who followed wrong धर्म (कारस्करान्  … दुर्धर्मांश् च विवर्जयेत् ॥ इति तीर्था-नुसर्तारं राक्षसी काचिद् अब्रवीत्) 8. 30. 45-46.
कारूषक: Kārūṣaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. The Dānavas called Krodhavaśagaṇa were born on the earth as kings among the Kārūṣakas (कारूषकाश् च राजानः … गणात् क्रोधवशाद् एवं राजपूगो ऽभवत् क्षितौ) 1. 61. 59, 61, 54.
कार्पासिक: Kārpāsika m.: Designation of a (cotton-growing ?) country. Those who lived in Bharukaccha brought as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira a hundred thousand Dāsīs living in the Kārpāsika country; they were dark, slender, long-haired, wearing gold ornaments and belonging to the Śūdra class (शतं दासीसहस्राणाम् कार्पासिकनिवासिनाम् । श्या-मास् तन्व्यो दीर्घकेश्यो हेमाभरणभू-षिताः । शूद्रा … ॥ बलिं च कृत्स्नम् आदाय भरुकच्छनिवासिनः । उपनिन्युः) 2. 47. 7-8.
कार्षिक: Kārṣika m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada (known for agriculture ?). Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (तथा माहिषकार्षिकाः) 6. 10. 45 (or do we have to treat माहिषकार्षिक as one word ?).
कालतोयक: Kālatoyaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (आभीराः कालतोयकाः) 6. 10. 45.
कालमुख: Kālamukha m. (pl.): Name of a people. They sprung from the Rākṣasas; Saha-deva in his expedition to the south (प्र-ययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; दक्षिणा-भिमुखो ययौ 2. 28. 8; प्रायाद् … दक्षि-णां दिशम् 2. 28. 37) before the Rājasūya defeated them (ये च कालमुखा नाम नरा राक्षसयोनयः । … वशे चक्रे महा-मतिः) 2. 28. 45-46.
काश: Kāśa m. (pl.): Name of a people. People in the kingdoms of different Kṣatriyas became Vṛṣalas due to non-regard for Brāhmaṇas and due to their not following the Kṣatriya धर्म; these were Dramiḍas, Kāśas etc (प्रजा वृषलतां प्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात् ॥ त एते द्रमिडाः काशाः … । वृषलत्वं परिगता व्युत्थानात् क्षत्रधर्मतः) 14. 29. 15-16; (द्रमिडा काशा … । … तास् ताः क्षत्रियजात-यः । वृषलत्वम् अनुप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 35. 17-18.
काशि: Kāśi m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; the people also referred to as Kāśika (7. 23. 7; 8. 4. 74), or Kāśya (8. 8. 19); often mentioned along with Kosalas or with Cedis and Karūṣas. A. Location: (1) Listed by Saṃjaya among the (northern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कुन्तलाः काशिकोशलाः) 6. 10. 38; (2) Listed by Saṃjaya a second time (सौधा मद्रा भुजिङ्गाश् च काशयो ऽपरकाशयः) 6. 10. 40; (are these two neighbouring Janapadas, the former being to the east, while the latter to the west ?) B. Characteristics: (1) The Kāśi warriors were famous as great chariot-fighters (महारथाः समाख्याताः), of noble lineage (कुलपुत्राः), having golden banners (सुवर्णविकृतध्वजाः), not turn-ing back, ready to die in battles (अपरा-वर्तिनः, तनुत्यजः) 6. 102. 17; (2) A certain Brāhmaṇa told the Kuru assem-bly (8. 30. 7, 34, 58) that the people of Kāśi knew what the eternal धर्म was (कोसलाः काशयो ऽङ्गाश् च … धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्) 8. 30. 60-61. C. Epic events: (1) Bhīṣma defeated the Kāśi and other warriors and brought for Vicitra-vīrya two Kāśi princesses (अहं विचित्र-वीर्याय द्वे कन्ये समुदावहम् । जित्वा … काशीन् अथ च कोसलान् ॥ ) 13. 44. 37; (2) When Pāṇḍu marched out for the conquest of the earth he made Kurus famous among the Kāśi people (तथा काशिषु … कुरूणाम् अकरोद् यशः) 1. 105. 12; (3) At the birth of Arjuna an incorporeal voice declared that he would subdue the people of Kāśi and enhance the fame of Kurus (वाग् उवाचाशरीरिणी … एष … वशे कृत्वा … चेदि-काशिकरूषांस् च कुरुलक्ष्म सुधास्यति) 1. 114. 28-31; (4) According to Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, Sahadeva had conquered the Kāśi people in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya (यः काशीन् … युधाजयत्) 5. 49. 28 (this event is not reported earlier at 2. 28. 48); (5) They joined the side of the Pāṇḍavas against Duryodhana (काशयश् चेदयश् चैव) 5. 56. 33: (6) The Kāśi warriors were already on the side of Yudhiṣṭhira when he had proposed to come to terms with Duryodhana in lieu of five villages (काशिभिश् चेदिपाञ्चालैर् … । भवता चैव नाथेन पञ्च ग्रामा वृता मया) 5. 70. 14; (7) But Duryodhana informed Dhṛtarāṣṭra that he had won over the Kāśi warriors on his side (अर्धं मे केकया लब्धाः काशिकाः कोसलाश् च ये) 7. 23. 7 (so these could mean a part of the Kāśi warriors on his side against the others who joined the Pāṇḍavas; or the division may be according as they belonged to Kāśi and Aparakāśi); (8) Yudhiṣṭhira asked the leaders of the Cedi, Kāśi and Karūṣa armies to move towards Kuru-kṣetra (चेदिकाशिकरूषाणाम्) 5. 197. 2; (9) On the first day of the war, Bhīṣma's palm-marked banner was seen moving among the Kāśi warriors (चेदिकाषिकरूषेषु  … बहुधा तालश् चरन् केतुर् अदृश्यत) 6. 45. 4; (10) On the third day of the war, the Kāśis, led by Dhṛṣṭaketu, were stationed on the right side of the Ardhacandravyūha (6. 52. 10) of the Pāṇḍavas (चेदिकाशिकरू-षैश् च … अभिसंवृतः) 6. 52. 13; (11) On the ninth day of the war, fourteen thousand warriors of Cedis, Kāśis and Karūṣas attac-ked Bhīṣma and perished along with their horses, elephants and chariots (चेदिकाशिक-रूषाणाम् सहस्राणि चतुर्दश । … निमग्नाः परलोकाय सवाजिरथकुञ्जराः ॥ ) 6. 102. 17-18; the result of their battle with Bhīṣma described in 6. 102. 16, 20-23; (12) Same description occurs for the tenth day of the war 6. 112. 73; (13) Defeating Kāśis mentioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra as one of the exploits of Kṛṣṇa (काशिकोसलान् । … अजयद् रणे) 7. 10. 15; (14) Kṛṣṇa while recount-ing the exploits of Bhīṣma during the first ten days of the war mentioned his having killed the Kāśis (स चेदिकाशिपाञ्चालान् … ।  … निधनम् अनयत्) 8. 51. 27; (15) Abhibhū, the king of Kāśi, who was pro-tected by many Kāśi warriors, was killed by the son of Vasudāna (अभिभूः काशिराजश् च काशिकैर् बहुभिर् वृतः । वसुदानस्य पुत्रेण न्यासितो देहम् आहवे) 8. 4. 74; (16) Karṇa's former victory over the Kāśis mentioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra to Saṃ-jaya (यश् चाजैषीद् … ॥ … काशिकोसलान्) 8. 5. 18-19; (17) On the fifteenth day of the war, Kāśi warriors mentioned among those who rushed at the Kaurava army; in the middle of their army was Bhīma-sena; the chariot-riders, the elephant-riders and excellent foot-soldiers, delighted in making different sounds; they laughed and danced (काश्या मागधाश् चापि दुद्रुवुः ॥ तेषां रथाश् च नागाश् च प्रवराश् चापि पत्तयः । नानाविधरवैर् हृष्टा नृत्यन्ति च हसन्ति च ॥ तस्य सैन्यस्य महतो … मध्यं वृकोदरो ऽब्यागात्) 8. 8. 19-21; (18) The army of the Kāśis, Kosalas and Matsyas consisted of Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras; they fought with Kṛpa and others on the seventeenth day of the war and got killed (कृपश् च … कृतवर्मा च । कोसलैः काशिमत्स्यैश् च … । … युयु-धुर् … ॥ तेषां अन्तकरं युद्धम् … । शूद्रविट्क्षत्रवीराणाम्) 8. 32. 16-18; (19) On the same day, Kāśi warriors were among those who checked the progress of Vasuṣeṇa (काशिकोसलाः । एते च त्वरिता वीरा वसुषेणम् अवारयन् ॥ ) 8. 33. 22; (20) The Aśvamedha sacrifice horse went to Kāśi, Andhra and Kosala countries (स तुरगोत्तमः । काशीन् अन्ध्रान् कोसलांश् च) 14. 84. 4. D. Past events: (1) Har-yaśva, grand-father of Divodāsa, ruled over Kāśi (काशिष्व् अपि नृपो राजन् दिवोदासपिता-महः । हर्यश्व इति विख्यातः) 13. 31. 10; (2) Later, Divodāsa, son of Bhīmasena, became the king of Kāśi (काशिनाम् ईश्वरः प्रभुः । दिवोदास इति ख्यातो भैमसेनिर् नराधिप) 5. 115. 1 (in 13. 31. 15, Divo-dāsa is said to be the son of Sudeva (सौदे-विस् त्व् अथ काशीशो दिवोदासो ऽभ्यषिच्यत); (3) Vītahavya's sons had plundered the Kāśi country of its store of jewels (उत्सादि-तश् च विषयः काशीनां रत्नसंचयः) 13. 31. 47.
काश्मीर: Kāśmīra m. (pl.): Name of a people, also referred to as Kāśmīraka (2. 24. 16; 7. 10. 16); the Janapada called Kāśmīra-maṇḍala (3. 130. 10; 13. 26. 8). A. Location: Counted by Saṃjaya among the (northern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; counted by Saṃjaya also among the northern म्लेच्छ people (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … । शूद्रा-भीराथ दरदाः काश्मीराः पशुभिः सह) (those who live in forest ?) 6. 10. 63, 66; Arjuna conquered the Kāśmīra people in his expedition to the north (प्रययाव् उत्तरां तस्माद् दिशं धनदपालिताम्) 2. 24. 1; near the river Vipāśā (एषा रम्या विपाशा च नदी … काश्मीरमण्डलं चैतत्) 3. 130. 8, 10; the rivers flowing through the region of Kāśmīra meet the Mahānada Sindhu (काश्मीरमण्डले नद्यो याः पतन्ति महानदम् । ता नदीः सिन्धुम् आसाद्य) 13. 26. 8. B. Holy character: All the Kāśmīra region is holy and is in-habited by great sages (काश्मीरमण्डलं चैतत् सर्वपुण्यम् अरिंदम । महर्षिभिश् चाध्युषितम्) 3. 130. 10; it is said in the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras to Gau-tama (13. 26. 3-4) that a man of good character visiting the rivers of Kāśmīra and Sindhu goes to heaven (ता नदीः सिन्-धुम् आसाद्य शीलवान् स्वर्गम् आप्नुयात्) 13. 26. 8; but the Kāśmīra people also counted among the northern म्लेच्छस् 6. 10. 66. C. Epic events: (1) Arjuna conquered the Kṣatriya warriors from Kāśmīra in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya (ततः काश्मीरकान् वीरान् क्षत्रियान् … । व्यजयत्) 2. 24. 16; (2) The Kṣatriya chiefs of Kāśmīra brought wealth in hundreds as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya (काश्मीराः … राज-न्या … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो … ) 2. 48. 13, 16; (3) Pointed out by Lomaśa to Yudhiṣṭhira during their pilgrimage (काश्मीरमण्डलं चैतत्) 3. 130. 10; (4) Kṛṣṇa had defeated the Kāśmīra warriors (काश्मीरकान् … जितवान्) 7. 10. 16, 18. D. Past event: In Kāśmīramaṇḍala a dialogue once took place between Agni and all northern sages, Nāhuṣa and Kāśyapa (काश्मीरमण्डलं चैतत् … ॥ अत्रोत्तरा-णां सर्वेषाम् ऋषीणां नाहुषस्य च । अग्नेश् चात्रैव संवादः काश्यपस्य च भारत) 3. 130. 10-11; (Nī on Bom. Ed. 3. 130. 10-11: औत्तराणाम् औदीच्यानाम्).
कश्यप: Kaśyapa m. (pl.): Name of a group of ascetics, descendants of Kaśyapa. A. Characteristic: They were rec-koned among the best Brāhmaṇas of the whole world (सर्वस्य जगतः श्रेष्ठा ब्राह्मणाः) 3. 27. 8. B. Epic events: (1) Mentioned by Baka Dālbhya among those Brāhmaṇa ascetics (ब्राह्मणानां तपस्विनाम् 3. 27. 6) who, protected by Yudhiṣṭhira in the Dvaitavana forest (वसत्स्व् अथ द्वैतवने 3. 27. 1), observed vows and practised धर्म (चरन्ति धर्-मं पुण्ये ऽस्मिंस् त्वया गुप्ता धृतव्र-ताः । … वासिष्थाः काश्यपैः सह) 3. 27. 7; (2) Lomaśa introduced to Yudhiṣṭhira Kāśyapas among the ascetics who were present on Mahendra mountain; Yudhiṣṭhira with his brothers honoured all of them (तापसानां परं चक्रे सत्कारं भ्रा-तृभिः सह ॥ लोमशश् चास्य तान् सर्वान् आचख्यौ तत्र तापसान् । … वासिष्ठान् अथ काश्यपान् ॥ ) 3. 115. 1-2.
कितव: Kitava m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; often mentioned along with Sauvīras. A. Location and their way of life: They are characterized as a Janapada (कितवाः … द्वादशैते जनपदाः) 6. 18. 13-14; 6. 114. 76-77; they lived near the ocean and along the rivers and lived on wild grain that grew of its own accord due to rain water, or along the river side (इन्द्र-कृष्टैर् वर्तयन्ति धान्यैर् नदीमुखैश् च ये । समुद्रनिष्कुटे जाताः परिसिन्धु च मानवाः ॥ … वङ्गाश् च कितवैः सह) 2. 47. 9-10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 11: समुद्रसमी पस्थनिष्कुटे गृहोद्याने समु-द्रनिष्कुटे । इन्द्रकृष्टैः इन्द्रेणैवाकृष्टैः न तु कर्षणादिक्षेत्रियकयत्नापेक्षैः वनधान्यैः वृष्ट्यभावे तु नदीमुखैः नदीप्रभवैः). B. Characteristics: Brave and ready to give life in war (सर्वे शूरास् तनुत्यजः) 6. 18. 14. C. Epic events: (1) As tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya, Kitavas brought various kinds of jewels, goats and sheep, cows and gold, donkeys and camels, wines made from fruits, and different varieties of blankets; they were not allowed to enter through the gate (वङ्गाश् च कितवैः सह । विविधं बलिम् आदाय रत्नानि विविधानि च ॥ अजाविकं गोहिरण्यं खरोष्ट्रं फलजं मधु । कम्बलान् विविधांश् चैव द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ ) 2. 47. 10-11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 12: फलजं मधूकादिजातीयम्); (2) Kitavas are mentioned among those who accompanied Duḥśāsana and his brothers who acted as rearguards of Bhīṣma on the first day of the war (पृष्ठगोपास् तु भीष्म-स्य पुत्रास् तव नराधिप । … दुःशासनो … तथैषाम् अनुयायिनः । … सौवीराः कितवाः) 6. 18. 10-13; (3) Kitavas were among those who, although they were being killed by sharp arrows, did not abandon Bhīṣma on the ninth day of the war (सौवीराः कितवाः … संग्रामे नाजहुर् भीष्मं वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः ॥ ) 6. 102. 7; (4) Kitavas were among the twelve Jana-padas who, on the tenth day of the war, did not abandon Bhīṣma fighting with Arjuna although they were injured by arrows and were distressed by wounds (सौवी-राः कितवाः … द्वादशैते जनपदाः शरार्ता व्रणपीडिताः । संग्रामे न जहुर् भीष्मं युध्यमानं किरीटिना) 6. 114. 76; (5) On the eleventh day of the war, when the Kaurava army was arranged in a Śakaṭa-vyūha (7. 6. 15), the Kitavas stood at the extreme end of the left side which was led by Duryodhana; they stood immediately behind Karṇa (सव्यं पार्श्वम् अपालयन् ॥ तेषां प्रपक्षाः … सौवीराः कितवाः … तवात्मजं पुरस्कृत्य सूतपुत्रस्य पृष्ठ-तः ॥ ) 7. 6. 4-5, 7.
किरात: Kirāta m. (pl.): Name of a mountain tribe of hunters. A. Location: (1) Listed by Saṃjaya among the various northern tribes of the Bhāratavarṣa; they probably occupied different regions since Saṃjaya has listed them thrice (पुण्ड्रा भार्गाः किराताश् च) 6. 10. 49; (किराता बर्बराः) 6. 10. 55; (उत्तराश् चापरे … किरातानां च जातयः) 6. 10. 63, 67; listed also by Bhīṣma as northerners (उत्तरापथजन्मानः कीर्तयि-ष्यामि तान् अपि । … किराता बर्बरैः सह) 12. 200. 40; (2) The large country of Subāhu on Himavant mountain was throng-ed by Kirātas and Taṅgaṇas (सुबाहोर् विषयं महत् । … किराततङ्गणाकीर्णम् … । हिमवति) 3. 141. 24-25; on the other side of the Himavant, near the mountain of sun-rise, on the shore of Vāriṣeṇa ocean and around Lohitya (Brahmaputra) river (ये परार्धे हिमवतः सूर्योदयगिरौ नृपाः । वारिषेणसमुद्रान्ते लोहित्यम् अभितश् च ये । … किराताः) 2. 48. 8; the inaccessible parts on the Himavant mountain was the place of residence of the Kirātas (किरात-किंनरावासं शैलं शिखरिणां वरम्) 3. 88. 17; (हिमवद्दुर्गनिलयाः) 7. 4. 6; (3) On the Indra mountain, near the Videha country (वैदेहस्थस् तु कौन्तेय इन्द्रपर्वतम् अन्तिकात् । किरातानाम् अधि-पतीन् व्यजयत् … पाण्डवः) 2. 27. 13. B. Origin: They were produced in ancient times by Vasiṣṭha's cow Nandinī from her foam when Viśvāmitra forcibly tried to take her away (पुण्ड्रान् किरातान् … फेनतः सा ससर्ज ह ॥ ) 1. 165. 36; they are, how-ever, reputed to have their origin from fire (सर्वे चैवाग्नियोनयः) 7. 87. 30. C. Characteristics: (1) Arrogant while fight-ing (युद्धदुर्मद) 7. 87. 30, 32: rough in battle (रणकर्कश) 7. 4. 6; of fierce prowess (उग्रविक्रम) 8. 51. 19; hostile (विकृत) 14. 72. 24; they have a collection of different kinds of weapons and they fight with them; when they strike, they act like poison (नानाशस्त्रसमावापैर् विविधा-युधयोधिभिः । किरातैश् च समेष्यामि विषकल्पैः प्रहारिभिः) 7. 87. 49; they fight with swords and bows (असिधनुर्-धर) 14. 72. 24; their army shone like a Karṇikāra forest full of Kāñcana trees (काञ्चनैर् इव संवृतान् । … बलम् … कर्णिकारवनं यथा) 5. 19. 15; they were always fondled by Duryodhana and they sought his welfare (लालितैः सततं राज्ञा दुर्योधनहितैषिभिः) 7. 87. 49; they were expert in training elephants and they fought from elephant-backs; their elephants used to be protected by armours (नागान् … । … वर्मसंछन्नान् किरातैः समधिष्ठि-तान् ॥ … तेषाम् एते महामात्राः किराता … हस्तिशिक्षाविदश् चैव) 7. 87. 27, 30; (2) they were eaters of fruits and roots and they wore skins (फलमूलाशना ये च किराताश् चर्मवाससः) 2. 48. 8; (3) They were included by Bhīṣma among those Kṣatri-yas who were degraded due to their non-respect for Brāhmaṇas (किराता … तास् ताः क्षत्रियजातयः । वृषलत्वम् अनुप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 35. 18; they were sinful and lived the life of dogs, crows, बलस् (a kind of crow ?) and vultures; they did not exist in the Kṛtayuga but exist since the Tretāyuga (एते पापकृतस् तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । श्वकाकबल-गृध्राणां सधर्माणो नराधिप ॥ नैते कृतयुगे तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । त्रे-ताप्रभृति वर्तन्ते ते जना … ) 12. 200. 41-42; some of them apparently lived on country side but they lived like दस्युस्; Māndhātṛ asked Indra what was the धर्म of the Kirātas and how they should be governed by kings like him (कथं धर्-मं चरेयुस् ते सर्वे विषयवासिनः) मद्विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः) 12. 65. 15; Indra then told Māndhātṛ the धर्म of the Dasyus 12. 65. 17-22; Bhīṣma included the Kirātas among those northern people who did not believe in Dhātṛ (12. 200. 33) or Bhūtapati (12. 200. 38) as being the superintendent of all beings (निरध्यक्षांस् तु कौन्तेय कीर्त-यिष्यामि तान् अपि … किराता बर्बरैः सह) 12. 200. 38, 40. D. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa told Yudhiṣṭhira that the King of the Cedis was known as Pauṇḍraka Vāsudeva among the Kirātas and others (वङ्गपुण्ड्र-किरातेषु … । पौण्ड्रको वासुदेवेति यो ऽसौ लोकेषु विश्रुतः) 2. 13. 19; (2) Arjuna, in his expedition before the Rājasūya, fought with Kirātas and Cīnas, who had joined King Bhagadatta of Prāgjyotiṣa (स किरातैश् च चीनैश् च वृतः) 2. 23. 19; (3) Bhīma, in his expedition to the east before the Rājasūya, defeated seven chiefs of the Kirātas (किरातानाम् अधिपतीन् व्यज-यत् सप्त पाण्डवः) 2. 27. 13; (4) The kings of Kirātas, who brought as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya loads of sandal-wood and aloe and heaps of कालीयक, as also large quantities of hides, jewels, gold and perfumes, an अयुत of Kirāta Dāsīs, charming exotic animals and birds, and ex-tremely brilliant gold collected from moun-tains, were halted at the gate (चन्दना-गुरुकाष्ठानां भारान् कालीयकस्य च । चर्मरत्नसुवर्णानां गन्धानां चैव राशयः ॥ कैरातिकानाम् अयुतं दासीनां च … । आहृत्य रमणीयार्थान् दूरजान् मृगपक्षिणः ॥ निचितं पर्वतेभ्यश् च हिरण्यं भूरिवर्चसम् । बलिं च कृत्स्नम् आदाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ ) 2. 48. 9-11; the kings of Kirātas acted at the Rājasūya as servers (यत्र सर्वान् मही-पालाञ् शस्त्रतेजोभयार्दितान् । … किरातान् … यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 20, 22; (5) Arjuna's encounter with Mahādeva, who appeared in the form of a Kīrāta, referred to in the list of events of the Āraṇyakaparvan (यदाश्रौषम् अर्जुनो देवदेवं किरातरूपं त्र्यम्बकं तोष्य युद्धे) 1. 1. 109; (महादेवेन युद्धं च किरातवपुषा सह) 1. 2. 107; (6) Bhaga-datta's army, unassailable on account of the inclusion of Cīnas and Kirātas, went to the side of Duryodhana (तस्य चीनैः किरातैश् च … बभौ बलम् अनाधृष्यम्) 5. 19. 15; (7) Kirātas are mentioned among those who, at the instance of Duryodhana (5. 196. 1) marched towards Kurukṣetra (शकाः किराता … निर्ययुः) 5. 196. 7-8; (8) Before the start of the war, the north side of the army was guarded by Kirātas and others led by Kṛpa (शारद्वतश् चोत्तर-धूर् महात्मा … शकैः किरातैर् … सार्-धं चमूम् उत्तरतो ऽभिपाति) 6. 20. 13; (9) On the second day of the war, Kirātas stood at the neck of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 38) of the Pāṇḍavas (किराताश् च ग्रीवायाम्) 6. 46. 46; (10) Among the past exploits of Karṇa, Bhīṣma mentions his bringing the Kirātas under the control of Duryodhana (किराताः दुर्योधनस्य वशगाः कृताः कर्ण त्वया पुरा) 7. 4. 6; (11) Sātyaki pointed out to Yudhiṣṭhira seven hundred elephants, mounted by Kirā-tas, in the Kaurava army; they were defeated by Arjuna and their king had presented them to him as servants; they once served Yudhiṣṭhira, but in the war they took the side of the Kauravas and were helping Duryodhana; Sātyaki assured Yudhiṣṭhira that he could break through them and reach Arjuna (यांस् त्व् एतान् अपरान् राजन् नागान् सप्तशतानी च । प्रेक्षसे … किरातैः समधिष्ठितान् ॥ किरातराजो यान् प्रादाद् गृहीतः सव्यसाचिना । … प्रेष्यान् इच्छञ् जीवितम् आत्मनः ॥ आसन्न् एते पुरा राजंस् तव कर्मकरा दृढम् । त्वाम् एवाद्य युयुत्सन्ते पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम् ॥ … एते विनिर्जिताः सर्वे संग्रामे सव्यसाचिना । मदर्थम् अद्य संयत्ता दुर्योधन-वशानुगाः ॥ एतान् भित्त्वा शरै राजन् किरातान्  … अनुयास्यामि पाण्डवम् ॥ ) 7. 87. 27-29, 31-32; Sātyaki was expecting to meet the Kirātas who desired the benefit of Duryo-dhana (किरातैश् च समेष्यामि … दुर्यो-धनहितैषिभिः) 7. 87. 49; Sātyaki killed thousands of them and made the ground impassable due to the mud of flesh and blood (सहस्रैस् तु … किरातानाम् … अग-म्यरूपां पृथिवीं मांसशोणितकर्द-माम्) 7. 95. 38-39; (12) On the seven-teenth day of the war, Kṛṣṇa told Arjuna that the Kirātas and others who had joined the Kauravas could not be defeated by any one except him (किराताश् च … । एते सुयोधनस्यार्थे संरब्धाः कुरुभिः सह । न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परंतप ॥ ) 8. 51. 19-20; (13) Kirātas mentioned among those who were formerly vanquished in the great war and whom Arjuna encountered again when he accom-panied the Aśvamedha horse (किराता … पूर्वं विनिकृता रणे । … समीयुः पाण्डु-पुत्रेण) 14. 72. 24-25; the Aśvamedha horse first reached the city of the Cedis; from there it went to the Kirāta country (आससाद पुरीम् रम्यां चेदीनाम् … तत्रा-र्चितो ययौ राजंस् तदा स तुरगोत्तमः ।  … किरातान्) 14. 84. 2, 4.
किकट: Kikaṭa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Karṇa related to Saṃjaya what a Brāhmaṇa had told the assembly of the Kurus (8. 30. 41) regarding the Kīkaṭas; he had said that the Kīkaṭas were follo-wers of bad religion and one should avoid them (कीकटाटवीन् । … दुर्धर्मांश् च विवर्जयेत्) 8. 30. 45.
कीचक: Kīcaka m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people. Epic events: (1) Young Pāṇḍavas and Kuntī, in their wanderings after their escape from the lac house, passed through many countries one of them being the Kīcakas (ते … वीरा … ययू … । … कीचकान् अन्तरेण च) 1. 144. 1-2; (2) Dhṛtarāṣṭra, while recounting past exploits of Karṇa, mention-ed that he had defeated the Kīcakas and made them pay tribute (वङ्गकीचकान् । … यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 19-20.
कुक्कुर: Kukkura m. (pl.): Name of a people (probably of the north-west). The Kṣatriyas among them brought tribute in hundreds for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rāja-sūya (शौण्डिकाः कुक्कुराश् चैव … आहार्षुः क्सत्रिया वित्तम् शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 15-16.
कुक्कुश: Kukkuśa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (जठराः कुक्कुशाश् चैव) 6. 10. 41.
कुट्ट: Kuṭṭa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कुट्टापरान्ता … ) 6. 10. 47.
कुणप: Kuṇapa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa told the Pāṇḍavas that not even Kuṇapas come near his forest called Aṅgāraparṇa on the river Gaṅgā (अङ्गारपर्णम् इति च ख्यातं वनम् इदं मम । अनु गङ्गां च वाकां च … ॥ न कुणपाः शृङ्गिणो वा … इदं समु-पसर्पन्ति) 1. 158. 13-14.
कुणिन्द: Kuṇinda, Kuṇindaviṣaya m. (pl., sg.): Name of a country and its people. A. Location: In the north (विजयाय प्रयास्यामि दिशं धनदरक्षिताम्) 2. 23. 4; (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् अजयत् पाक-शासनिः) 2. 23. 9; they lived along the river Śailodā between the mountains Meru and Mandara and enjoyed the shadows of bam-boos and reeds (मेरुमन्दरयोर् मध्ये शैलोदाम् अभितो नदीम् । ये ते कीचकवेणू-नां छायां रम्याम् उपासते … कुणिन्दाश् च) 2. 48. 2-3; on the mountain Himavant; on way to Gandhamādana, the Pāṇḍavas first saw the country of hundreds of Kuṇindas ruled by Subāhu (सुबाहोर् विष-यं महत् … कुणिन्दशतसंकुलम्) 3. 141. 24-25; the Pāṇḍavas on their return journey again saw the town of Subāhu and the Kuṇinda country (देशान् कुणिन्दस्य … अतीत्य दुर्गं हिमवत्प्रदेशं पुरं सुबाहोर् ददृशुः नृवीराः) 3. 174. 12. B. Characterization: People characterized as mountaineers (कुणिन्दाश् च … पार्वतीयाः) 2. 48. 3. 7; expert in fighting with rocks (पाषाणयोधिनः, अश्मयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 7. 97. 29-30, 34, 35, 38-39. C. Description: (1) The country: Large (महन्त्) 3. 141. 24; having many jewels (भूरितत्न) 3. 174. 12; full of many wonders (बह्वाश्चर्य-समाकुल) 3. 141. 25; liked by gods (अम-रैर् जुष्टम्) 3. 141. 25; (2) The warriors: The Kuṇinda warriors were very strong, difficult to conquer (अतिबल, दुर्जय) 8. 5. 18. D. Epic events: (1) Kuṇindas were one of the eighteen peoples who, out of fear of Jarāsandha, fled to the west (कुलान्य् अष्टादशाभिभो । जरासन्धभयाद् एव प्रतीचीं आइशम् आश्रीताः ॥ … कुणिन्दाः कुन्तिभिः सह) 2. 13. 24-25; (2) Kuṇinda country was the first to be conquered by Arjuna in his expedition before the Rājasūya (पूर्वं कुणिन्दविषये वशे चक्रे मही-पतीन् । … कुणिन्दांश् च विजित्य सः) 2. 23. 13-14; (3) The kings of Kuṇinda country brought as tribute for the Rājasūya, पिपी-लिक variety of gold, given as boon by ants (?), in heaps, to be measured by द्रोणस्, best black chowries and other chowries white like the moon, sweet honey from Himalayan flowers, garlands of flowers brought down by waters from the Uttara kurus, and powerful herbs from northern Kailāsa; they were halted at the gate (पशुपाश् च कुणिन्दाश् च … ते वै पिपीलिकं नाम वरदत्तं पिपीलिकैः । जातरूपं द्रोणमेयम् अहार्षुः पुञ्जशो नृपाः … द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 48. 3-7; (4) Subāhu, the king of the Kuṇindas respectfully and happily received the Pāṇḍavas when they entered his country (सुबाहुश् चापि तान् दृष्ट्वा पूजया प्रत्यगृह्णत । विषयान्ते कुणिन्दानाम् ईश्वरह् प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ॥ ) 3. 141. 26, 29; (5) The Pāṇḍavas on their re-turn journey crossed the impassable regions of the Himavant to reach the country of the Kuṇindas and the town of Subāhu; the king received them and greeted them joy-fully; having passed one night there they allowed Ghaṭotkaca and his followers to leave them; from there they went to the Yāmuna mountain (देशान् कुणिन्दस्य च … अतीत्य दुर्गं हिमवत्प्रदेशं पुरं सुबाहोर् ददृशुः सुवीराः ॥ … सुखोषितास् तत्र त एकरात्रं … घटोत्कचं सानु-चरं विसृज्य ततो ऽभ्ययुर् यामुनम् अद्रि-राजम्) 3. 174. 12-15; (6) On the four-teenth day of the war, Kuṇindas attacked Sātyaki; Sātyaki repulsed their shower of rocks with his नाराच arrows (कुणिन्दास्  … अभ्यद्रवन्तो शैनेयम्) 7. 97. 14; (अश्मवृष्टिं समन्ततः । … कुणिन्दैश् च क्षिप्तां क्सिप्तां स सात्यकिः । नाराचैः प्रतिविव्याध) 7. 97. 39-40 (also cf. 7. 97. 29-30, 34-35, 38); (7) Dhṛtarāṣṭra, re-counting the past exploits of Karṇa, men-tioned his defeating the Kuṇindas and mak-ing them pay tribute (यश् चाजैषीत्॥।कुणिन्-दान् … यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 18-20; (8) On the seventeenth day of the war, the Kuṇindas, riding huge and swift elephants, opposed eleven prin-cipal heroes from the Kaurava side; the Kuṇinda prince was killed by Kṛpa and his brother by Śakuni; when the Kuṇindas were killed, the Kaurava heroes were happy and blew their conches (हस्तिभिस् तान् उदीयुर् गिरिशिखरनिकाशैर् भीमवेगैह् कुणिन्दाः ॥ … कुणिन्दपुत्रो … शरद्वत्-सुतसायकैर् हतः … कुणिन्दपुत्रावरजस् तु … ननाद … ततो ऽस्य गान्धारपतिः शिरो ऽहरत् ॥ ततः कुणिन्देषु हतेषु … भृशं प्रदध्मुर् लवणाम्बुसंभवान्) 8. 62. 35, 37-39; many elephants of Kuṇinda warriors were killed by the Kaurava heroes 8. 62. 40-43; the battles fought by mountain-dwelling Kuṇinda princes and their ele-phants with Kaurava heroes described in 8. 62. 44-50 (कुणिन्दराजावरजाद् अनन्तरः 44; कुणिन्दपुत्रप्रहितो ऽपरद्विपः 46; द्विपस्थेन … पर्वतजेन 47; द्विपस्थं गिरिराजवासिनम् 48, कुणिन्दजः 50. (9) In the battle that was fought by the Kuṇinda prince (कुणिन्दपुत्रः), who was fighting from the side of the Kauravas, with Śatā-nīka, the former, along with his elephants got killed 8. 62. 51-52.
कुण्डीविष: Kuṇḍīviṣa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. On the second day of the war, they were stationed on the right side of the Krauñcā-ruṇa (or Krauñca 6. 47. 1) Vyūha of the Pāṇḍavas (व्यूहः क्रौञ्चारुणो नाम) 6. 46. 39; (पुण्द्रा कुण्दीविषैः सह … एते जनपदा राजन् दक्षिणं पक्षम् आश्रिताः) 6. 46. 49-50.
कुनट: Kunaṭa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कुशलाः कुनटास् तथा) 6. 10. 50.
कुन्तल: Kuntala1 m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the (northern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वम् जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कुन्तलाः काशिकोसलाः) 6. 10. 38. B. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa told Karṇa that if he were to come over to the side of the Pāṇḍavas, Draviḍas, Kuntalas and others would move in front of him in his march (पुरोगमाश् च ते सन्तु द्रविडा सह कुन्तलैः) 5. 138. 25; (2) On the second day of the war, Droṇa, to-gether with Kuntalas and others, followed Bhīṣma in order to protect him (तम् अन्वयान् महेष्वासो भारद्वाजः प्रताप-वान् । कुन्तलैश् च दशार्णैश् च) 6. 47. 12; (भीष्मम् एवाभिरक्षन्तु सह सैन्यपुरस्-कृताः) 6. 47. 9.
Kuntala2 m. (pl.): Name of a people. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Mlecchas of the Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना भरतसत्तम … सक्षद्द्रुहः कुन्तलाश् च) 6. 10. 63-64.
कुन्ति: Kunti m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: One of the (northern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) listed by Saṃjaya (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कुन्-तयो ऽवन्तयश् चैव) 6. 10. 41; the eastern Kośalas formed part of it (पूर्वाः कुन्तिषु कोशलाः) 2. 13. 26. B. Description: In battles, the Kunti warriors proved to be valorous, of great spirit and great strength (कुन्तयो युधि विक्रान्ता महासत्त्वा महा-बलाः) 8. 4. 59. C. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa told the Pāṇḍavas that, afraid of Jarāsandha, Kuntis retreated to the south (कुणिन्दाः कुन्तिभिः सह … । दक्षिणां दिशम् आश्रिताः … जरासन्धभयार्दिताः) 2. 13. 25, 27-28; (2) Kunti warriors, together with their followers and relatives, were killed by Bhīṣma in battle (कुन्तयो … सानुबन्-धाः सहामात्या भीष्मेण युधि पातिताः) 8. 4. 59.
कुन्तिक: Kuntika m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. One of the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhārata-varṣa listed by Saṃjaya (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (कर्-णिका कुन्तिकाश् चैव) 6. 10. 58.
कुन्दमान: Kundamāna m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their Kṣatriya kings brought wealth in hundreds for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya (काश्मीराः कुण्दमानाश् च … राजन्या … ॥  … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजात-शत्रवे) 2. 48. 13, 16.
कुमारविषय: Kumāraviṣaya m.: Name of a country. A. Location: Close to Cedi (2. 26. 12) and Kosala (2. 27. 1) in the east (2. 26. 1). B. Epic event: Bhīma in his ex-pendition to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1) conquered Śreṇimant in Kumāraviṣaya (ततः कुमारविषये श्रेणि-मन्तम् अथाजयत्) 2. 27. 1.
कुमुदोत्तर: Kumudottara m. Name of a Varṣa. One of the Varṣas in the Śākadvīpa; it was related to the mountain Malaya (जलदः (i. e. मलयः) कुमुदोत्तरः) 6. 12. 23.
कुरक: Kuraka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. One of the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (कर-ण्थाः कुरकास् तथा) 6. 10. 61.
कुरङ्ग: Kuraṅga m. (pl.): Name of a country. The river Karatoyā flew through this country (करतोयां कुरङ्गेषु) 13. 26. 11.
कुरु: Kuru m. (pl.): Name of a country (once distinguished as northern and sou-thern (14. 69. 19), also referred to as Kururāṣṭra (1. 105. 21), and its people (in general or those of Hāstinapura in parti-cular); the term often signifies the des-cendants of Kuru or the the Kuru family in general (also called Kuruvaṃśa), or the descendants of Kuru sitting in the assembly of the Kauravas; very often it signifies the chief warriors in the army of the Kauravas (in which case the term occasionally in-cludes heroes like Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa or the Saṃśaptakas (8. 59. 1, 3), or some-times it refers even to the Kaurava army in general; sometimes the term Kuravaḥ includes the Pāṇḍavas and their descendants (Abhimanyu, Parikṣit and Janamejaya), or, as opposed to the Pāṇḍavas, the term is restricted to refer to the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra (otherwise called Kauravas). A. Country (often it is difficult to distinguish between the country and the people): Listed by Saṃjaya among the Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम । तत्रेमे कुरुपाञ्चालाः) 6. 10. 37. 5; its capital town Hāstinapura (स हास्तिनपुरे रम्ये कुरूणां पुटभेदने) 1. 94. 10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 100. 12: पुटभेदने पत्तने); (स धर्मात्मा (भीष्मः) … ययौ कुरून्) 1. 96. 44; नान्धः कुरूणां नृपतिर् अनुरूपस् तपोधन) 1. 100. 11; when Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura were born the Kuru country, as also Kuru-jāṅgala and Kurukṣetra prospered (तेषु त्रिषु कुमारेषु जातेषु कुरुजाङ्गलं । कुरवो ऽथ कुरुक्षेत्रम् त्रयम् एतद् अवर्धत ॥ ) 1. 102. 1 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 1. 109. 1: कुरुजाङ्गलं देशः कुरवः पुरुषाः कुरुक्षेत्रं तेषां वास-स्थानम्); the Kuru country described after the birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura: it rained on time, draught-animals as well as birds and animals were happy; the cities were crowded with merchants and craftsmen; there were no robbers and no one took delight in unlawful acts; in all parts of the Kuru country, Kṛta yuga prevailed; people, free from pride, anger and greed, helped one another to prosper; there were tall houses and people sported in rivers, ponds and forest tracts; people of the southern Kurus as though vied with those of the Uttarakurus (see p. 635 ff.); no one was wretched; women did not suffer from widowhood; wells, gardens, and assembly halls, and lodging places for Brāhmaṇas were raised by the Kuru people; the country prospered by obliging other countries; the people celebrated festivals at all times; one always heard the words ‘give, enjoy’ in the houses of the people and of the Kuru chiefs; in short, the wheel of धर्म, set in motion by Bhīṣma, prevailed in the land of Kurus (यथर्तुवर्षी पर्जन्यो … नाभवन् दस्-यवो केचिन् नाधर्मरुचयो जनाः … प्र-देशेष्व् अपि राष्त्राणां कृतं युगम् अवर्-तत ॥ … उत्तरैः कुरुभिः सार्धं दक्षि-णाः कुरवस् तद । विस्पर्धमाना व्यच-रंस् … ॥ … तस्मिञ् जनपदे रम्ये बहवः कुरुभिः कृताः । कूपारामसभावाप्यो ब्राह्मणावसथास् तथा । … भीष्मेण विहि-तं राष्ट्रे धर्मचक्रम् अवर्तत ॥ … गृहेषु कुरुमुख्यानाम् पौराणाम् च नरा-धिप । दीयतां भुज्यतां चेति वाचो ऽश्रू-यन्त सर्वशः) 1. 102. 1-14); कुरुराष्ट्राणि 1. 105. 21; अभ्यागच्छं कुरून् भीष्म 1. 122. 38; कुरुभ्यः प्रस्थितास् ते तु 2. 18. 26; क्षिप्रं कुरून् याहि 4. 61. 22; यावद् अध्यावसत् कुरून् 4. 65. 11; कुरून् असपत्नो ऽनुशिष्याम् 5. 30. 46; 5. 31. 4; कुरवस् ते सजाङ्गलाः 5. 53. 7; कुरून् गत्वा भारताञ् शमयेः प्रभो 5. 70. 90; समत्स्यैः कुरुमध्यदेशैः 5. 158. 20; बाह्लीकं कुरुवासिनम् 8. 30. 20; भव राजा कुरुष्व् इति 9. 32. 3; कृष्नः … अन्वयात् कुरून् 12. 38. 39; कुरून् वै दक्षिणोत्तरान् 14. 69. 19; कुरून् अभ्याजगाम ह 14. 89. 25; गत्वा कुरून् 16. 5. 2; कुरूंस् तदा दारुको … ययौ 16. 5. 3; 16. 6. 1; kingdom of the Kuru country (कुरुराज्ये … अभ्यषिञ्चत्) 1. 95. 12; Arjuna expressed his wish to win the whole king-dom of the Kuru country (राज्यं कुरूणां अवजेता समग्रम्) 5. 47. 91; (एकराज्यं कुरूणं स्म चिकीर्षति युधिष्ठिरे) 5. 54. 10; (राज्यम् इच्छामि कुरूणाम्) 9. 30. 41; (प्राप्य राज्यं कुरूणाम्) 13. 75. 28. B. Kuru dynasty, Kuru family: Sūta traced the lineage of the Kuru to the Sun through five intervening generations (तेभ्यो ऽयं कुरु-वंशश् च) 1. 1. 44; Vaiśaṃpāyana narrated to king Janamejaya a brief and a detailed account of the Kuru dynasty starting from the very beginning (विस्तरं कुरुवंशस्य) 1. 1. 59; (कथितं वै समासेन … कुरू-णां चरितं महत्) 1. 56. 1; कुरूणां वंशम् आदितः) 1. 62. 2; King Parikṣit was born in the line of the Kurus (कुरुकुलोत्-पन्न) 1. 38. 36; after Parikṣit, Janamejaya got the kingdom which came to him in the line of the Kurus (राज्यं कुरुकुलागतम्) 1. 45. 16; birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu necessary for the continuation of the line of the Kurus (अस्माकम् अपि ते जन्म विदि-तं … कुरूणां वंशवृद्धये) 1. 113. 23; Pāṇḍu brought fame to the Kurus (कुरू-णां अकरोद् यशः) 1. 105. 12; Pāṇḍu told Kuntī that a son born to her by Dharma would be, among the Kurus, the one devo-ted to धर्म (धार्मिकश् च कुरूणां सः) 1. 113. 41; an incorporeal voice pro-phesied at Arjuna's birth that he would set right the emblem of the Kurus (कुरु-लक्ष्म सुधास्यति) 1. 114. 31; the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas and others spoke about the extent of the glorious Kuru dynasty (यक्षराक्षस-गन्धर्वाः … विस्तरम् कुरुवंशस्य श्री-मतः कथयन्ति ते ॥ ) 1. 159. 3; the Gan-dharva Aṅgāraparṇa himself had observed the prowess of the (Kuru)kula while wandering on the earth (स्वयं चापि मया दृष्टश् … प्रभावः स्वकुलस्य ते) 1. 159. 5; sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra had crossed the limits of धर्म of the Kuru dynasty (यत्रा-भ्यतीतां कुरुधर्मवेलाम् 2. 60. 33; if Yudhiṣṭhira got the kingdom of the illustrious Kurus, he could obtain great place (?) and perform sacrificial rites (प्राप्य राज्यं कुरुपुंगवानाम् शक्यं महत् प्राप्तुम् अथ क्रियाश् च) 3. 173. 12; the Kuru dynasty depended on Dhṛtarāṣṭra (त्वय्य् आधीनं कुरुकुलम्) 5. 36. 71; it depended on Yudhiṣṭhira 15. 44. 25; the Kuru dynasty was glorious (कुरुवंशस्य श्रीमतः) 1. 159. 3; it was considered the best of all the royal families (इदम् अद्य कुलं श्रेष्ठं सर्वराजसु); it was learned, marked by good conduct and good qualities; it was distinguished for its compa-ssion, sympathy, kindness, non-cruelty, straightforwardness, mercy, and truthful-ness 5. 93. 5-6; according to the hereditary धर्म of the Kuru family their kingdom was to be ruled according to succession (राज्यं कुरूणाम् अनुपूर्वभोग्यं क्र-मागतो नः कुलधर्म एषः) 5. 146. 29; Yudhiṣṭhira should be allowed to rule the kingdom of the Kurus that had legitimately gone to him (न्यायागतं राज्यम् इदं कुरूणां) 5. 146. 35; during the war, singers sang songs in praise of Kuru family (जगुर् गीतानि गायकाः । कुरुवंशस्तवार्थानि) 7. 58. 3; Arjuna desired to win back the kingdom of the Kurus (राज्यप्रेप्सुः सव्य-साची कुरूणां) 7. 120. 85; Bhīṣma revived the Kuru dynasty which appeared to have ended (प्रनष्टः कुरुवंशश् च पुनर् येन समुद्धृतः) 11. 23. 24; Bhagavān prophesied that when Tiṣya would arrive again high-souled Bhārata kings, called Kurus, would be born and would become famous on the earth; there would be feud for mutual destruction in the family of those born of Vyāsa (पुनस् तिष्य च सं-प्राप्ते कुरवो नाम भारताः । भविष्यन्ति  … तेषां त्वत्तः प्रसूतानां कुलभेदो भविष्यति) 12. 337. 42-43; bards and others praised Kṛṣṇa with songs proclaiming the praise of the Kuru family and by blessings (कुरुवंशस्तवाख्याभिर् आशीर्भिर् … ) 14. 69. 7; Yudhiṣṭhira had distinguished himself among the Kuru heroes by observing धर्म (त्वं चाद्य कुरुवीराणां धर्मे-णाभिविराजसे) 14. 70. 23; a Brāhmaṇa living in Hāstinapura, called Sāmba, told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that no king in the dynasty of the Kurus was at any time, as the protector of subjects, unpopular among them; he assured Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Yudhiṣṭhira would follow the footsteps of the ancient royal sages in his dynasty like Kuru, Saṃvaraṇa and Bharata (न जात्व् अस्य तु वंशस्य राज्ञां कश्चित् कदाचन । राजासीद् यः प्रजापालः प्रजानाम् अप्रियो ऽभवत् ॥ राजर्षीणां पुराणानाम् भवतां वंश-धारिणाम् । … वृत्तं समनुयात्य् एष धर्-मात्मा) 15. 15. 15; 23-24; Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī told Yudhiṣṭhira that the श्रा-द्ध libation, fame and the lineage (of the Kurus) were established in him (त्वय्य् अद्य पिण्डः कीर्तिश् च कुलं चेदं प्रतिष्ठितम् ।  … त्वय्य् अधीनं कुरुकुलं पिण्डश् च श्वशुरस्य मे) 15. 44. 21, 25. C. Members of the Kuru family, who lived at Hāstina-pura (or outside it 2. 52. 8, 25) and who sided with the Kauravas: Dhṛtarāṣṭra told Vidura that he did not rejoice at the destruc-tion of the Kurus (न च प्रीये कुरुक्षये) 1. 1. 97; Janamejaya wanted to know from Vyāsa the story of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas to which he was a witness (कुरूणां पाण्डवाणां च भवान् प्रत्य-क्षदर्शिवान्) 1. 54. 18; Vaiśaṃpāyana was to tell Janamejaya the account of the feud, loss of kingdom, and war between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas (कुरूणां पाण्ड-वानां च यथा भेदो ऽभवत् पुरा) 1. 54. 22; (भेदं राज्यविनाशं च कुरुपाण्डव-योः) 1. 54. 24; 1. 55. 4-5; the Kurus could not bear the glory, fame etc. of the Pāṇḍa-vas (नामृष्यन् कुरवो दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवाञ् श्रीयशोभृताः) 1. 55. 7; Bhīṣma asked all the Kuru chiefs to perform the funeral rites of Vicitravīrya (प्रेतकार्याणि … अकारयत् ।  … भीष्मः सर्वैश् च कुरुपुंगवैः) 1. 96. 59; many Kurus got wells, gardens etc. constructed in the Kuru country 1. 102. 11; in the houses of the Kuru chiefs, gifts were given and food offered (गृहेषु कुरु-मुख्यानाम् … दीयताम् भुज्यतां चेति वाचो ऽश्रूयन्त सर्वशः) 1. 102. 14; Gāndhārī, after her marriage, gave satisfaction to all the Kurus (तुष्टिं कुरूणां सर्वे-षाम्) 1. 103. 16; as the Kurus watched, the sages disappeared after telling them to perform the funeral rites of Pāṇḍu and Mādrī (एवम् उक्त्वा कुरून् सर्वान् ॥।कुरूणाम् एव पश्यताम्) 1. 117. 32; once the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas went out for hunting 1. 123. 15; Pāṇḍavas, while proceeding to Vāraṇāvata, bowed down to all elderly Kurus (कुरून् वृद्धान्) 1. 133. 3; Vidura and other distinguished Kurus followed them 1. 133. 5; the distinguished Kurus might get angry when they knew about the Vāraṇāvata incident 1. 134. 22; Kurus prospered due to the marriage of the Pāṇḍavas with Draupadī 1. 192. 17; the Pāṇḍavas were to be protected by all the Kurus—Bhīṣma told Dhṛtarāṣṭra (तथा कुरूणां सर्वेषाम् अन्येषाम् अपि भारत) 1. 195. 3; Droṇa told Karṇa what was very much in the interest of the Kurus; if his advice was not followed, the Kurus would soon perish (हितं तु परमं कर्ण ब्रवीमि कुरुवर्धनं … कुरवो विनशि-ष्यन्ति नाचिरेण) 1. 196. 27-28; the Kurus were anxious to meet the Pāṇḍavas after their marriage with Draupadī 1. 198. 21; all Kurus gathered at Hāstinapura at the time of द्यूत (समागताः कौरवश् चैव सर्वे 2. 52. 8); Pāṇḍavas met the Kurus who had arrived from all sides (कुरुभिश् चापि सर्वशः) 2. 52. 25; according to Vidura many of the Kurus would follow Duḥśā-sana to hell and that the end of the Kurus was at hand (त्वाम् अन्वेतारो बहवः कुरू-णाम्) 2. 59. 10; (अन्तो नूनं भवितायं कुरूणाम्) 2. 59. 12; 3. 5. 9; 3. 48. 40; 3. 225. 24; according to Bhīṣma, the end of the Kurus was not far since all of them were under the influence of greed and delusion (नूनम् अन्तः कुलस्यास्य भविता न चिराद् इव । तथा हि कुरवः सर्वे लोभमोहपरा-यणाः) 2. 62. 17; the second game of dice could mean the end of the Kurus 2. 67. 16; the priests of Kurus would recite Sāmans addressed to Yama and Rudra (2. 71. 7) when the Bhāratas would be killed in war (हतेषु भारतेष्व् आजौ कुरूणाम् गुरवस् तदा । एवं सामानि गास्यन्ति) 2. 71. 22; in the opinion of Vidura the Pāṇḍavas were stronger than the Kurus 2. 72. 33; Vyāsa knew where lay the happiness of the Kurus 3. 11. 2; Vyāsa, if he had any mercy for the Kurus, should advise Duryodhana (कौर-वेषु दया यदि) 3. 11. 3; Maitreya asked Duryodhana to do what was in the interest of the Kurus 3. 11. 20; if Kṛṣṇa could have spoken to Dhṛtarāṣṭra against द्यूत, the धर्म of the Kurus would not have suffered (अनामयम् स्यात् धर्मस्य कुरू-णाम्) 3. 14. 11; all Kurus, except four (the four include Karṇa and Śakuni), shed tears when Pāṇḍavas started for the forest 3. 28. 7; according to Draupadī that was not the time to show forgiveness to Kurus 3. 29. 34; Duryodhana exhorted all the Kurus against the Pāṇḍavas (उद्योजयाम् आस कुरूंश् च सर्वान्) 3. 35. 13 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 34. 14: उद्योजयाम् आस उत्कर्-षेण स्वेच्छया तेषु तेषु दुर्गदेशादिपालन-कार्येषु इष्टान् योजितवान्); Duryodhana, surrounded by Kurus, shone like the moon surrounded by the नक्षत्रस् 3. 226. 10; soldiers of the Kurus (कुरुसैनिकाः) were halted by the Gandharvas 3. 230. 6; Pāṇḍa-vas, honoured by Kurus and their wives and children (सस्त्रीकुमारैः कुरुभिः), shone like fires in their midst (कुरु-मध्ये) 3. 235. 19; Draupadī com-plained to Bhīma that distress had over-taken her defeating all Kurus, Pāñcālas and Pāṇḍavas (कुरून् परिभवन् सर्वान् … संप्राप्तो मम क्लेशो ह्य् अरिंदम) 4. 19. 11; Balarāma wished that some one went to Hāstinapura to strive for conciliation between Kurus and Pāṇḍavas (शमार्थं कुरुपाण्डवानाम्) 5. 2. 4; according to Kṛṣṇa, the relations of Yādavas with Kurus and Pāṇḍavas ought to be the same, no matter how they behaved (संबन्धकं तुल्यम् अस्माकं कुरुपाण्डुषु) 5. 5. 3; if the chief of the Kurus (Dhṛtarāṣṭra ?) would behave justly, large scale destruction could be avoided by the good brotherli-ness between Kurus and Pāṇḍavas (न भवेत् कुरुपाण्डूनाम् सौभ्रात्रेण महान् क्षयः) 5. 5. 8; the whole earth was agitated due to (the feud between) the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas (कुरुपाण्डव-कारणात्) 5. 5. 16; Drupada sent his priest to the Kurus 5. 5. 18; the Pāṇḍavas desired peace, and not conflict, with the Kurus 5. 20. 12, 64; Yudhiṣṭhira hoped that the Kurus did not talk ill of the Pāṇḍavas 5. 23. 19; what Saṃjaya wanted to say was for the prosperity of the Kurus 5. 25. 3, 8; according Saṃjaya if the Pāṇḍavas wanted to discipline the Kurus (by killing them), Pāṇḍavas' being alive would be as good as their death (ते चेत् कुरून् अनुशास्य स्थ पार्-थाः … समं वस् तज् जीवितं मृत्युना स्यात्) 5. 25. 9; according to Saṃjaya who could face the attack of the Kurus when prote-cted by Droṇa Bhīṣma and others ? 5. 25. 11; Saṃjaya begged the Pāṇḍavas and others to see where lay the welfare of the Kurus and the Sṛñjayas (कथं स्वस्ति स्यात् कुरुसृञ्जयानाम्) 5. 25. 14; Yudhiṣṭhira to Saṃjaya: Why should Dhṛtarāṣṭra desire to separate the Pāṇḍa-vas from the Kurus ? Vidura wished wel-fare of the Kurus, but Dhṛtarāṣṭra did not remember him from among the Kurus; while playing the game of dice, Vidura wonder-ed if disaster was in store for the Kurus; when the Kurus followed the advice of Vidura, calamity did not strike the Kurus; on the other hand, their kingdom prospered; if Vidura was kept out, how could welfare come to the Kurus and the Sṛñjayas (कथं स्वस्ति स्यात् कुरुसृञ्जयानाम्); all the Kurus-including Karṇa, Duryo-dhan, Droṇa and Bhīṣma—knew that there was no archer like Arjuna 5. 26. 7, 12, 15-16, 18, 21-22; Kṛṣṇa to Saṃjaya: If all the Kurus, young and old, had pre-vented Duḥśāsana, it would have pleased Kṛṣṇa (सकुमारवृद्धाः … कुरवः); if Kṛṣṇa could establish peace with the Kurus, they would be saved from the bond of death; he would approach the Kurus if they would be willing to respect him 5. 29. 32, 41-42; Yudhiṣṭhira wished well for the Kuru chiefs (कुरुमुख्या युवानः) as also for their Dāsas and the sons of Dāsas (दासी-पुत्रा ये च दासाः कुरूणाम्) 5. 30. 22, 37; the Pāṇḍavas, though stronger than the Kurus, had patiently borne the hardships—this was known to the Kurus 5. 31. 14; the counsellors of the Kurus were convinced that a hell had been let loose for the des-truction of the Kurus (कुरुक्षयार्थे निरयो व्यपादि) 5. 32. 20 (Nī. who reads नियमेनोदपादि (Bom. Ed. 5. 32. 21) para-phrases as नियमेन उत्पन्नः); Dhṛta-rāṣṭra requested Vidura to tell him what was beneficial for the Kurus 5. 34. 2, 5; Dhṛtarāṣṭra was one on whom the Kuru family depended (त्वय्य् आधीनं कुरु-कुलम्) 5. 36. 71; the Kurus would witness the destruction of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in case of war (प्रत्यक्षं वः कुरवः) 5. 47. 90; all the Kurus would be long-lived if they followed the advise of Bhīṣma and others 5. 47. 103; otherwise, annihila-tion was in store of the Kurus (नो चेद् अयम् अभावः स्यात् कुरूणाम्) 5. 48. 25; Jarāsandha could not subdue the Kurus 5. 50. 39; Dhṛtarāṣṭra felt that destruction of the Kurus was certain 5. 50. 36, 57, 59; he advised the Kurus not to confront the Pāṇḍavas if they wanted to avoid destru-ction of the whole family 5. 52. 14; many kings blamed Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and the Kurus, (व्यगर्हयंश् च संगम्य भवन्तं कुरुभिः सह) 5. 54. 4; Saṃjaya was to tell the Kurus and others to deal justly with Yudhiṣṭhira 5. 56. 56; all the Kurus were of the opinion that peace with the Pāṇḍavas meant acting according to धर्म (एतद् धि कुरवः सर्वे मन्यन्ते धर्मसंहितं) 5. 57. 4; Kurus were inferior to the Pāṇḍavas in point of strength and lustre, both divine and human (देवमानुषयोः शक्त्या तेजसा चैव पाण्डवान् । कुरून् शक्त्याल्पतरया) 5. 59. 4; Agni would help the Pāṇḍavas in war between them and the Kurus 5. 59. 8; brooding over peace between Kurus (and Pāṇḍavas) Dhṛtarāṣṭra passed sleep-less nights; he felt destruction of the Kurus was at hand, for he always rated Pāṇḍavas stronger than Kurus 5. 59. 21-23; he wanted Duryodhana to listen to him whose advice was in the interest of the Kurus (कुरूणाम् अर्थवादिनम्) 5. 63. 12; Kṛṣṇa wished to release the agitated Kurus and Sṛñjayas from the noose of death (संरब्धान् कुरुसृञ्जयान्) 5. 70. 81; Yudhiṣṭhira initially did not approve of Kṛṣṇa's approaching the Kurus 5. 70. 82; Kṛṣṇa would burn all the Kurus if they tried to do anything improper to him 5. 70. 87; if Kṛṣṇa, while striving for peace, did not get any response which would be in accord with धर्म (न धर्मं तत्र लप्स्यसे), all kings would blame Kurus 5. 71. 30, 32; Kṛṣṇa warned Kauravas that fierce war was certain 5. 75. 17; Bhīma did not want Kṛṣṇa to incite the Kurus for war; he remembered that at one time they lived happily together with the Kurus and their sons (कुरवः सहपुत्रास् तथा वयम्); he wanted Kṛṣṇa to act in such a way that the Pāṇḍavas could remain neutral with the Kurus and that Kurus did not resort to an unjust course (अप्य् उदासीन-वृत्तिः स्याद् यथा नः कुरुभिः सह । वासुदेव तथा कार्यं न कुरून् अनयः स्पृशेत्) 5. 72. 1, 9, 21; Kṛṣṇa was a great friend of Kurus and Pāṇḍavas; he could lead them to well-being (निरामयम्) 5. 76. 7-8; 5. 81. 1; but Sahadeva wanted Kṛṣṇa to strive for war between Kurus and Pāṇḍavas even if the former sought peace 5. 79. 2; Kṛṣṇa would strive to do that what was just and beneficial to the Pāṇḍavas and well-being of the Kurus (धर्म्यम् अस्मद्धितं चैव कुरूणाम् यद् अनामयम्) 5. 81. 5; Kṛṣṇa left for Hāstinapura, the seat of the Kurus (कुरू-णां सदनं) 5. 81. 29; (कुरुसद्मन्) 5. 83. 18; Duryodhana in his house was surrounded by Kurus 5. 89. 4; there the Kurus waited on Kṛṣṇa 5. 89. 36; Kṛṣṇa approached by the Kurus in Vidura's house; they offered him their houses and treasures; when Kurus left, Vidura wor-shipped Kṛṣṇa 5. 89. 35-36, 38; Kṛṣṇa assured Vidura that he would try for conciliation between Kurus and Sṛñja-yas who would (otherwise) perish in war 5. 91. 8; great calamity loomed large over the Kurus who followed Karṇa and Duryodhana 5. 91. 9; 5. 93. 11; Kṛṣṇa tried for conciliation lest he was blamed (by others) for not checking, though capable, the agitated Kurus and Pāṇḍavas 5. 91. 16; Kṛṣṇa wished that the Kurus honoured him 5. 91. 20; Kurus, led by Bhīṣma, reached the Sabhā 5. 92. 8; they surrounded Kṛṣṇa when he started for the Sabhā; the whole town of the Kurus desired to see Kṛṣṇa whose chariot moved on the road (पुरं कुरूणां संवृत्तं द्रष्टुकामं जनार्द-नम् 5. 92. 14, 24; Kṛṣṇa went to the Kuru-assembly to establish peace between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas 5. 93. 3; Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, as the seniormost among the Kurus (श्रेष्ठः कुरूणां), could control them if they misbehaved 5. 93. 8; if Dhṛtarāṣṭra could restrain his sons (5. 93. 13), he, supported by the Kurus and the Pāṇḍa-vas, could become the lord of the world 5. 93. 22; Kaṇva advised Duryodhana to be reconciled to the Pāṇḍavas so that they and the Kurus might protect the earth 5. 95. 8; Gāndhārī advised Duryodhana not to be responsible for the killing of the Kurus 5. 127. 49; Dhṛtarāṣṭra desired and strove for conciliation between the Kurus (and the Pāṇḍavas) and that was known to all the Kurus 5. 129. 26, 28; Duryodhana should not think of war but should think of peace for the prosperity of the Kurus (अलं युद्धेन … शाम्य त्वं कुरु-वृद्धये) 5. 137. 22; Karṇa felt that the war between the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas was certain and that there were astronomical conjunctions foreboding great danger for the Kurus (विशेषेण हि वार्ष्णेय चित्रां पीडयते ग्रहः) 5. 141. 3, 9; Vidura wondered that when the धर्म was being forcibly driven away by the Kurus, who could not be afflicted; the unlawful act of the Kurus would cause destruction of the heroes 5. 142. 8-9; Kuntī wished that the Kurus saw the coming together of Karṇa and Arjuna as good brothers 5. 143. 9; according to Karṇa, Bhīṣma always wished ill of the Kurus, but Duryodhana did not realize it (कुरूणाम् अहितो नित्यम् न च राजावबुध्यते) 5. 165. 12; Bhīṣma felt that by their association with Karṇa, the Kurus had very much gone astray (कुरूणाम् अनयो महान्) 5. 166. 8; Vyāsa assured Dhṛtarāṣṭra that he would make known the fame of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas 6. 2. 13; he told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that there was nothing like permanent for his kinsmen, (as well as) for the Kurus (नेह विद्यति शाश्वतम् । ज्ञातीनां च कुरूणां च) 6. 4. 3; for the Kurus as well as for the Pāṇḍavas, Vyāsa was their धर्म, purification, glory, fame, forbearance, and स्मृति; he was their respected grand-sire (त्वं हि धर्मः पवित्रं च यशः कीर्तिर् धृतिः स्मृतिः । कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च मान्यश् चासि पिता-महः ॥ ) 6. 4. 13; the Kurus and the Pāṇḍa-vas were striving for the sovereignty of the earth by all sorts of means 6. 10. 73; during the battle between Arjuna and Bhīṣma-Droṇa, huge dust arose in the sky which looked like an excessive and fright-fully unjust conduct of the Kurus (कुरू-णाम् अनयस् तीव्रः समदृश्यत दारुणः) 6. 51. 21; if Dhṛtarāṣṭra had urged the Kurus to arrest Duryodhana before the war, he would not have faced calamity 7. 62. 6; when calamity was in store for the Kurus, Balarāma started on a pilgrimage (कुरूणां वैशसे) 9. 34. 18; when Dhṛtarāṣṭra and others started for the battlefield a big cry arose from all the houses of the Kurus (प्रणादः संजज्ञे सर्वेषु कुरुवेश्मसु) 11. 9. 8; according to Gāndhārī, Kṛṣṇa neglected the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, who were relatives, kill-ing each other (ज्ञातयः कुरुपाण्डवाः) 11. 25. 40; with Kṛṣṇa as a boat, the Pāṇḍavas were able to cross the ocean of the Kurus (तीर्णाः स्म कुरुसागरम्) 14. 51. 7; Uttaṅka wanted to know if Kṛṣṇa went to the seat of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas (?) to strive for conciliation (कच्चिच् छौरे त्वया गत्वा कुरुपाण्डव-सद्म तत्); Uttaṅka wanted to curse Kṛṣṇa since the latter failed to save Kurus and Pāṇḍavas although he could do that; he also blamed Kṛṣṇa for acting falsely with the best of the Kurus since he remained indifferent to them; he was capable of doing (otherwise) (त्वया हि शक्तेन सता … उपचीर्णाः कुरुश्रेष्ठा यस् त्व् एतान् समु-पेक्षथाः) 14. 52. 22 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 53. 22: मिथ्याचारेण कपटपूर्वकं अविरोधच्छलेन विरोधं द्रढयता); Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka chiefs were honoured by the Kuru chiefs (कुरूद्वहाः) of Hāstinapura 14. 70. 11; Vaiśaṃpāyana narrated to Janamejaya in details all the deeds of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas (कुरूणां चरितं कृत्स्नं पाण्डवानां च) 18. 5. 25. D. People in general of the Kuru country or of Hāstinapura: At the श्राद्ध ceremony of Pāṇḍu, Bhīṣma fed the people of the Kuru country and also the principal Brāhmaṇas by thousands (कुरूंश् च विप्रमुख्यांश् च भोजयित्वा सहस्रशः) 1. 119. 2; at the birth of Arjuna, an incorporeal voice prophesied that he would subdue the Kurus and others 1. 114. 31; all the people of the Kuru country prospered when the Pāṇḍavas followed धर्म; the people became free from blemish and were happy (व्यवर्धन् कुरवः सर्वे हीनदोषाः सुखान्विताः) 1. 205. 4; if Dhṛtarāṣṭra could check Duryo-dhana, all the Kuru people would be happy 2. 55. 8; Kurus, when ruled by Yudhiṣṭhira, would not be lamented (अशोच्याः कुरवो राजन्) 2. 65. 13; Kuru people waited on Yudhiṣṭhira as do the servants (कुरवः किङ्करा यथा) 4. 65. 14; Saṃjaya infor-med Yudhiṣṭhira that the spirited Kuru people were all well (कुरून् कुरुश्रेष्ठ जनं च पृच्छसि । अनामयास् तात मनस्वि-नस् ते) 5. 24. 1; Yudhiṣṭhira wished that the Kuru and the Pāñcāla people came to-gether with smiles and not cause injury to each other (स्मयमानाः समायान्तु पाञ्चा-लाः कुरुभिः सह ॥ अक्षतान् कुरुपाञ्चालान् पश्येम) 5. 31. 21-22; the conflict among the Bhāratas would mean an end of the people and the burning up of the Kurus (अन्तो नूनं भवितायं प्रजानाम् । नो चेद् … कुरून् दहेत्) 5. 32. 27; the Kuru people did not welcome war (कुरवः … युद्धं नाभिनन्दन्ति) 5. 57. 8; Kuru people counted among those who knew well the eternal धर्म and they followed it (कुरवः … धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्) 8. 30. 60-61, 75; कुरुपाञ्चालदेश्याः … धर्मं पुराणम् उपजीवन्ति सन्तो … ) 8. 30. 62; E. Kurus in the Sabhā: 1. Kurus seated in the Sabhā of the dice-game: Duryodhana cheated Yudhiṣṭhira at the game of dice in the presence of Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Vidura and the other Kuru chiefs (पश्यतां कुरुमुख्यानाम् … द्यूतेना-वञ्चयत् तदा) 5. 71. 11-12; Draupadī blamed the Kurus present in the assembly as they simply watched the transgression of the limits of the Kuru धर्म (and did not intervene) (यत्-राभ्यतीतां कुरुधर्मवेलां प्रेक्षन्ति सर्वे कुरवः सभायाम्) 2. 60. 33; Drau-padī asked the elderly Kurus in the Sabhā to answer her question (इमे कुरवः सभायाम्) 2. 60. 45; she bowed down to the elders in the Kuru assembly (गुरूणां कुरुसंसदि) 2. 62. 2; she lamented in the Sabhā as follows: she who was not seen before in the open had been brought to the Kurusabhā; she whom neither wind nor the sun saw in her house could now be seen in the Kuru assembly; that the Kurus tolerated all this showed that the times had changed (मृष्यन्ते कुरवश् चेमे मन्ये कालस्य पर्ययम्); although she was a chaste woman she was standing in the Sabhā (of the Kurus) 2. 62. 2-5, 7-8; Vidura felt that what the Kurus in the assembly talked about was sinful (पापान् मन्त्रान् कुरवो मन्त्रयन्ति);
