excellent armies of Kurus attacked Bhīma (कुरू-णां प्रवरैर् बलैर्) 8. 58. 1; Arjuna acted as god Yama to Kurus 8. 58. 4; Kurus turned back when they were burnt (निर्-दग्धाः) by Arjuna 8. 58. 18-19; ninety chariot-fighters of Kurus (here the term Kuru refers to Saṃśaptakas 8. 59. 3) chas-ed Arjuna as he was rushing towards Karṇa; Arjuna killed them 8. 59. 1, 4; other Kuru warriors (in this episode, Kuru refers to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons 8. 59. 7), un-daunted, assailed Arjuna 8. 59. 6; they obstructed Arjuna's onward march and struck him with शक्तिस्, ऋष्टिस् and other weapons 8. 59. 8; Kurus uttered sounds of grief when struck by Arjuna with arrows; Kurus lost hope about Karṇa; defeated, they turned back and fled in all directions; persecuted by Arjuna, they took refuge with Karṇa who granted them freedom from fear 8. 59. 29-30, 33-34, 37-41; Kurus thought highly of Vṛṣasena's (Karṇa's son) heroism, but knowing the prowess of Arjuna they thought Vṛṣasena was as good as dead 8. 62. 54; when Karṇa faced Arjuna, Kurus gathered together with musical instruments and, to encourage Karṇa, they blew their con-ches 8. 63. 10; Kuru and Pāṇḍava warriors (कुरुपाण्डुयोधाः) filled the earth and directions with sounds of instruments, arrows and lion-like roars, and killed their opponents; when their elephants, foot-soldiers, horses and chariot-fighters were afflicted by the arrows of Karṇa and Arjuna, they fled 8. 64. 3, 13; Arjuna alone killed two thousand chief warriors of Kurus together with their chariots, horses and charioteers (कुरुप्रवीरान् … कुरूणां  … सरथाश्वसूतान्); then the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the remaining Kurus (तवात्मजाः कुरवश् चावशिष्टाः) ran away abandoning Karṇa; Karṇa, left alone by the shattered Kurus since they were afraid, was not afflicted 8. 65. 43-45; Kurus, whose armies were routed (कुरवो भिन्नसेनाः) and stood at a distance of only an arrow-shot from Karṇa (शरपात-मात्रम् अवस्थिताः), saw the missile relea-sed by Arjuna 8. 66. 1; when Arjuna broke the flag-staff of Karṇa, the hearts of Kurus sank and they uttered a loud sound of grief (तदा कुरूणां हृदयानि चापतन् बभूव हाहेति च निस्वनो महान्) 8. 67. 15; when Karṇa was killed, Kurus, afraid and deeply wounded in battle, fled looking again and again at the shining banner of Arjuna; they all left for their camp 8. 67. 36; 8. 68. 5, 35-36; Janamejaya asked what did the Kurus, whose number had diminished, do after the death of Karṇa (अल्पावशिष्टाः कुरवः) 9. 1. 1; Kurus and Pāṇḍavas confronted each other and perished in large number 9. 3. 1; on the eighteenth day, Duryodhana was protected by Kuru chief warriors (रक्षितः कुरुपुंगवैः) 9. 7. 25; seeing Śalya stoutly facing the enemies, Kurus returned to the battlefield determined to fight till death (कुरवः संन्यवर्तन्त मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्) 9. 9. 7; Pāṇḍava warriors, being killed by Kurus, fled 9. 15. 3; all Kurus together saw the शक्ति hurled by Yudhiṣṭhira at Śalya 9. 16. 41; when Śalya fell, Kurus fled shouting words of grief (हाहाकारं विकुर्-वाणाः कुरवो विप्रदुद्रुवुः) 9. 16. 65; Kurus again returned determined to fight till the end and started fighting with Pāṇḍa-vas 9. 20. 4; Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas killed seven hundred desperate Kuru-chariot-fighters (रथान् सप्तशतान् हत्वा कुरूणाम् आततायिनाम्) 9. 22. 14; Kurus and Pāṇḍavas watched the शक्तिस् hurled by heroic Pāṇḍava warriors and by those of Śakuni, as heavenly bodies 9. 22. 43; Bhīma put to flight all the Kurus 9. 25. 36; Yuyutsu was grieved since all the Kurus, led by Bhīṣma and Droṇa, had perished; he alone survi-ved the holocaust of the Kurus (हस्ताश् च कुरवः सर्वे भीष्मद्रोणपुरःसराः अहम् एको विमुक्तस् तु … । … अस्मिन् कुरु-क्षये वृत्ते) 9. 28. 76-77, 84; Kurus, Kaliṅgas and others perished by confront-ing Bhīma 9. 32. 42; Balarāma and other sages asked Nārada news about the Kurus (यथावृत्तम् कुरून् प्रति); Nārada repor-ted to them the great destruction of Kurus just as it took place (सर्वम् एव यथावृत्तं अतीतं कुरुसंक्षयम्) 9. 53. 19-20; Pāṇḍavas had accomplished a great feat by killing Kurus led by Bhīṣma (कृत्वा सुमहत् कर्म हत्वा … भीष्म-मुखान् कुरून्) 9. 57. 10; destruction of Kuru and Pāṇḍava warriors (कुरुपाण्ड-वयोः क्षयम्) lamented by Aśvatthāman 10. 1. 29; since the start of the war a certain कृत्या used to appear at nights between the armies of Kurus and Pāṇḍa-vas 10. 6. 67; a great calamity was des-tined to overtake Kurus—Vyāsa told lamenting Dhṛtarāṣṭra (अवश्यं भवितव्ये च कुरूणां वैशसे) 11. 8. 16; women of Hāstinapura lamented the destruction of Kurus 11. 9. 19, 21; 11. 13. 14; Gāndhārī with her divine sight, saw all around the destruction of Kurus (गान्धारी कुरूणां आविकर्तनम् । अपश्यत् … दिव्येन चक्षुषा) 11. 16. 1: (however, Nī. who reads अव-कर्तनम्, Bom. Ed. 11. 16. 1, explains it as युद्धस्थानम्); having witnessed the calamity that had overtaken the Kurus (कुरूणां वैशसम्), Gāndhārī spoke to Kṛṣṇa 11. 16. 17; she said she did not imagine that such a calamity would overtake Pāñcālas and Kurus 11. 16. 26; Gāndhārī pointed towards Droṇa whom Kurus appointed their leader and challe-nged the Pāṇḍavas (कुरव आह्वयन्ति स्म पाण्डवान्) 11. 23. 29; Somadatta's wife said fortunately her husband was not alive to see the terrible destruction of the Kurus which was as good as युगान्त (कुरुसंक्रन्दनं घोरं युगान्तम्) 11. 24. 4; Gāndhārī cursed Kṛṣṇa for being deliberately indifferent to the des-truction of the Kurus (इच्छतोपेक्षितो नाशः कुरूणाम्) 11. 25. 38; but according to Kṛṣṇa, the Kurus were killed due to the fault of Gāndhārī 11. 26. 1; the Kurus who somehow got killed between battles had obtained the world of the Uttara-kurus (ये तत्र निहता राजन्न् अन्तरायो-धनं प्रति । यथाकथंचित् ते … संप्राप्ता उत्तरान् कुरून्) 11. 26. 17; Yudhiṣṭhira blamed Kuntī for the grief he and his brothers felt at the death of Abhimanyu and others and at the fall of Kurus (कुरूणां पतनेन च) 11. 27. 18; Kurus, the enemies of Pāṇḍavas, acted and (as warriors) fully accomplished their objective (अमित्रा नः समृद्धार्थाः वृत्तार्थाः कुरवः किल) 12. 7. 4 (Nī., how-ever, on Bom. Ed. 12. 7. 4; यतो वयं वृत्तार्थाः संक्षिप्तपुरुषार्था ज्ञाति-वधेन हतभाग्याः स्म ततो हेतोर् नः अस्माकम् अमित्राः समृद्धार्था इत्य् अर्थः); Yudhiṣṭhira, along with Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, performed the obsequies of Kurus prominent among whom were Bhīṣma and Karṇa (भीष्मकर्णपुरोगाणां कुरूणां) 14. 14. 15; Kṛṣṇa reported to Vasudeva and Devakī the death of Kuru warriors 14. 59. 5; destruction of Kurus due to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's fault 15. 5. 1; destruction of Kurus as destined by fate 15. 16. 1; Kṛṣṇa witnessed the annihilation of Yādavas as he did before of kings and of prominent Kurus (राज्ञां च पूर्वं कुरुपुंगवा-नाम्) 16. 5. 8; Kṛṣṇa contemplated on the destruction of the Vṛṣṇis, Andhakas and Kurus and realized that it was time for him to depart 16. 5. 18. II. Kurus in the battle of the cow-raid: The victory of Arjuna over Kurus in this battle men-tioned in the contents of the Virāṭaparvan (गोग्रहे यत्र पार्थेन निर्जिताः कुरवो युधि) 1. 2. 132; Kurus drove away sixty thousand cows of Virāṭa 4. 33. 5, 10; 4. 35. 3, 6, 12; Bhūmiṃjaya (Uttara) was to defeat the Kurus and turn back the cattle 4. 33. 14, 19; Uttara boasted that he could defeat the Kurus if he had the help of a good charioteer 4. 34. 5, 17; Kurus succeed-ed in capturing the cows since there was no one to protect them (शून्यम् आसाद्य कुरवः प्रयान्त्य् आदाय गोधनम्) 4. 34. 8; Uttara wanted the Kurus to see his heroism 4. 34. 9; Uttarā asked Bṛhannaḍā to get for her the thin (upper) garments of the Kurus led by Bhīṣma and Droṇa, when they were defeated 4. 35. 23; Bṛhan-naḍā drove the chariot towards the Kurus 4. 35. 26; Uttara's chariot to be driven in the direction of the fleeing Kurus 4. 36. 1; he wanted to defeat the Kurus 4. 36. 2; strong Kurus and their army within sight near the cremation ground 4. 36. 4; Uttara afraid to fight with the Kurus since their army had many excellent heroes, was very fierce, unassailable even by gods and was endless (बहुप्रवीरम् अत्युग्रं देवैर् अपि दुरासदम् … कुरुसैन्यम् अनन्त-कम्) 4. 36. 9, 13; Bṛhannaḍā, however, was determined to take Uttara in the midst of the Kurus who were ready to kill their opponents (मध्यम् … कुरूणां आततायिनाम् । नेष्यामि) 4. 36. 19; if not Uttara, Bṛhannaḍā was ready to fight with the Kurus 4. 36. 23; Uttara unwilling to face the Kurus even if the Kurus plunder-ed more wealth of the Matsyas 4. 36. 24; the Kurus seeing Bṛhannaḍā run after Uttara wondered who he was; they dis-cussed but came to no conclusion 4. 36. 29, 36; Bṛhannaḍā again assured Uttara that he would fight with the Kurus and asked Uttara to drive his chariot close to their army 4. 36. 44-45; 4. 40. 4; the sound which Arjuna produced with his bow was thought by the Kurus to be the sound produced by the splitting of the lightning (तं शब्दं कुरवो ऽजानन् विस्फोटम् अशनेर् इव) 4. 40. 27; Karṇa said that the Kurus may return with the booty or, seated in their chariots, watch him fight alone with Arjuna 4. 43. 21; Kṛpa remind-ed the Kurus that they were rescued from the Gandharvas by Arjuna single-handed 4. 44. 5; Uttara drove Arjuna's chariot in the direction of the Kurus and Duryo-dhana 4. 48. 13; Arjuna's chariot moved all around in the army of the Kurus 4. 49. 12; all groups of gods, Siddhas and great sages gathered in the air to witness the battle between Arjuna and Kurus 4. 51. 13; all Kurus were struck with wonder to see the battle between Arjuna and Aśvatthā-man 4. 54. 11; Arjuna said that let the Kurus and their forces act as spectators when he fought with Karṇa 4. 55. 6; Kurus would get a sight of Arjuna's Gāṇḍīva and would keep wondering whether he shot arrows with his right or left hand 4. 56. 4; Arjuna wanted to burn with the lustre of his missiles the forest of the Kuru army, with trees in the form of banners, grass in the form of foot-soldiers and lions in the form of chariot-(fighters) (ध्वजवृक्षं पत्तितृणं रथ-सिंहगणायुतम् । वनम् आदीपयिष्यामि कुरूणाम् अस्त्रतेजसा ॥ ) 4. 56. 12; Arjuna, when he employed Aindra astra, covered all the Kurus (with its lustre) 4. 58. 9; Arjuna warded off every missile of the Kuru stalwarts with a corresponding missile 4. 61. 8; when Arjuna used his Saṃmohana astra he struck the minds of (Kurus) with fear and when he blew the conch, the chief Kuru warriors were stupefied by the loud sound of the conch 4. 61. 8-11; Arjuna asked Uttara to go to the unconscious Kurus to get their (upper) garments 4. 61. 12; when Arjuna saw the chief Kuru heroes returning to Hāstinapura he was satisfied 4. 61. 25, 29; Arjuna defeated the Kurus in the battle who left (for Hāstinapura) 4. 62. 1, 7; when the defeated sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra had left, their soldiers (कुरुसैनिकाः) came out of hiding from the dense forest 4. 62. 2; Virāṭa informed about the cattle-raid of the Kurus 4. 63. 6; he knew that when the Kurus came to know about the defeat of the Trigartas, they would not keep quiet (कुरुवस् ते हि … न स्थास्यन्ति कदाचन) 4. 63. 10; Virāṭa was grieved and tormented when he knew that his son had gone to fight with the Kurus 4. 63. 15; Yudhiṣṭhira assured Virāṭa that Uttara would be able to defeat the Kurus and other kings 4. 63. 16; the minister re-ported the defeat of the Kurus and the winning back of the cows 4. 63. 18-21, 36; Uttara told that the Kurus were defeated and their (upper) garments taken away by a Devaputra 4. 64. 21, 28, 30; later it was known that it was Arjuna who won back the cows and defeated the Kurus 4. 66. 14. H. The word Kuru refers to the army of the Kurus (fighting for the Kauravas): Many hundreds and thousands of kings joined the Kurus in their conflict (with the Pāṇḍavas) (कुरू-णां विग्रहे तस्मिन् समागच्छन् बहून्य् अथ । राज्ञां शतसहस्राणि) 1. 57. 105; the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas together made eighteen अक्षौहिणीस् (अक्षौ-हिण्यो … अष्टादशैव ताः । एतया संख्यया ह्य् आसन् कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः) 1. 2. 24; Bhīṣma fought for ten days for the Kuru army, while Droṇa protected it for five days (कुरुवाहिनीम्) 1. 2. 26; march of the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas to-wards Kurukṣetra described in the (अभि-) निर्याण पर्वन् (निर्याणं पर्व च ततः कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः) 1. 2. 52 (reference to 5. 149-152); the army of the Kurus will be destroyed in war (बलं कुरूणां) 5. 57. 28; (एते नश्यन्ति कुरवो … ) 5. 146. 21, 25; the army got ready for battle at day-break (उदतिष्ठन् … सूर्योदये महत् सैन्यं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः) 6. 16. 24; army, large like an ocean (कुरूणां … सैन्यं सागर-प्रतिमं महत्) 7. 85. 81; army looked upon as a dice-player (सेनां दुरोदरं विद्धि) 7. 105. 17; looked upon as a herd of bulls (कुरुसैन्याद् विमुक्तो वै सिंहो मध्याद् गवाम् इव) 7. 116. 22; other references to the army: सेनानिवेशे … कुरु-पाण्डवसेनयोः) 5. 156. 3; 6. 42. 25; 7. 4. 12; 7. 120. 4; 12. 336. 8; destruction of the army of the Kurus, Sauvīras and Sain-dhavas, (कुरुसौवीरसैन्धवानां बल-क्षयम्) 7. 114. 17; (घ्नन्तं कुरूणाम् इषुभिर् बलानी) 7. 115. 20; 7. 133. 63; 9. 7. 34. I. References to the war between Kurus (i. e. those who fought for the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra) and the Pāṇḍavas: 1. In-quiries about the war: (i) Janamejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana how the two armies fought with each other (कथं युयुधिरे वीराः कुरुपाण्डवसोमकाः) 6. 1. 1, 2; (ii) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya (यथा तद् अभवद् युद्धं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः) 6. 15. 75; (के पूर्वं प्राहरंस् तत्र कुर-वः पाण्डवास् तथा) 6. 42. 1; 6. 111. 2; (Saṃjaya replied) 6. 111. 3; (कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च) 7. 71. 1; 7. 158. 12; (पाञ्चालाः कुरुभिः सार्धम्) 7. 81. 1, 4; 2. J. References to Kuru women of Hāstinapura (mostly of the royal family): Bhīṣma, Vidura, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and all Kuru women offered water libations to Pāṇḍu (उदकं चक्रिरे तस्य सर्वाश् च कुरुयोषिताः) 1. 118. 27; all high-ranking women of the Kurus (सर्वाः कुरुवरस्त्रि-यः) were anxious to meet newly-married Draupadī 1. 198. 23; the desires of Kuru women would remain unfulfilled after the death of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra (हत-संकल्पाः … कुरुस्त्रियः) 3. 224. 8; ser-vants of Kauravas requested help from Pāṇḍavas lest the wives of the Kurus were molested (परामर्शो मा भविष्यत् कुरु-दारेषु) 3. 237. 7; Gāndhārī and all Kuru women became unconscious hearing Saṃ-jaya say that all except ten perished in battle (सर्वाश् च कुरुयोषितः) 9. 1. 39; Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍavas and Kṛṣṇa met Kuru women (कुरुस्त्रियः समासाद्य) and they all went to Kurukṣetra; there, those women whose husbands were killed (ताः स्त्रियो निहतेश्वराः) saw their dead sons, brothers, fathers, husbands; seeing the sight they, lamenting, fell down from their vehicles (स्त्रियः … यानेभ्यो विक्रोशन्त्यो निपेतिरे); that was a very piti-able condition of Pāñcāla and Kuru women (पाञ्चालकुरुयोषाणां कृपणं तद् अभून् महत्); Gāndhārī showed to Kṛṣṇa daughters-in-law who were lamenting like कुररीस् (स्नुषा मे … प्रकीर्णकेशाः क्रोशन्तीः कुररीर् इव माधव); they remembered their near ones and ran to them separately; those women from noble families (परमाङ्गनाः), afflicted by sorrow and grief, lamented; their faces had dried up (मुखानि परमस्त्रीणाम्; वक्त्राणि कुरुयोषिताम्); grieving Kuru women described by Gāndhārī 11. 16. 10-11, 13, 15, 18-19, 42-58; Kuru women, took away their ornaments, upper garments, girdles and, weeping due to excessive grief, knowing their धर्म, gave water libations to their relatives and friends; when they were performing these rites, the river became fordable and then again spread out widely (भूषणान्य् उत्तरीयाणि वेष्टनान्य् अवमुच्य च । … कुरुस्त्रियः॑उदकं चक्रिरे सर्वा रुदन्त्यो भृशदुःखिताः । … धर्मज्ञाः प्र-चक्रुः सलिलक्रियाः ॥ ) 11. 27. 2-4; all Kuru women, Kuntī and Draupadī, mounted different vehicles and went to Hāstinapura led by Vidura 12. 38. 41; Kuru women (कुरुयोषितः) held Subhadrā, grieving over Abhimanyu's death, in their arms and lamented 14. 60. 26; Citrāṅgadā and Ulupī approached Draupadī, Subhadrā and other Kuru women (याश् चान्याः कुरुयोषितः) with modesty 14. 90. 2; knowing Kuntī's firm resolve to retire to forest and seeing the Pāṇḍavas return without her, Kuru women wept loudly (कुरुस्त्रियः । … प्ररुरुदुस् तदा ॥ ) 15. 24. 11; wives of Kuru chiefs followed Pāṇḍavas on foot when they too on foot started towards the आश्रम of Dhṛtarāṣṭra (स्त्रियश् च कुरुमुख्यानां पद्भिर् एवान्वयुस् तदा) 15. 31. 2; Saṃ-jaya introduced by name Draupadī and all other Kuru women to the ascetics in the आश्रम (सर्वान् नामाभिनामतः ।  … सर्वाश् चान्याः कुरुस्त्रियः) 15. 32. 4. कुरुजाङ्गल: Kurujāṅgala nt. (sg.), m. (pl.): Name of the country with Hāstinapura as capital and people living there (while referring to people used in m. pl.); occasionally the term refers to the battlefield at Kurukṣetra (5. 150. 4; 6. 5. 6; 8. 1. 17). A. Description: Called देश 1. 102. 22; राष्ट्र 1. 191. 9; 12. 38. 23; after the birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura, Kurujāṅgala was looked upon as the most distinguished among all countries (देशा-नां कुरुजाङ्गलम्) 1. 102. 22. B. Epic events: (1) To Dhṛtarāṣṭra belonged as ancestral share the rulership of the Kurujāṅgala country and its people (पित्र्यं राज्यं महाराज कुरवस् ते सजाङ्गलाः) 5. 53. 7; (2) Kuntī and the Pāṇḍavas, with the hermits from the Himā-laya, reached the Kurujāṅgala 1. 117. 8; (3) Kuntī blessed Draupadī that she will be the anointed queen of the countries and cities among which the Kurujāṅgala was the principal one (कुरुजाङ्गल-मुख्येषु राष्ट्रेषु नगरेषु च) 1. 191. 9; (4) To reach the Magadha country, Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna started from the Kurus and passed through the Kuru-jāṅgala (कुरुभ्यः प्रस्थितास् ते तु म-ध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम्) 2. 18. 26; (5) People of the Kurujāṅgala country saw Draupaḍī helpless in the Sabhā (यदा जनौ-घः कुरुजाङ्गलानां कृष्णां सभायाम् अवशाम् अपश्यत्) 3. 180. 20; (6) Dhṛta-rāṣṭra asked sage Maitreya if he reached Kurujāṅgala comfortably 3. 11. 9; (7) The Kurujāṅgala people and their chiefs grieved while taking leave of the Pāṇḍavas (मुख्याश् च सर्वे कुरुजाङ्गलानाम् । … जनौघं कुरुजाङ्गलानाम् 3. 24. 5-6; (8) The entire Kurujāṅgala country and the country around it became disturbed when the Kaurava army came together (कृत्स्नं च कुरुजाङ्गलम्) 5. 19. 29; (9) Janamejaya wanted Vaiśaṃpāyana to tell him what transpired at Kurujāṅgala (= Kurukṣetra) (संभ्रमे तुमुले तस्मिन् यद् आसीत् कुरुजाङ्गले) 5. 150. 4; (10) According to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, crores of heroic men had gathered at Kurujāṅgala (= Kurukṣetra) (कोट्यश् च लोकवीराणां समे-ताः कुरुजाङ्गले) 6. 5. 6; (11) After the fall of Karṇa, Saṃjaya went to Hāstina-pura to report what had happened at Kurujāṅgala (= Kurukṣetra) (आचख्यौ धृटराष्ट्राय यद् वृत्तं कुरुजाङ्गले) 8. 1. 17; (12) Yudhiṣṭhira went to Bhīṣma with the kings who survived the battle and all Kurujāṅgala people (सर्वे च कुरु-जाङ्गलाः) 13. 153. 22; (13) Dhṛtarāṣṭra requested the Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras of the Kurujāṅgala country to give him permission to go to the forest; he said they had lived for a long time happily with the Kurus (ब्राह्मणाः कुरुजाङ्गलाः । क्षत्रियाश् चैव वैश्याश् च शूद्राश् चैव … ॥ भवन्तः कुरवश् चैव बहुकालं सहोषि-ताः । … परस्परस्य सुहृदः परस्परहिते रताः ॥ ) 15. 13. 13-14; hearing those words the people of Kurujāṅgala (कुरु-जाङ्गलाः) wept with their voices chocked due to tears 15. 13. 21; 15. 14. 17; 15. 15. 6; they consulted among themselves and appointed one Brāhmaṇa to speak on their behalf 15. 15. 7-10. F. Past events: (1) A certain Bāhlīka chief while once living away in Kurujāṅgala remembered his beloved and sang a गाथा 8. 30. 19-20; (2) The large quantity of gold accumulat-ed at Kurujāṅgala was given away by king Suhotra in a sacrifice (तद् धिरण्यम् अपर्यन्तम् आवृत्तं कुरुजाङ्गले । ईजानो वितते यज्ञे) 12. 29. 26. [See Jāṅgala].
कुलक: Kulaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (कुलिन्दाः कुलकाश् चैव) 6. 10. 61.
कुलिन्द: Kulinda m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (कुलिन्दाः कुलकाश् चैव) 6. 10. 61.
कुलिन्दोपत्यका: Kulindopatyakā f. (pl.): Name of a Janapada (low-land of Kulinda). Listed by Saṃjaya among the nor-thern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; कुलिन्दोपत्यकास् तथा) 6. 10. 54.
कुलूत: Kulūta m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (अभीसाराः कुलूताश् च) 6. 10. 52; Kṣemadhūrti, their king (कुलूताधिपतिः 8. 8. 35), was killed by Bhīma (निहतं नृपतिं दृष्ट्वा कुलूता-नाम्) 8. 8. 45.
कुशद्वीप: Kuśadvīpa m.: Name of one of the seven Dvīpas of the terrestrial world. A. Location: They lie to the north (apparently of the Jambudvīpa) (उत्तरेषु तु कौरव्य द्वीपेषु) 6. 13. 1. B. Disti-nctive features as described by Saṃjaya to Dhṛtarāṣṭra 6. 12. 2: (1) It has a bunch of Kuśa grass in the middle of the country (कुशद्वीपे कुशस्तम्बो मध्ये जनपद-स्य ह) 6. 13. 6; (2) There are six exce-llent mountains (पर्वतोत्तमाः) in the Kuśadvīpa viz.: (1) Sudhāman, full of corals and unassailable (विद्रुमैश् चितः  … दुर्धर्षः), (2) Dyutimant, golden (हेमपर्वतः), (3) Kumuda, (4) Puṣpa-vant, (5) Kuśeśaya, and (6) Hari; the distance between these mountains doubles as one goes from one mountain to the other (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभा-गशः) 6. 13. 9-11. C. Characteristics common to all the seven Dvīpas: (1) All Dvīpas are progressively double the size of the Dvīpa preceding it (as one proceeds towards the north ?) and they are all sur-rounded by mountains on all sides (पर-स्परेण द्विगुणाः सर्वे द्वीपा नराधिप । सर्वतश् च महाराज पर्वतैः परिवारि-ताः ॥ ) 6. 13. 3; (2) All Dvīpas receive different kinds of jewels from Jambudvīpa (जम्बुद्वीपात् प्रवर्तन्ते रत्नानि विविधान्य् उत । द्वीपेषु तेषु सर्वेषु) 6. 13. 26; (3) The state of health and the duration of life progressively doubles in these Dvīpas owing to ब्रह्मचर्य, truth, and self-control of the Brāhmaṇas (विप्राणां ब्रह्मचर्येण सत्येन च दमेन च । आरोग्यायुःप्रमा-णाभ्यां द्विगुणं द्विगुणं ततः) 6. 13. 27; (4) In these islands there is only one Janapada and even if in some there are many Janapadas there is only one धर्म in all of them (एको जनपदो राजन् द्वीपेष्व् एतेषु भारत । उक्ता जनपदा येषु धर्मश् चैकः प्रदृश्यते ॥ ) 6. 13. 28; (5) Prajāpati himself, raising his दण्ड, protects the people of these Dvīpas, both dull and learned; he is their king, is kind to them, their father, and their grand-father (ईश्वरो दण्डम् उद्यम्य स्वयम् एव प्रजापतिः । द्वीपान् एतान् महा-राज रक्षंस् तिष्ठति नित्यदा ॥ स राजा स शिवो … स पिता स पितामहः । गोपायति नरश्रेष्ठ प्रजाः सजदपण्डिताः ॥ ) 6. 13. 29-30; (3) People eat food received ready for use (भोजनं चात्र कौरव्य प्रजाः स्वयम् उपस्थितम् । सिद्धम् एव महाराज भुञ्जते तत्र नित्यदा ॥ ) 6. 13. 31. D. Epic event: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to describe to him the different Dvīpas including the Kuśadvīpa 6. 12. 2. E. Past event: Upamanyu told Kṛṣṇa that the rulership of Kuśadvīpa was given to Vidyutprabha (Dānava) by the Un-born god (Śiva) (कुशद्वीपं च स ददौ राज्येन भगवान् अजः) 13. 14. 57.
कुशबिन्दु: Kuśabindu m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (रोमाणः कुश-बिन्दवः) 6. 10. 54.
कुशल: Kuśala1 m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37; (कुशलाः कुनटास् तथा) 6. 10. 50.

Kuśala2 m.: Name of a Deśa related to the Krauñca mountain on the Krauñca Dvīpa. Each of the six mountains on this Dvīpa is related to some Deśa (देशांस् तत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि … क्रौञ्चस्य कुशलो देशो … ) 6. 13. 20; these Deśas are resorted to by gods and Gandharvas (देवगन्ध-र्वसेविताः) 6. 13. 23.
कुशिक: Kuśika, Kauśika m. (pl.): Designa-tion of the descendants of king Kuśika; also referred to as Kuśikavaṃśa 13. 3. 5, Kauśika vaṃśa (13. 52. 4). A. History: (1) Kuśikas were those born in the lineage of Jahnu of boundless spirit (अन्वयाः कुशिका राजन् जह्नोर् अमित-तेजसः) 1. 89. 29; (2) They were made firm in this world by Viśvāmitra (तेन (i. e. by Viśvāmitra) … कुशिकवंशश् च … स्थापितो नरलोके ऽस्मिन्) 13. 3. 3, 5; (3) Yudhiṣṭhira once asked Bhīṣma how one born in the Kṣatriya lineage of Kauśikas became a Brāhmaṇa (कौशिकाच् च कथं वंशात् क्षत्राद् वै ब्राह्मणो ऽभवत्) 13. 52. 4; Bhīṣma then told him how the rela-tionship between Kuśikas and Bhṛgus was formed (भृगूणां कुशिकानां च प्रति सं-बन्धकारणम्) 13. 56. 19. B. Descrip-tion: Great (महन्त्), learned (विद्वंस्), full of many Brahmarṣis (ब्रह्मर्षिशत-संकुल), and praised by Brāhmaṇas (ब्राह्-मणसंस्तुत) 13. 3. 5. C. Past events: (1) Cyavana wanted to burn all the descen-dants of Kuśika and destroy them (चिकी-र्षन् कुशिकोच्छेदं संदिधक्षुः कुलं तव) 13. 55. 12; 13. 52. 9; (2) Vasiṣṭha, controlling his anger, did not wish to des-troy the descendants of Kuśika on account of the fault of Viśvāmitra (यस् तु नोच्छे-दनं चक्रे कुशिकानाम् उदारधीः । विश्वा-मित्रापराधेन धारयन् मन्युम् उत्त-मम् ॥ ) 1. 164. 6.
कृमि: Kṛmi m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned by Bhīma among the six-teen peoples whose kings were defilers of their families (कुलपांसनाः), most wicked men in their families (कुलेषु पुरुषाध-माः), and who extirpated their kinsmen and friends together with their relatives (ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च स-बान्धवान्); one of them was the rude Vasu of the Kṛmis (कृमीणाम् उद्धतो वसुः) 5. 72. 11, 13.
केकय: Kekaya, Kaikaya, Kaikeya m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and the warriors of this country; they are often mentioned along with Pāñcālas (or Sṛñjayas) and Matsyas in the war. A. Use of the terms: The term Kekaya is specifically used to refer to the five brothers fighting on the side of the Pāṇḍa-vas (one of them was named Bṛhatkṣatra 7. 81. 7); the warriors and the five brothers also referred to as Kaikaya or Kaikeya (6. 52. 4); a warrior once referred to as केकयज (8. 4. 69); a Kekaya princess (Su-kumārī) referred to as Kaikeyī (1. 90. 45). B. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37. 5; (सुराषृराः केकयास् तथा) 6. 10. 47. C. Relationship with Pāṇḍavas: The five brothers were the sons of the sister of Pāṇḍavas' mother (भ्रातरः पञ्च कैकेया  … मातृष्वसुः सुता वीराः) 7. 9. 53 (how-ever, see below Nī.'s remark under F. Epic events No. 4). D. Description (often only of the five brothers, occasionally of all warriors): High-souled (महात्मन्) 1. 61. 11; having the colour of a fire-fly (इन्द्रगोपकवर्ण) 5. 139. 26; 7. 9. 52 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 141. 26: इन्द्रगोपकः वर्षासु प्रचलन् रक्तजन्तुस् तद्वर्णास् ताम्रा इत्य् अर्थः); religious (धार्मिक) 7. 9. 52; heroic (वीर) 7. 9. 52-53; brave (शूर) 5. 47. 23; 5. 49. 35; 6. 18. 14; 8. 8. 19; 11. 25. 13; of great prowess (महा-वीर्य) 3. 13. 2; 7. 34. 5; 8. 31. 21; strong (बलिन्) 5. 22. 19; (बलवन्त्) 6. 112. 107; always on their guard (संयत्त) 6. 112. 107; of true valour (सत्यविक्रम) 7. 9. 52; eminent Kṣatriyas (क्षत्रियर्षभ) 3. 13. 4; tigers among men (नरव्याघ्र) 5. 19. 25; best and prominent among the kings (पार्थिवर्षभसत्तम) 1. 61. 11; famous among the world (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 13. 2; great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 6. 112. 107; 7. 135. 16; bowmen (धन्विन्) 6. 112. 7; having large bows (महेष्वास) 2. 4. 27; 3. 252. 16; 5. 22. 19; 5. 49. 35; 6. 45. 29; 6. 73. 56, 58, 59; 11. 26. 36; versed in the science of archery (धनुर्वेदविशारद) 6. 70. 33; (धनुर्वेदविद्) 6. 57. 13; who had learnt the use of missiles (कृतास्त्र) 7. 34. 6; wearing shining bracelets (रुचिरा-ङ्गद) 11. 25. 13; having gold banners (सुवर्णविकृतध्वज) 6. 73. 58; having copper-coloured standards, and chariot-garlands (ताम्रध्वजरथस्रजः) 11. 25. 14; having red banners (लोहितकध्वज) 7. 22. 11; 7. 24. 40; wearing well-polished armours (सुमृष्टकवच) 5. 49. 35; wearing armours shining like heated gold (तप्त-काञ्चनवर्माणः) 11. 25. 14; having red armours, weapons and banners (रक्तवर्-मायुधध्वज) 7. 9. 52; in war, invincible by enemies (अजेयाः शत्रुभिर् युधि) 6. 57. 13; arrogant in war (युद्धदुर्मद) 7. 34. 6; ready to die (in war) (तनुत्यज्) 6. 18. 14. E. History: The five great and strong Asuras Ayaḥśiras, Aśvaśiras, Ayaḥśaṅku, Gaganamūrdhan, and Vegavant were born as the five great, prominent kings among the Kekayas (पञ्चैते जज्ञिरे … केक-येषु … पार्थिवर्षभसत्तमाः) 1. 61. 10-11. F. Epic events: (1) At the birth of Arjuna a non-corporal voice prophesied that he would defeat Kekayas and other peoples 1. 114. 31; 8. 48. 7 (here the pro-phecy is said to have been heard a week after Arjuna's birth (सप्ताहजाते त्वयि) 8. 48. 6; (2) Kekayas mentioned among those who waited on Yudhiṣṭhira in his Sabhā 2. 4. 27; (3) The Kekaya Kṣatriyas (क्षत्रियाः 2. 48. 16; राजन्याः 2. 48. 13) brought tribute in hundreds for Yudhi-ṣṭhira's Rājasūya 2. 48. 13, 16; (4) The five Kekaya brothers, along with others, came to meet the Pāṇḍavas during their वनवास (केकयाश् च … भ्रातरो लोक-विश्रुताः) 3. 13. 2; they took leave of Pāṇḍāvas and left the forest 3. 23. 48 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 22. 51: केकयाश् सहदेवश्यालाः); (5) Bhīma assured Yudhiṣṭhira that with the support of Sṛñjayas and Kekayas they were sure to get back the lost kingdom 3. 34. 85; (6) Kṛṣṇa mentioned Kekayas among those who would help them in the war 3. 120. 25; (7) Draupadī warned Jayadratha that if he tried to abduct her, Kekayas and Vṛṣṇi warriors would chase him to rescue her (केकयाश् चापी सर्वे । … मम … पदवीं चरेयुः) 3. 252. 16; but according to 11. 22. 12 Kekayas were Jayadratha's compa-nions (यदा कृष्णाम् उपादाय प्राद्रवत् केकयैः सह): (8) Drupada asked Yudhiṣṭhira to send messengers to Keka-yas to seek their support 5. 4. 8; (9) The five Kekaya brothers joined Duryodhana with the army of one अक्षौहिणी (केकयाश् च … सोदर्याः पञ्च … । … कौरव्यम् अक्षौहिण्या समाद्रवन्) 5. 19. 25; Keka-yas were among those who were brought together by Duryodhana to fight with the Pāṇḍavas (ये राजानः पाण्डवायोधनाय समानीता धार्तराष्ट्रेण … केकयाश् च) 5. 30. 23; Dhṛtarāṣṭra was able to win over half of the Kekayas (अर्धं मे केकया लब्धाः) 7. 23. 7 (also see the next); (10) The five Kekaya brothers, driven out from the Kekaya country, joined the Pāṇḍavas anxious to get back the king-dom of the Kekayas (अवरुद्धा बलिनो केकयेभ्यो महेष्वासो भ्रातरः सन्ति पञ्च । केकयेभ्यो राज्यम् आकाङ्क्षमाणा युद्धार्थिनस् चानुवसन्ति पार्थान्) 5. 22. 19 (Nī. on 5. 22. 20: केकयेभ्यो देशेभ्यः । अवरुद्धाः बहिर् निःसा-रिताः । … पूर्वम् अस्मदीया अपि संप्रति पाण्डवान् अनुवसन्ति अनुसरन्ति); 5. 49. 7, 35; 5. 52. 2; they do not respect Dhṛta-rāṣṭra 5. 53. 17; 5. 54. 3; 5. 139. 26; 5. 142. 3; Dhṛtarāṣṭra considered the presence of the Kekayas on the side of the Pāṇḍavas a great asset to them (केकयाश् चैव  … क एताञ् जातु युध्येत) 7. 61. 39, 41; since Kekayas were divided, one Kekaya brother was killed by his own brother fighting from the opposite side (केकयेनैव विक्रम्य भ्रात्रा भ्राता निपातितः) 8. 4. 69; (11) When Duryodhana would see the Kekayas rushing against him, he would repent the war 5. 47. 23; but Duryodhana assured Dhṛtarāṣṭra that he would defect them 5. 60. 25; (12) Kekayas were among those who followed Kṛṣṇa some distance when he started for Hāstinapura 5. 81. 32; (13) When Yudhiṣṭhira started for Kuru-kṣetra, Kekayas followed him 5. 149. 58; 5. 150. 2; (14) Kekayas (on the side of the Kauravas), led by Droṇa, ready to march against Pāṇḍavas (केकया … । प्रय-युः सर्व एवैते भारद्वाजपुरोगमाः) 5. 196. 5; (15) Mentioned among the twelve Janapadas who protected Bhīṣma with their force of chariot-riders (केकयास् तथा । … द्वादशैते जनपदाः … ।महता रथवंशेन तेऽभ्यरक्षन् पितामहम् ॥ ) 6. 18. 13-14; (16) Arjuna expected Kekayas to act only as spectators when Bhīma would fight with his गदा (केकया  … एते तिष्ठन्ति … प्रेक्षकास् … ) 6. 19. 14; (17) On the first day of the war, the five Kekaya brothers with their armies fought with five Gāndhāras and their armies 6. 43. 73; they rushed to protect Abhimanyu 6. 45. 30; Bhīṣma felled them with his arrows (केकयांश् च … । भीष्मः … पात-याम् आस मार्गणैः) 6. 45. 54; (18) On the second day of the war, Virāṭa, supported by Kekayas, guarded the rear of the Krauñcavyūha of Pāṇḍavas 6. 46 54; Bhīṣma, protected by Kekayas (those on the side of the Kauravas) and other warriors, opposed Arjuna (गुप्तः प्राच्य-सौवी रकेकयैः) 6. 48. 21; (19) On the third day of the war, Kaikeyas (Kauravas' side) stood at the head of the Garuḍavyūha of the Kauravas (शीर्षम् आस्तां … । … मत्स्यकैकेयैर् … ) 6. 52. 4; (20) On the same day Kekayas stood behind Yudhi-ṣṭhira in the middle of the Ardhacandra-vyūha of the Pāṇḍavas 6. 52. 16; (21) The chief Kekayas (मुख्याः) (Kaura-vas' side), Trigartas and Madras, totalling thirty-five thousand, surrounded Arjuna and Abhimanyu as ordered by Duryo-dhana (सह केकयैः पञ्चत्रिंशतिसाह-स्रास् तव पुत्रेण चोदिताः) 6. 57. 12-13; Dhṛṣṭadyumna, with his army, marched against them 6. 57. 16; (22) Sātyaki, Cekitāna and Abhimanyu engaged Śālvas and Kekayas 6. 68. 8; (23) Matsyas and Kekayas encircled Arjuna 6. 70. 33; (24) On the sixth day of the war, the five Kekaya brothers stood on the left side of the Makaravyūha of the Pāṇḍavas (वामं पार्श्वं समाश्रिताः); when Droṇa and Bhīṣma started killing Sṛñjayas and Keka-yas they began to flee 6. 71. 19, 32; at mid-day, Kekayas, Draupadī's sons, and Dhṛṣṭa-ketu, led by Abhimanyu, formed the Sūci-mukhavyūha and broke the chariot-army of the Kauravas (रथानीकं बिभिदुह्) 6. 73. 54-55; they fought with Dhṛtarāṣṭra's eight sons 6. 75. 21; Duḥśāsana fought a wonderful battle with the five Kekaya brothers (तद् अद्भुतम् इवाभवत्) 6. 74. 25; the five Kekaya brothers rushed to help Śatānīka; five Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, Dur-mukha and others, attacked the advancing Kekaya brothers 6. 75. 50, 52; (25) On the same day, Bhagadatta, along with Madras, Sauvīras and Kekayas stood at the chest (उरस्य् अभून् … ) of the Krauñcas vyūha of the Kauravas 6. 71. 18; (26) On the eighth day of the war, Kekayas, Abhi-manyu and others surrounded the Supra-tīka elephant of Bhagadatta 6. 91. 39-40; Bhagadatta pierced the (five) Kekayas with five नाराच arrows; that was a fierce battle (तुमुलं युद्धम्) of Bhagadatta with Pāñcālas, Sṛñjayas, and Kekayas 6. 91. 67, 80; (27) On the tenth day of the war, Ambaṣṭhas, Kekayas and others, instigated by Duryodhana, attacked Arjuna; he burnt them with his missiles; then they did not return 6. 112. 110, 112, 114; Keka-yas (Kauravas' side) mentioned among the twelve Janapadas who, although affli-cted with arrows and pained by wounds, did not abandon Bhīṣma fighting with Arjuna ( … केकयैः सह । द्वादशैते जनपदाः शरार्ता व्रणपीदिताः । संग्रामे न जहुर् भीष्मम्) 6. 114. 77; (28) Eleventh day: Kekayas mentioned among those who did many valorous acts and checked the army of Droṇa 7. 7. 4, 6-7; Droṇa bruised the five principal warriors (brothers) of Kekayas with arrows (स केकयानां प्रवरांश् च पञ्च … शरैः प्रमृद्य) 7. 7. 24; (द्रोणेन निहताः शूराः शेरते … । … सर्वे भ्रातरः पञ्च केकयाः ॥ ) 11. 25. 13; (29) Dhṛtarāṣṭra felt that Droṇa must have been encircled and confused by Kekayas and others when Dhṛṣṭadyumna killed him 7. 8. 27-28; he wanted Saṃjaya to tell him who checked the five Kekaya brothers when they advanc-ed towards Droṇa 7. 9. 52; (30) Kekayas mentioned among those who rushed to rescue the sons of Draupadī when they were attacked by Aśvatthāman 7. 15. 11; Kekayas among those who checked Droṇa advancing towards Yudhiṣṭhira 7. 15. 32; (31) On the 12th day, Kekayas (on Kauravas' side) stood at the neck of the Suparṇavyūha (ग्रीवायां … मद्र-केकयाः) 7. 19. 8; (32) Kekayas (on Pāṇḍavas' side) attacked Droṇa when they saw Yudhiṣṭhira running away from him; Droṇa scattered them away and defeated them again and again 7. 20. 18-19, 23; when a Pāñcāla prince was killed by Droṇa (7. 20. 48), angered Pāñcālas, Kekayas and others rushed at him shouting ‘kill Droṇa, kill Droṇa’; Droṇa agitated them all (व्यक्षोभयत्); when they were getting killed by Droṇa they trembled (समकम्-पन्त) 7. 20. 49, 53; Duryodhana delighted to see Pāñcālas, Kekayas and others put to flight by Droṇa's arrows (द्रोणसाय-कैह् प्रणुन्नान्) 7. 21. 7; (33) Karṇa told Duryodhana that Kekayas and other warriors would rally round Bhīma espe-cially when instigated by him (विशेषतश् च भीमेन … अभिचोदिताः) 7. 21. 23-24; in the battle that followed, Kekayas follow-ed Virāṭa; the five Kekaya brothers rode in chariots drawn by firefly-coloured horses and carrying red-coloured banners 7. 22. 8, 11; (34) There was extremely tumultuous fighting (उत्पिञ्जलकं यु-द्धम्) between Matsyas and Kekayas (Kauravas' side) in which the horse-riders, chariot-fighters and elephant-riders were not afraid (अभीताश्वरथद्विपम्) 7. 24. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 25. 31: उत्पिञ्जजलकम् अत्यन्ताकुलम्); (35) Karṇa tried to halt the march of five Kekaya brothers towards Droṇa; angered, they showered arrows on him; Karṇa repeatedly covered them with arrows; neither Karṇa nor they could be seen as they were covered with arrows 7. 24. 40-42; (36) On the thirteenth day, Kekayas and others attacked Droṇa 7. 34. 5; Bhīma assured Abhimanyu that he, along with Kekayas and others, would follow him in his attempt to make an opening in the Cakravyūha 7. 34. 22; Kekayas mentioned among those who raised a loud roar (केक-याश् चैव सिंहनादम् अथानदन्) seeing Abhimanyu compelling Duḥśāsana to sit down in his chariot; they advanced to-wards Droṇa's army to get through it 7. 39. 13, 17; (37) The day Abhimanyu was killed, great sound which used to be heard in the evenings issuing from the houses of Kekayas (on Kauravas' side) could not be heard by Dhṛtarāṣṭra (शिबिरे यो महाध्वनिः । श्रूयते सो ऽद्य न तथा केकयानां च वेश्मसु) 7. 61. 16; (38) On the fourteenth day, Droṇa repul-sed the attack on him by Pāñcālas and Kekayas 7. 70. 13; Duryodhana pierced Kekayas with sharp arrows 7. 128. 23; (39) During the night war, Kekayas men-tioned among those who fought with Droṇa 7. 129. 7; Droṇa killed Kekaya warriors with swift arrows 7. 130. 12; when Bhīma killed Durmada and Duṣkarṇa (Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons), Kekayas and others applauded him 7. 130. 38; Duryodhana pointed out to Karṇa that the Kaurava army was surrounded by Pāñcālas, Matsyas and Kekayas 7. 133. 3; Karṇa assured him that he would kill all of them including Keka-yas (केकयान् … शकलीकृत्य) 7. 133. 11; Duryodhana wanted Aśvatthāman to check Kekayas before they, protected by Arjuna, destroyed his army 7. 134. 8; Aśvatthāman assured him that he would fight with the Kekayas and the rest 7. 135. 10; he challeng-ed Kaikeyas and others and asked them to remain steady and show their skill in the use of the missiles (ततो ऽब्रवीत् स कैकेयान् पाञ्चालान् गौतमीसुतः । … स्थिरीभूताश् च युध्यध्वं दर्शयन्तो ऽस्त्रलाघवम्) 7. 135. 16; thus challenged, they showered arrows on Aśvatthāman, but were killed by him 7. 135. 17-18; Kekayas and others rushed towards Droṇa and made all attem-pts to kill him (सर्वोद्योगेन) 7. 141. 60; Yudhiṣṭhira wanted Sātyaki and Kekayas to attack Droṇa with great speed (अभि-द्रवन्तु वेगेन) 7. 159. 6; Droṇa defeat-ed Kekayas and killed them 7. 161. 32, 35; (40) On the fifteenth day, Droṇa killed many Kekayas and others with his ब्रह्मास्त्र 7. 165. 100-101; after the fall of Droṇa, Aśvatthāman assured Duryodhana that he would put to flight (विद्रावयिष्यामि) Kekayas and others with his नारायणास्त्र 7. 166. 52; (41) After the death of Droṇa, Karṇa fought bravely to kill Kekayas 8. 2. 18; (42) Kekayas (Kauravas' side) listed by Saṃjaya among those killed by Arjuna 8. 4. 45; (43) On the sixteenth day, Kekayas helping Bhīma riding on an elephant rush-ed against the army of the Kauravas 8. 8. 19; (44) When Anuvinda was killed, (the hearts of) Kekayas (on Kauravas' side) were dried up (शोषयन् केकयान् सर्वान्) 8. 9. 21; Sātyaki dissipated the large army of Kekayas 8. 9. 34; (45) Kekayas mentioned among those who showered various weapons on Karṇa (नानाशस्त्रैर् अवाकिरन्) 8. 21. 26-27; (46) On the seventeenth day, Duryodhana, protected by Kekayas and Madras, stood at the rear of the Vyūha of the Kauravas 8. 31. 21; Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman and Śakuni fought with Kekayas 8. 32. 16-17; (47) Kekayas were among those who attacked Karṇa to kill him 8. 32. 43; they checked the advance of Karṇa towards Yudhiṣṭhira 8. 33. 9; they checked Vasuṣeṇa 8. 33. 22; Karṇa check-ed the onward march of Bhīmasena, Keka-yas and Sṛñjayas towards Kṛpa 8. 38. 16; 8. 40. 1; when Bhīma left, Karṇa killed Kekayas by thousands 8. 40. 4; (48) Bhīmasena fought with Kurus, Madras and Kekayas (Kauravas' side) 8. 40. 69; (49) Kekayas and others, protected by Arjuna, destroyed Kauravas' army 8. 51. 6; (50) Bhīṣma reported to have killed Kekayas and others warriors along with their kings 8. 51. 27; (पृथिवी पालांश् चेदिपान्चालकेक-यान्) 8. 51. 32; (51) On the eighteenth day, Duryodhana checked the advance of Kekayas and others 9. 20. 34; (52) Keka-yas accompanied Jayadratha when he tried to abduct Draupadī (यदा कृष्णाम् उपादाय प्राद्रवत् केकयैः सह) 11. 22. 12; (53) At the instance of Yudhiṣṭhira, Sudhar-man (Duryodhana's Purohita), Dhaumya and others cremated the dead bodies of Kekayas and other fallen heroes (केक-यांश् च … । … पावकैः समदाहयन्) 11. 26. 36, 38 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 11. 26. 24: सुधर्माणम् दुर्योधनपुरोहितम्). D. Other events: (1) A certain king of Keka-yas doing स्वाध्याय and observing rigid vows in a forest was possessed by a dread-ful Rakṣas (केकयानाम् अधिपतिं रक्षो जग्राह दारुणम्) 12. 78. 7; (2) Śatayūpa was once a great king of the Kekayas (स हि राजा महान् आसीत् केकयेषु परंतपः) 15. 25. 10. E. Use in a title: Certain princes (probably the well known five Kekaya brothers) referred to as ‘princes of the Kekayas’ (केकयराजपुत्राः) 3. 48. 38.
केकरक: Kekaraka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (त्र्यङ्-गाः केकरकाः) 6. 10. 60.
केतुमाल: Ketumāla m.: Name of Dvīpa. A. Location: One of the four Dvīpas on the four sides of mountain Meru (तस्य पार्श्वे त्व् इमे द्वीपाश् चत्वारः … । भद्रा-श्वः केतुमालश् च) 6. 7. 11; to the west of Meru (मेरोस् तु पश्चिमे पार्श्वे केतु-मालो महीपते) 6. 7. 29. B. Characteri-stics: (1) A large Jambūṣaṇḍa, beautiful like Nandana, is located there 6. 7. 29; see Vol. I. p. 356); (2) People live there for ten thousand years; men have golden complexion, women are like Apsaras; they are free from sickness and grief, and are always of delightful disposition; all have lustre like that of heated gold (अनामया वीतशोका नित्यं मुदितमानसाः । जायन्ते मानवास् तत्र निष्टप्तकनकप्रभाः) 6. 7. 30-31.
केरल: Kerala m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Included by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also call-ed Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (द्रविडाः केरलाः) 6. 10. 57; Sahadeva subjugated them in his expedi-tion to the south (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1; (दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 8; (दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 37; lay along the coast (ततः समुद्रतीरेण … पुण्ड्रान् सकेरलान्) 14. 83. 29. B. Description of the people: Of pleasing appearance (प्रियदर्शन), having long-arms (दीर्घभुज), broad-chest (व्यूढो-रस्क), red teeth (रक्तदन्त), tall (प्रा-ंशु) 8. 8. 15; they had long hair (दीर्घ-केश), wore chaplets (आपीडिन्), they put on garments of different colours (नाना-विरागवसन), and smeared their bodies with fragrant powder (गन्धचूर्णावचूर्-णित) 8. 8. 16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 12. 16: आपीडिनः भूषावन्तः नाना पृथक् विविधरागाणि वसनानि येषां ते); equipped with swords (बद्धासि), holding nooses in hand (पाशहस्त), they were capable of forcing back the (enemy's) elephants (वारणप्रतिवारण) 8. 8. 17; they liked battles (प्रियाहव), carried bows and quivers filled with arrows (चापहस्त, कलापिन्), fought on foot (पत्ति) 8. 8. 18; their valour was like that of elephants in rut (मत्तमातङ्गविक्रम) 8. 8. 16 and fierce (घोररूपपराक्रम) 8. 8. 18; they were ready to die with their comrades-in-arms (समानमृत्यवो राजन्न् अनीकस्थाः परस्परम्) 8. 8. 17. C. Epic events: (1) Sahadeva, in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya, subjugated them just by sending envoys and made them pay tribute 2. 28. 47-48; (2) They were hired for war by Pāṇḍavas by paying them large sums (भृता वित्तेन महता  … ओड्राः सकेरलाः) 8. 8. 15; (3) After defeating Meghasaṃdhi in Magadha, Arjuna, with the Aśvamedha horse, went along the coast to the Vaṅga, Puṇḍra and Kerala countries (ततः समुद्रतीरेण वङ्गान् पुण्ड्रान् सकेरलान्) 14. 83. 29.
कोकनद: Kokanada m. (pl.): Name of a people. They probably lived in Punjab; chara-cterized as क्षत्रियस्; mentioned along with the Trigartas; Arjuna defeated them in his expedition to the north (प्रययाव् उत्तरां दिशम् 2. 24. 1; 2. 23. 9) before the Rājasūya (ततस् त्रिगर्तान् कौन्तेयो दार्वान् कोकनदाश् च ये । क्षत्रिया बहवो राजन्) 2. 24. 17.
कोङ्कण: Koṅkaṇa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (कोङ्कणा माल-वाणकाः) 6. 10. 58, 5.
कोपन: Kopana m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (समङ्गाः कोप-नाश् चैव) 6. 10. 59.
कोल्लगिर: Kollagira m. (pl.): Name of a degra-ded Kṣatriya tribe. Mentioned among those Kṣatriyas who lost their upper caste and became low owing to their not respecting Brāhmaṇas (कोल्लगिरास् तथा । … तास् ताः क्षत्रियजात-यः । वृषलत्वम् अनुप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 35. 17-18 [see the next].
कोल्लगिरेय: Kollagireya m. (pl.): Tribes living on Kollagiri in the south. Living near the southern ocean (प्र-ययौ … दक्षिणं सलिलार्णवम्) 14. 84. 10; Arjuna fought with them while he accompanied the horse of the Aśvamedha 14. 84. 11 [Identical with the preceding ? See Kollagirī Vol. I, p. 319].
कोसल: Kosala m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people; the name is found twice as Kośala (2. 13. 26; 8. 17. 3) and once as Kosalā (f.) (9. 37. 22 कोसलाभागे). A. Location: Distinguished as eastern and southern Kosalas; the eastern Kośalas formed part of the Kuntī country (पूर्वाः कुन्तिषु कोशलाः) 2. 13. 26; in the east, beyond the river Sarayū; beyond Kosala lay Mithilā and the rivers Mālā and Car-maṇvatī 2. 18. 28 (see Epic events no. 3 below); in the south, beyond the Kosalas lay the region called Dakṣiṇāpatha (अतः परं च देशो ऽयं दक्षिणे दक्षिणापथः) 3. 58. 22 (see Past events no. 1 below); its capital town Ayodhyā (see B. 2 below). B. Designation of certain kings after Kosala: (1) Bṛhadbala called कोसलाधिपति 2. 27. 1; 8. 4. 21; 11. 25. 10; कोसलानाम् अधिपः 7. 46. 20; कोसलराज 7. 46. 21; कोसला-नाम् भर्ता 7. 46. 22; Sukṣatra's father (Bṛhadbala ?) called कोसलाधिपति 7. 22. 47; (2) Ṛtuparṇa, king of Ayodhyā, called कोसलाधिप 3. 71. 23; (3) Kṣemadarśin called कोसलानाम् अधिपतिः (कोसलानाम् आधिपत्यं संप्राप्ते क्षेमदर्शिनि) 12. 83. 6. C. Description: (1) Holy (उत्तरे कोसलभागे पुण्ये) 9. 37. 22; (2) Their warriors: Brave (शूर) 8. 8. 19 and heroic (वीर) 8. 33. 22; (शूरवीर) 8. 32. 17; skilled in battles while riding elephants (कोशला … गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 3. D. Characterization: Kosalas were counted among those who knew the eternal धर्म (कोसला … धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्) 8. 30. 60-61; they comprehended a thing as soon as they saw it (प्रेक्षितज्ञाश् च कोसलाः) 8. 30. 79. E. Epic events: (1) Bhīṣma defeated all Māgadhas, Kāśis and Kosalas and brought two maidens for Vicitravīrya 13. 44. 37; (2) Kośalas, along with many other peoples, resorted to the west as they were afraid of Jarāsandha 2. 13. 26-28; (3) Bhīma, Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa, while going to the Magadha country, had to cross the river Sarayū before they could reach the eastern Kosala (संतीर्य सर-यूं रम्यां दृष्ट्वा पूर्वांश् च कोसलान् । अतीत्य जग्मुर् मिथिलां मालां चर्मण्व-तीम् नदीम् ॥ ) 2. 18. 28; (4) Kṛṣṇa once defeated them 7. 10. 15; (5) Karṇa also had once defeated them 8. 5. 19; (6) Some of the Kosalas sided with the Kauravas (and others with the Pāṇḍavas) (अर्धं मे केकया लब्धाः काशिकाः कोसलाश् च ये) 7. 23. 7; (7) On the second day of war, Kosalas and others, led by Duryodhana, guarded the army of Śakuni 6. 47. 15-16; (8) On the twelfth day of war, Kosalas, on the side of the Pāṇḍavas, attacked Droṇa when they saw Yudhiṣṭhira retreating from Droṇa; he scattered their army 7. 20. 18-19; (9) On the sixteenth day of war, they rush-ed at the Kaurava army; their chariot-fighters, elephant-riders, and excellent foot soldiers, who were delighted, danced mak-ing various sounds and laughed (नाना-विधरवैर् हृष्ता नृत्यन्ति च हसन्ति च) 8. 8. 19-20; Bhīma, seated on an elephant was in the midst of their army 8. 8. 21; (10) On the same day, Kośalas (on the side of the Kauravas), skilled in elephant battles, attacked Dhṛṣṭadyumna to kill him; they showered arrows, तोमरस् and नाराचस् (कोशला … गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 3-4; (11) On the seventeenth day of war, Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman and Śakuni fought with Kosalas (on the side of the Pāṇḍavas) and killed many of them 8. 32. 17-18; (12) On the same day, Kosalas, along with other warriors, checked the advance of Vasuṣeṇa 8. 33. 22; (13) On the same day, Arjuna killed many Kosalas (on the side of the Kauravas) 8. 37. 2; (14) Kosala country mentioned among those reached by the Aśvamedha horse 14. 84. 4. F. Past events: (1) Nala showed to Damayantī the roads leading to Dakṣiṇā-patha; one of them led to Kosala country (एते गच्छन्ति बहवः पन्थानो दक्षिना-पथम् … एष पन्था विदर्भाणाम् अयं गच्छति कोसलान् । अतः परं च देशो ऽयं दक्षिणे दक्षिणापथः ॥ ) 3. 58. 20, 22; (2) For the sacrifice of Auddālaka, per-formed in the northern Kosalā, Sarasvatī appeared as Manohradā (उत्तरे कोसला-भागे … औद्दालकेन यजता … सरस्वती ॥ आजगाम … मनोह्रदेति विख्याता) 9. 37. 22-23.
कौकुट्टक: Kaukuṭṭaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … कौकुट्टकास् तथा चोलाः) 6. 10. 56, 58.
कौकुर: Kaukura m. (pl.); Name of a people. (1) Characteristics: They are mention-ed among those who acted on Kṛṣṇa's advice and subdued their enemies to gladden their friends (कौकुराः सृञ्जयाश् च । उपा-सीना वासुदेवस्य बुद्धिं निगृह्य शत्रून् सुहृदो नन्दयन्ति) 5. 28. 11; (2) Epic events: At the time of Rājasūya, they lived in Yudhiṣṭhira's house like docile slaves (आवर्जिता इवाभान्ति निघ्नाश् चैत्रकिकौ-कुराः) 2. 46. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 50. 20; आवर्जिताः दासवद् वशगाः); the Kṣatriyas among them brought wealth in hundreds for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya (कौकुरास् … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातश-त्रवे) 2. 48. 14-16.
कौमार: Kaumāra m. (pl.): Name of a Varṣa. It is related to the mountain Raivata-(ka) (6. 12. 16) in the Śākadvīpa (वर्षाणि तेषु कौरव्य … रैवतस्य तु कौमारः) 6. 12. 22, 24.
कौरव: Kaurava, Kauraveya, Kauravya (pl.): Name of a people; like the word Kuru, these words also have various significances (the choice of the word depending on metrical requirements). A. People of the Kuru country: Duryodhana, the king of the Kauravas (कौरवाणाम् अधिपः) 6. 55. 106; Yudhi-ṣṭhira, the king of the Kauravas (स राजा  … कौरवाणाम्) 5. 32. 9; he was the pro-tector and the ruler of Kaurava people 5. 147. 31; Karṇa, while praising the people of certain countries as opposed to the Bāhlī-kas, said that Kauraveyas were the reli-gion incarnate (i. e. they practised धर्म scrupulously) (कौरवेयाः स्वधर्मः) 8. 30. 73 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 45. 28 reads कौरवेयास् तु धर्म्यम् which he explains as धर्म्यं धर्माद् अनपेतं कर्म मानयन्तीति शेषः). B. Those born in the lineage of Kuru and living at Hāstinapura; the term may occasionally include also those like Droṇa, Kṛpa and others not born in Kuru's line but who sided with Dhārtarāṣṭras; the term may also refer not only to the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra but also the sons of Pāṇḍu; occasionally the word कौरववंश or कौरव वंश is used instead of simple कौरव: All Kauravyas sat near the sages who brought with them Kuntī and the five Pāṇḍavas 1. 117. 16; Kauravas and others delighted to hear the arrival of the Pāṇḍavas 1. 1. 73; the sage (Vyāsa) composed in the ninth पर्वन् three thousand two hundred and twenty stanzas to describe the events of the famous Kauravas (कौरवाणां यशोभृ-ताम्) 1. 2. 177; Parikṣit was born in the lineage of the Kauravas (कौरववंश-भृत्) 1. 36. 8; Śakuni took his sister to the Kauravas 1. 103. 14; Pāṇḍu described as the bearer of the fame of the Kaura-vas; he procured for them fame and kingdom (कौरवाणां यशोभृता) 1. 105. 8; (पाण्डुनावर्जितं राज्यं कौरवाणां यशस् तथा) 7. 62. 15; Bhīṣma and other Kauravas did not see the end of the riches brought by Pāṇḍu 1. 105. 24; Bhīṣma, Vidura and other Kauravas grieved at the funeral of Pāṇḍu and Mādrī 1. 118. 26; Droṇa accepted Kauravas (i. e. also the Pāṇḍavas) as his pupils 1. 122. 40; Dhṛtarāṣṭra told Duryodhana that they (i. e. Dhṛtarāṣṭra himself and his sons) and the Pāṇḍavas were the same to Kauraveyas (i. e. to Bhīṣma and other Kauraveyas); if they acted contrary to the wishes of the Kauraveyas they may be killed by them (समा हि कौरवेयाणां वयम् एते च … ।  … ते वयं कौरवेयाणां … कथं न वध्यतां तात गच्छेम) 1. 130. 14, 15; Vidura gave to Drupada and others gifts given to them by Kauravas (यथा दत्तानि कौरवैः) 1. 198. 13; Bhīṣma and all other Kauravas enquired through Vidura about the well-being of Drupada in all respects 1. 198. 17; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Kauravas to receive the sons of Pāṇḍu 1. 199. 12; Arjuna was one who brought fame to Kauravas (in-cludes the Pāṇḍavas) (कौरवाणां यशस्-करम्) 1. 206. 1; Balarāma willing to kill all Kauravas (includes the Pāṇḍavas) (अद्य निष्कौरवाम् एकः करिष्यामि वसुन्-धराम्) 1. 212. 31; Bhīṣma was the leader of the Kauravas (includes Pāṇḍavas) 2. 38. 3; Kauravas delighted to see Pāṇḍavas in Hāstinapura 2. 52. 30; asking Draupadī to come to the Sabhā meant that the doom of the Kauravas was imminent (मन्ये प्राप्तः संक्षयः कौरवाणाम्) 2. 60. 12; forcing virtuous women to appear in the Sabhā meant that the Kaura-veyas were acting against their ancient, eternal धर्म (स नष्टः कौरवेयेषु पूर्वो धर्मः सनातनः) 2. 62. 9; Duḥśāsana defiled the good name of Kauravas (कौरवाणां यशोहरः) 2. 62. 12; Vidura was impartial, hence was respe-cted by the Kauravas (includes Pāṇḍavas) (समश् च त्वं संमतः कौरवाणां) 3. 5. 2; Vidura spoke what was proper for Kauravas (यत् क्षमं कौरवाणाम्) 3. 6. 13; destruction of Kauravas was certain 3. 6. 16; Vyāsa wanted to tell what was beneficial to the Kauravas 3. 9. 1; if Kauravyas wished to remain alive (कौर-व्याञ् जीवमानान्) conciliation with the Pāṇḍavas was necessary 3. 10. 23; Kṛṣṇa would have come to Hāstinapura at the time of the game of dice even if not in-vited by the Kauravas 3. 14. 2; Dhṛta-rāṣṭra surrounded by all Kauravas 3. 242. 19; Duryodhana expressed his desire to the Kauravas to perform Rājasūya 3. 243. 14; Dhṛtarāṣṭra was the central figure among Kauravas (including Pāṇḍa-vas) (मेढीभूतः कौरवाणाम्) 5. 36. 71; Kṛṣṇa to approach the Kauravas for peace 5. 70. 89; Kṛṣṇa to find out the view of the Kauravas towards war 5. 71. 33; 9. 62. 2; Kṛṣṇa did not deserve to be arrest-ed by the Kauraveyas 5. 86. 18; Kṛṣṇa dismissed Kauravas 5. 89. 37; Kṛṣṇa advis-ed Duryodhana to see that the Kauravas were not destroyed without any one to survive and that the (Kaurava) family did not perish (अस्तु शेषं कौरवाणां मा पराभूद् इदं कुलम्) 5. 122. 58; bad omens for Kauravas 5. 141. 18; Kaura-vas destined to be destroyed 5. 144. 24; Bhīṣma carried forward the line of the Kauravas (कौरवं वंशम् उद्वहन्) 5. 145. 32; Bhīṣma had saved the race of the Kauravas which had (almost) perished (प्रनष्टः कौरवो वंशस् त्वयायं पुनर् उद्धृतः) 5. 146. 18; Arjuna born in the family of Kauravas 5. 155. 31; Balarāma could not be a witness to the destruction of the Kauravyas 5. 154. 33; Citrāṅgada was installed on the throne of the Kauravas 5. 169. 18; Kauravas, who had assembled to witness Bhīṣma battle with Paraśu-rāma and who stood by him, were distress-ed to see Bhīṣma fall on the ground 5. 183. 11; Bhīṣma, the foremost among the Kauravas (कौरवाणां ऋषभात्) 7. 11. 3; (कौरवाणां धुरंधरे) 12. 46. 23; 12. 52. 14; 12. 54. 4; (कौरवाग्र्य) 13. 153. 5; Duryodhana prided himself on his birth in the Kuru lineage (कौरवे वंशे) 9. 30. 21; the jewel held by Aśvatthāman on his head more valuable than the riches collected by Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas 10. 15. 28; attempts were made by Yudhiṣṭhira to avoid conflict among the Kauravas (i. e. those siding with Duryo-dhana and with Pāṇḍavas (अविग्रहे कौरवाणाम्) 11. 8. 37; Kauravyas, while fighting amongst themselves got killed (युध्यमाना हि कौरव्याः कृन्तमानाः परस्परम्) 11. 13. 16; the battle led to the annihilation of Kauravas (वैशसं घोरं कौरवान्तकरम्) 11. 27. 20; Gaṅgā spoke to Kauravas (i. e. to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Yuyutsu and the Pāṇḍavas) (कौरवान् अभ्यभाषत) 13. 154. 19; Arjuna called the foremost among Kaura-vas (कौरवाणां धुरंधरे) 14. 78. 36; Dhṛtarāṣṭra admitted his fault to Kauravas that he installed Duryodhana as their chief (ममापराधात् तत् सर्वम् इति ज्ञेयं तु कौरवाः … दुर्योधनम् कौरवाणाम् आधिपत्ये ऽभ्यषेचयम्) 15. 5. 1-2; when Dhṛtarāṣṭra left for the forest, women of the royal family of Kauravas (कौरव-राजवंश्याः) uttered loud cry 15. 21. 4; all Kaurava women made a round of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī (प्रजग्मुस् ते प्रदक्षिणम् । … सर्वाः कौरवयोषितः) 15. 44. 49. C. Those present in the Sabhā of Hāstinapura: 1. The द्यूत-सभा: Vikarṇa exhorted the Kauravas to reply to Draupadī's question (विब्रूत॥। तद् धि वक्ष्यामि कौरवाः) 2. 61. 19; none of the Kauravyas present in the Sabhā replied to the question (न विब्रुवन्ति कौरव्याः प्रश्नम् एतम्) 2. 61. 50; Drau-padī exhorted the Kauravas present in the Sabhā to reply to her question 2. 62. 11-13; Bhīma spoke in the assembly of the Kauravas (संसदि कौरवाणाम्) 2. 68. 25; Nārada prophesied that the Kauravas seated in the assembly would perish in the coming fourteenth year 2. 71. 30; Karṇa abused Draupadī (in the Sabhā) in the pre-sence of all Kauravas 7. 112. 39; citizens of Hāstinapura grieved when at the end of the द्यूत in the assembly hall of Kaura-vas, Pāṇḍavas went out of Hāstinapura (द्यूते राजन् कौरवाणां सभायाम्) 15. 21. 12; 2. The राजसभा of the Kauravas: 1. Saṃjaya reminded the Kauravas (present in the assembly) of their ancient धर्मस् (एतान् धर्मान् कौरवाणां पुराणान्) 5. 29. 29; Saṃjaya addressed the Kauravas seated in the Sabhā (5. 46. 2, राजसभा 5. 46. 3) after his return from the Pāṇḍavas (तद् विजानीत कौरवाः) 5. 46. 15 (those present in the Sabhā included Bhīṣma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vidura, Somadatta, Duryo-dhana and other sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and also Droṇa, Kṛpa, Śalya, Kṛtavar-man, Jayadratha, Aśvatthāman, Śakuni, Karṇa, Ulūka (5. 46. 3-9); Karṇa spoke to Duryodhana in the assembly of Kauravas (संसदि कौरवाणां) 5. 61. 1; Duḥśāsana feared that the Kauravas might tie up Duryodhana and hand him over to Yudhiṣṭhira (बद्ध्वा किल त्वां दास्यन्ति कुन्तीपुत्राय कौरवाः) 5. 126. 22; Karṇa always boasted in the संसद् of the Kauravas 8. 46. 35. D. Although it is difficult always to distinguish between those born in Kuru family in gene-ral and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in parti-cular, in the following references the terms Kaurava, Kauraveya and Kauravya (pl.) seem to refer to the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra: 1. 1. 73; 1. 122. 43; 2. 61. 5; 3. 9. 3; 3. 26, 17; 3. 225. 4; 3. 230. 8; 3. 232. 17, 19; 3. 233. 5; 3. 235. 2, 17; 4. 25. 5; 5. 6. 17; 5. 26. 27; 5. 29. 15, 17; 5. 36. 72; 5. 47. 59; 5. 64. 8; 5. 70. 43; 5. 151. 15; 6. 1. 25; 6. 4. 9; 6. 16. 39; 6. 41. 25, 53, 80; 6. 48. 23; 6. 53. 4; 6. 84. 34; 6. 85. 12, 18; 6. 93. 26; 6. 107. 15; 6. 110. 42; 7. 135. 32; 7. 167. 24; 8. 5. 22; 8. 6. 2; 8. 58. 28; 9. 15. 16; 12. 42. 9; 14. 52. 13; 15. 21. 4(a); (पाण्डवानां च ये योधाः कौरवा-णां च सर्वशः) 15. 40. 5. E. In the following references the term Kaurava or Kauravya refers to the Pāṇḍavas: 1. 138. 8; 3. 1. 2; 3. 93. 3; 3. 222. 55; 3. 244. 16; 4. 4. 8; 4. 32. 40; 12. 50. 10-11; 14. 88. 15. F. The term Kaurava some-times refers to the warriors born in the Kuru family and even others not born in that family but who joined the Kauravas; (sometimes it is used as an adj. (fem. -ई) to refer to the Kaurava army in general: कौरवं सैन्यम् 6. 41. 27; 6. 54. 25; 7. 113. 11 (सिन्धुसौवी रकौरवम्); 7. 139. 30; 8. 40. 3; 9. 18. 13; कौरवं बलम् 8. 51. 8; कौरवी सेना 6. 54. 18; 7. 135. 4; 7. 146. 45; 8. 17. 47; 8. 36. 40; 8. 54. 23; 9. 9. 59; (कौरवी चमू 9. 9. 62 कौरवी पृतना 9. 10. 9): (a) In the great battle with the Pāṇḍavas: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa and many others, as well as many kings had joined the side of the Kauravas and, together with their sons, counsellors and soldiers they formed the army of the Kauravas; they were apportion-ed money and all enjoyments (संश्रिताः कौरवं पक्षं … सर्वे कौरवसैन्य-स्य सपुत्रामात्यसैनिकाः । संविभक्ता हि मात्राभिर् भोगैर् अपि च सर्वशः) 3. 37. 9, 11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 36. 13 मात्राभिः अंशपरिच्छेदैः); the very spacious land became very crowded with the army of the Kauraveyas 5. 19. 31; Bhīṣma, the chief warrior of the Kauravas (कौरवाणां प्रवीरे) 5. 47. 35; Kauravas eager to fight with the Pāṇḍavas (कौरवाणां युयुत्स-ताम्) 5. 56. 52; Kaurava army of eleven अक्षौहिणीस् 5. 152. 23; Bhīṣma became the general of the Kauravas 5. 162. 4; Pāṇḍa-vas and Somakas faced Kauravas on the Kurukṣetra 6. 1. 3; the Kṣatriyas praised the Kaurava heroes 6. 41. 25; Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna was to kill the Kauravas 6. 46. 34; Arjuna killing the Kaurava army (विनिघ्नन् कौरवानीकम्) 6. 48. 19; Kaura-vas recognized Bhīṣma by the mark on (his banner) (चिह्नमात्रेण) 6. 48. 58; the व्यूह of the Kaurava army impregn-able 6. 53. 7; no one could save the chariot (i. e. the chariot-fighter Bhīṣma) of the Kauravas from enraged Kṛṣṇa (नासौ रथः सात्वत कौरवाणां क्रु-द्धस्य मुच्येत रणे ऽद्य कश्चित्) 6. 55. 83; Kauraveyas dejected to see Arjuna (6. 56. 9); Kauravas acted as advised by Bhīṣma and left for their camp 6. 60. 70, 73; Pāṇḍavas attacked the Kauravas and the latter fought with them 6. 71. 13, 22, 36; the large armies of Kauravas were arranged in a व्यूह by Bhīṣma, Droṇa and others (कौरवाणां महाचमूः) 6. 83. 4; Bhīmasena killed Kauraveyas 6. 85. 24; the princīpal Kaurava heroes (कौरवाणां महारथाः) faced Bhīma's attack 6. 90. 24; Droṇa, Duryodhana, Śalya and Aśva-tthāman named among the principal heroes of Kauravas 6. 90. 41; Arjuna faced the attack of the Kaurava army 6. 91. 78; many Pāṇḍava warriors, difficult to be killed in battle, were put to death in battle by Kauravas (अवध्या बहवो वीराह् सं-ग्रामे … । निहताः कौरवैः संख्ये) 6. 92. 4; Kauravas would not try to save their lives 6. 99. 46; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked: Did Karṇa fill up the gap of Kauravas caused by the fall of Bhīṣma ? (अपि तत् पूरयां चक्रे … यत् … कौरवाणाम् अपावृतम्) 7. 1. 48; after Bhīṣma, Karṇa to be the refuge of Kauravas 7. 4. 8; Pāṇḍavas and Kaura-vyas struck one another with arrows 7. 6. 31; if Pāṇḍavas were defeated, Kṛṣṇa would kill Kauravas 7. 10. 35; Kauravas surrounded Pāñcālas on all sides; they were obstructed by Droṇa and Kauravyas 7. 21. 9, 14; Arjuna killed Kauravyas with arrows 7. 27. 12; he showered arrows on the army of Kauravas 7. 29. 28; कौशिज: Kauśija m. (pl.): Name of Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (पाञ्चालाः कौशिजाश् चैव) 6. 10. 40, 37, 5.
क्रथक: Krathaka m.: Name of a people. Caturyu (Jarāsandha ?) conquered Pāṇḍyas, Krathakas and Kaiśikas on the strength of his knowledge (in the use of missiles ?) (चतुर्युः स महाराज भोज इन्द्रसखो बली । विद्याबलाद् यो व्यजयत् पाण्ड्यक्रथककैशिकान्) 2. 13. 20.
क्रौञ्चद्वीप: Krauñcadvīpa m.: Name of a द्वीप। A. Location: It lay to the west of the great mountain Meru (क्रौञ्चद्वीपो  … अपरेण महामेरोर् … ) 12. 14. 22; the great mountain Krauñca, full of jewels, was in Krauñcadvīpa (क्रौञ्चद्वीपे महा-क्रौञ्चो गिरी रत्नचयाकरः) 6. 13. 7, 17; the Deśa of the Krauñcadvīpa was known as Kuśala (क्रौञ्चस्य कुशलो देशो … ) 6. 13. 20. B. Description: It resembled Jambūdvīpa; and the Śākadvīpa which lay to the east of Meru resembled Krauñcadvīpa (जम्बूद्वीपेन सदृशः क्रौञ्चद्वीपो … । क्रौञ्चद्वीपेन सदृशः शाकद्वीपो … ) 12. 14. 22-23; the Deśas of all Dvīpas were frequented by gods and Gandharvas (देव-गन्धर्वसेविताः) 6. 13. 23; the people of these Dvīpas got jewels of all sorts from the Jambudvīpa; due to chastity, truthful-ness and self-control of the twice-born, health and longevity was doubled in each next Dvīpa; all Dvīpas had only one Janapada and one धर्म; god Prajāpati himself protected the Dvīpas with his raised दण्ड; he was their king, source of their welfare, their father and grand-father; he protected dull and learned alike; people there always got their food cooked by itself and ready to serve (विप्राणां ब्रह्मचर्येण सत्येन च दमेन च । आरोग्यायुःप्रमाणाभ्यां द्वीगुणं द्विगु-णं ततः ॥ … ईश्वरो दण्डम् उद्यम्य स्वयम् एव प्रजापतिः । द्वीपान् एतान् महा-राज रक्षंस् तिष्ठति नित्यदा ॥ स राजा स शिवो राजन् स पिता स पितामहः । … भोजनं चात्र कौरव्य प्रजाः स्वयम् उपस्थितम् । सिद्धम् एव महाराज भुञ्जते तत्र नित्यदा ॥ ) 6. 13. 26-31. C. Epic events: (1) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to des-cribe to him the Krauñcadvīpa along with the other द्वीपस् 6. 12. 3; (2) Draupadī reminded Yudhiṣṭhira that he had once caused Krauñcadvīpa to tremble (as also theor the द्वीपस्) (दण्डेन मृदितस् त्वया) 12. 14. 22.
क्षुद्रक: Kṣudraka m. (pl.): Name of a people, often mentioned along with Mālavas. A. Description: Described as Kṣatri-yas 2. 48. 16. B. Epic events: (1) They and Mālavas brought wealth in hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 48. 14; (2) On the first day of war, Duryodhana, along with Kṣudraka, Mālava and other warriors, took position to protect the army of Śakuni (क्षुद्रकमालवैः अभ्यरक्षत  … सौबलेयस्य वाहिनीम्) 6. 47. 16; (3) On the third day, they and Mālavas attacked Arjuna at the instance of Bhīṣma 6. 55. 74; towards the end of the day, they were killed by Arjuna which was looked upon as a great feat not possible for any other warrior (महत् कृतं कर्म ध-नंजयेन कर्तुं यथा नार्हति कश्चिद् अन्यः) 6. 55. 130; (4) On the eighth day, they and Mālavas accompanied Droṇa who followed Bhīṣma 6. 83. 7; (5) On the fifteenth day, after the fall of Droṇa, Aśvatthāman, along with twenty Kṣudra-kas, rushed towards Dhṛṣṭadyumna 7. 171. 35; (6) Mentioned by Saṃjaya among those on the side of the Kauravas who were killed during the first fifteen days of war 8. 4. 46.
कर्ण: Karṇa told Śalya that the glory of all the Vāsudevas was established in Kṛṣṇa (सर्वेषां वासुदेवानां कृष्णे लक्ष्मीः प्रतिष्ठिता) 8. 27. 62 [See Vṛṣṇi].
कुण्डधार: Kuṇḍadhāra m.: Name of a cloud. A. Description: An attendant of gods (देवानुचर) 12. 263. 6; lustrous (कुण्ड-धारस्य तेजसा) 12. 263. 13; of great lustre (महाद्युति) 12. 263. 17, 20; of great fame (महायशस्) 12. 263. 27; magnanim-ous (महात्मन्) 12. 263. 7. B. Kuṇḍa-dhāra figures in an ancient narrative (इतिहासं पुरातनम्) told by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira in reply to his question: What is most profitable among the three Puruṣārthas viz. धर्म, अर्थ and काम (2. 263. 1-2); in the narrative, Kuṇḍadhāra obliges a Brāhmaṇa due to affection for his devotee (कुण्डधारेण यत् प्रीत्या भक्तायोपकृतं पुरा) 12. 263. 2-55; the narrative runs as follows: A certain poor Brāhmaṇa desired to obtain wealth in order to perform a sacrifice; he therefore worshipped many deities but did not get wealth; he then wondered which could be that one deity which would show him favour quickly; he then saw standing near him the cloud Kuṇḍadhāra (जलधरं कुण्ड-धारं st. 6) who appeared before him assuming an agreeable form (सौम्येन वपुषा st. 6); the Brāhmaṇa felt assured by Kuṇḍadhāra's form and felt that he would definitely give him ample wealth; the Brāhmaṇa became his devotee and worshipped Kuṇḍadhāra with incenses, perfumes, garlands and oblations (ततो धूपैश् च गन्धैश् च माल्यैर् उच्चावचैर् अपि । बलिभिश् चापि … , st. 9); the cloud, satisfied, told the Brāhmaṇa that there were expiations for the sins committed due to killing a Brāhmaṇa, drinking wine, theft, breaking a vow, but there was no expiation for the sin of ungratefulness (कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः st. 11); अधर्म was the child of craving, anger of envy, greed of insult (निकृत्याः), and that an ungrateful person did not deserve progeny (कृतघ्नो नार्हति प्रजाम् st. 12); then the Brāhmaṇa, lying on the कुश grass, due to the lustre (तेजस्) of Kuṇḍadhāra, saw in a dream (निदर्शनम् अपश्यत st. 14), Maṇibhadra distributing kingdoms and wealth as desir-ed by gods (मणिभद्रं व्यादिशन्तम् … । तत्र देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति राज्यानि च धनानि च st. 15-16); Kuṇḍadhāra fell at the feet of Maṇibhadra; Maṇibhadra, at the instance of gods, asked Kuṇḍadhāra what he desired; Kuṇḍadhāra replied that if the gods were satisfied with him they should show that kind of favour to the Brāhmaṇa which would lead him to happiness (अस्या-नुग्रहम् इच्छामि कृतं किंचित् सुखो-दयम् st. 19); again, at the instance of the gods, Maṇibhadra told Kuṇḍadhāra that he was willing to give the Brāhmaṇa as much wealth as desired by him; Kuṇḍa-dhāra then, reflecting that a man's (wealth) was fickle, decided to fix the Brāhmaṇa's mind on practising austerities (विचार्य कुण्डधारस् तु मानुषं चलम् अध्रुवम् । तपसे मतिम् आधत्त ब्राह्मणस्य यशस्-विनः) 12. 263. 22; Kuṇḍadhāra therefore told Maṇibhadra that he would not seek wealth for the Brāhmaṇa, but that the Brāhmaṇa be devoted to धर्म; he desir-ed that the Brāhmaṇa should take delight in धर्म and should live following the धर्म (भवेद् एष तु धार्मिकः । धर्मे ऽस्य रमतां बुद्धिर् धर्मं चैवोप-जीवतु । ) 12. 263. 25; when Maṇibhadra persisted on giving the Brāhmaṇa kingdom and various kinds of happiness since that was what one aspired to get by follow-ing धर्म, Kuṇḍadhāra did not change his mind and wanted his Brāhmaṇa devotee to live following the धर्म; the gods were pleased with him; Maṇibhadra told Kuṇḍadhāra that the gods were satisfied with him and that the Brāhmaṇa's mind would be fixed on धर्म and that he would be a धर्मात्मा; Kuṇḍadhāra was delight-ed for having obtained what was desired in the form of a boon not easily obtained by others; the Brāhmaṇa saw thin garments around him but his mind was not deluded; abandoning them, he went to the forest and practised severe austerities; he felt that if he so desired he could certainly give some one even kingdom (12. 263. 30-39); at that juncture Kuṇḍadhāra again appeared before the Brāhmaṇa due to his friendship with him and the severe austerities per-formed by him; the Brāhmaṇa, surprised, received him according to the rites; Kuṇḍa-dhāra told the Brāhmaṇa that he had now obtained the highest divine insight (दिव्यं ते चक्षुर् उत्तमम् 12. 263. 42) and by using it the Brāhmaṇa should see the ulti-mate fate of the kings and the worlds they would get; then the Brāhmaṇa by his divine eye saw thousands of kings sunk in the hell; Kuṇḍadhāra wondered that if the Brāhmaṇa, after worshipping him was to get unhappiness, what kind of favour had he done to him ? He therefore asked the Brāhmaṇa (to use his divine eye and) to realize that it was futile to run after various longings because the door to heaven was closed for such men (कामान् इच्छेद् कथं नरः । स्वर्गद्वारं हि संरुद्धं मानु-षेषु विशेषतः ॥ 12. 263. 45); the Brāhmaṇa then saw that lust, anger, greed, fear, arrogance, sleep, drowsiness, laziness hinder men from going to heaven (ततो ऽपश्यत् स कामं च क्रोधं लोभं भयं मदम् । निद्रां तन्द्रीं तथालस्यम् आवृत्य पुरुषान् स्थितान् ॥ 12. 263. 46); Kuṇḍadhāra again told the Brāhmaṇa that the vices, mentioned before, stopped men from going to heaven; gods were afraid of such men; (these vices), as ordained by the gods, create obstacles all around (तथैव देववचनाद् विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति सर्वशः ॥ 12. 263. 47); no one who was not permitted by gods could be virtuous; the Brāhmaṇa, due to his auste-rities, could confer kingdoms and wealth on others; the Brāhmaṇa fell at the feet of the cloud (तोयधारिणे i. e. Kuṇḍa-dhāra) and told him that he had done a great favour to him; he requested Kuṇḍa-dhāra to forgive him for having formerly envied him (पुरा ते यद् असूयितम्) due to his hankerings and greed; Kuṇḍadhāra embraced the Brāhmaṇa and told him that he had forgiven him and then disappeared; the Brāhmaṇa then roamed through the skies due to his austerities to which he was led by Kuṇḍadhāra; due to his virtuousness he also gained what he wanted and the highest bliss (विहायसा च गमनं तथा संकल्पितार्थता । धर्माच् छक्त्या तथा योगाद् या चैव परमा गतिः ॥ ) 12. 263. 53.
कौस्तुभ: Kaustubha m.: Name of a jewel. A. Origin: It arose from the ocean (मन्थध्वम् उदधिं देवा … 1. 15. 13; 1. 16. 12); (मथ्यातां कलशोदधिः 1. 15. 12); (समुद्रम् उपतस्थिरे 1. 16. 8); when it was churned by the gods and the demons to obtain nectar (देवा मथितुम् आरब्धाः समुद्रं … । अमृतार्थिनस् … सहिता दैत्य-दानवाः 1. 16. 12; कौस्तुभश् च … उत्पन्नो ऽमृतसंभवः) 1. 16. 35; 5. 100. 12. B. Descrption: A jewel (मणि) 1. 16. 35; 5. 92. 13; 12. 45. 15; best among jewels (मणिरत्न) 5. 100. 12; heavenly (दिव्य), lustrous (श्रीमन्त्), and brilliant due to rays (मरीचिविकच) 1. 16. 35. C. Nārā-yaṇa (Kṛṣṇa) wears it: It rests on the chest of Nārāyaṇa (नारायणौरोगतः) 1. 16. 35; on the chest of Kṛṣṇa (कृष्णम् … कौस्तुभेन उरःस्थेन मणि-नाभिविराजितम्) 12. 45. 13, 15; 5. 92. 13; D. Epic events: (1) When Kṛṣṇa started for Hāstinapura to mediate between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kauravas he wore the Kaustubha jewel and appeared very bright due to excellent lustre (कौस्तुभं मणिम् आमुच्य श्रिया परमया ज्वलन्) 5. 92. 13; (2) when Yudhiṣṭhira went to meet Kṛṣṇa after his coronation, he saw him adorned with Kaustubha jewel (कौस्तुभेन उरः-स्थेन) 12. 45. 15. E. Viṣṇu (Hari), Nārāyaṇa (Kṛṣṇa Vāsudeva) referred to as किरीटकौस्तुभधर 3. 194. 15; 6. 62. 22.
